# Hud

> The Hotline framework's modder API.

```csharp
public static class Hud
```

Namespace `Hotline.Api`

The Hotline framework’s modder API. Reference Hotline.Api.dll OR drop this single file into your mod. Register a panel and you instantly get a ready-made, toggleable, draggable in-game window inside the one unified Hotline overlay - no custom hotkey, no custom uGUI, no per-mod debug window. One master key opens the overlay; every mod’s controls live there as buttons. Optionally bind a central hotkey to an action and Hotline owns the polling and conflict detection for you.

Every call is a zero-overhead no-op when Hotline is not installed and lights up automatically when it is, so you can ship this unconditionally with no hard dependency.

```csharp
using Hotline.Api;
Hud.RegisterPanel("MyMod", "My Mod")
   .Text(() => "queue = " + _queue.Count)
   .Action("Reload", Reload)
   .Toggle("Verbose", () => _verbose, v => _verbose = v)
   .Hotkey("Reload", HotlineKey.F8, Reload);   // optional central hotkey
```

Tip: a class named `HotlineProbe` with a static `Register()` is auto-discovered and called on bind (see `AutoRegister`), so your mod’s Core does not have to wire anything.

All calls MUST be made from the Unity main thread.

## Properties

[Section titled “Properties”](#properties)

### Available

[Section titled “Available”](#available)

```csharp
public static bool Available { get; }
```

True only when the Hotline host is installed AND bound. You rarely need this - the API is a safe no-op when absent.

## Methods

[Section titled “Methods”](#methods)

### RegisterPanel

[Section titled “RegisterPanel”](#registerpanel)

```csharp
public static Panel RegisterPanel(string id, string title = null)
```

Declare a panel: a named, toggleable, movable window in the Hotline overlay that groups everything this mod exposes (text readouts, action buttons, toggles, a log channel). Returns a fluent builder. Load-order-proof; a no-op (the builder still works) if Hotline is absent.

### RegisterAction

[Section titled “RegisterAction”](#registeraction)

```csharp
public static void RegisterAction(string panelId, string label, Action run)
```

A clickable button in a mod’s panel - the in-game replacement for a debug hotkey action. Runs on the main thread when clicked. Load-order-proof.

### RegisterToggle

[Section titled “RegisterToggle”](#registertoggle)

```csharp
public static void RegisterToggle(
    string panelId,
    string label,
    Func<bool> get,
    Action<bool> set)
```

An on/off control in a mod’s panel - the in-game replacement for a toggle hotkey. `get` reports the current state, `set` applies it; both run on the main thread. Load-order-proof.

### RegisterSlider

[Section titled “RegisterSlider”](#registerslider)

```csharp
public static void RegisterSlider(
    string panelId,
    string label,
    double min,
    double max,
    Func<double> get,
    Action<double> set,
    double step = 0d,
    string unit = null)
```

A draggable value in a mod’s panel - the in-game replacement for typing a number into a console to find it. `get` reports the current value, `set` applies it; both run on the main thread. The host clamps to \[`min`, `max`] and snaps to `step` (0 = continuous), so a setter never sees a value outside its range. Load-order-proof; a no-op on an older Hotline host that predates slider support.

### RegisterText

[Section titled “RegisterText”](#registertext)

```csharp
public static void RegisterText(string panelId, Func<string> provider)
```

A free-text, multi-line readout in a mod’s panel. Polled by the host on the main thread. Load-order-proof.

### RegisterImage

[Section titled “RegisterImage”](#registerimage)

```csharp
public static void RegisterImage(string panelId, Func<int[]> provider)
```

An image in a mod’s panel (e.g. a QR code). The provider returns `{ width, height, argb0, argb1, ... }` - ARGB32 pixels, row-major top-down - or null/empty for “nothing to show”. Polled by the host on the main thread and drawn Point-filtered. Kept as a raw int\[] so this shim needs no Unity reference. Load-order-proof; a no-op on an older Hotline host that predates image support.

### BindPanelLog

[Section titled “BindPanelLog”](#bindpanellog)

```csharp
public static void BindPanelLog(string panelId)
```

Mark that a panel should display its own log channel (the lines you send via `Log` / `Write` with the same id). Load-order-proof.

### Log

[Section titled “Log”](#log)

```csharp
public static void Log(
    string channel,
    string message,
    LogLevel level = LogLevel.Info)
```

Send a log line to a channel (use your mod/panel id as the channel). It appears in that mod’s panel log AND in Hotline’s combined timeline. Load-order-proof; a no-op if Hotline is absent.

### RegisterHotkey

[Section titled “RegisterHotkey”](#registerhotkey)

```csharp
public static void RegisterHotkey(
    string ownerId,
    string label,
    HotlineKey key,
    Action run)
```

Bind a central hotkey to an action. Hotline owns the key polling and conflict detection, so every mod’s hotkeys live in one place. Pass `None` to skip the key and only label the action. The same action typically also appears as a panel button. Load-order-proof.

### ShowOverlay

[Section titled “ShowOverlay”](#showoverlay)

```csharp
public static void ShowOverlay(bool show)
```

Added in `1.3.0`

Raise or dismiss the whole overlay from code - the same thing the master key does. Lets a mod offer a console command for its HUD instead of relying on a keypress, which nothing can automate or verify. No-op when Hotline is absent or has not bound yet (this one is NOT queued: showing an overlay minutes later, once the host finally turns up, would be a surprise rather than a favour).

### ShowPanel

[Section titled “ShowPanel”](#showpanel)

```csharp
public static void ShowPanel(string panelId, bool show)
```

Added in `1.3.0`

Show or hide one panel by id. Showing it raises the overlay too, so a single call is enough to put a mod’s panel in front of the player. No-op when Hotline is absent.

### IsPanelVisible

[Section titled “IsPanelVisible”](#ispanelvisible)

```csharp
public static bool IsPanelVisible(string panelId)
```

Added in `1.3.0`

Whether a panel is on screen right now (false when Hotline is absent, or the overlay is down).

### AutoRegister

[Section titled “AutoRegister”](#autoregister)

```csharp
public static void AutoRegister()
```

Discover a convention type named `HotlineProbe` with a static `Register()` in THIS mod’s own assembly and invoke it once - so a mod never has to wire a Register() call into its Core. Drive it from a `[ModuleInitializer]` in your probe file. No-op + load-order-proof.

# Panel

> Fluent builder for a mod's Hotline panel (returned by `RegisterPanel`).

```csharp
public sealed class Panel
```

Namespace `Hotline.Api`

Fluent builder for a mod’s Hotline panel (returned by `RegisterPanel`). Everything is a safe no-op when the Hotline host is absent.

## Properties

[Section titled “Properties”](#properties)

```csharp
public string Id { get; }
```

The panel id (also the default log channel).

## Methods


A free-text, multi-line readout in this panel.

### Image

An image in this panel (e.g. a QR code). Provider returns { width, height, argb… } or null.

### Action


A clickable button (replaces a debug hotkey action).

An on/off control (replaces a debug toggle hotkey).

A draggable value (replaces typing a number into a console to find it).

# Hotline changelog

> Every released version of Hotline and what changed in it.

All notable changes to Hotline are documented here. This project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).

## \[1.3.1] - 2026-08-04

[Section titled “\[1.3.1\] - 2026-08-04”](#131---2026-08-04)

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed)

* `hotline` shows up in the game’s command list, so a console autocomplete or a terminal can offer it and complete it. It was answered by a patch and registered nowhere, which made it invisible to every tool that lists commands. Nothing about running it changes.

## \[1.3.0] - 2026-08-04

[Section titled “\[1.3.0\] - 2026-08-04”](#130---2026-08-04)

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added)

* A mod can show and hide the overlay from code, without the player pressing the key.

## \[1.2.1] - 2026-08-04

[Section titled “\[1.2.1\] - 2026-08-04”](#121---2026-08-04)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed)

* The overlay no longer takes the game down when a mod’s panel shows an image. Opening it with Snitch installed crashed straight to desktop, because the way the image was drawn does not exist in this build of the game.
* A panel that fails to draw is skipped instead of killing the whole overlay, and it says so once in the log rather than sixty times a second.

## \[1.2.0] - 2026-07-31

[Section titled “\[1.2.0\] - 2026-07-31”](#120---2026-07-31)

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-1)

* Panels can now hold a **slider** (`Panel.Slider`, `Hud.RegisterSlider`) - a value you drag rather than a number you type. The host clamps it to the declared range and snaps it to the step before your setter runs, so a setter never sees a value it did not declare as legal, whichever control wrote it.
* `hotline slider <sliderId> [value]` reads or writes the same value from the console. A slider is a mouse control and a mouse control cannot be driven by a test harness, so anything reachable only by dragging reaches testers unverified.

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-1)

* Dragging a slider continues while the cursor is off the track, which is how every slider anywhere behaves.

### Notes

[Section titled “Notes”](#notes)

* Additive and backward-compatible: older mods are unaffected, and a mod that registers a slider is a no-op on an older Hotline.
* Control ids are slugified from the label and punctuation is dropped, so two labels that differ only in punctuation collide and the second replaces the first. Give each control distinct words.

## \[1.1.0] - 2026-07-08

[Section titled “\[1.1.0\] - 2026-07-08”](#110---2026-07-08)

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-2)

* Panels can now show an **image** (`Panel.Image`) alongside their text, actions and toggles - a mod supplies raw pixels and the overlay draws them crisply. Additive and backward-compatible: older mods are unaffected, and a mod that uses it is a no-op on an older Hotline. First user: Snitch’s in-game connect-a-phone QR.

## \[1.0.0] - 2026-06-26

[Section titled “\[1.0.0\] - 2026-06-26”](#100---2026-06-26)

Initial release.

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-3)

* One in-game overlay for every mod’s HUD, opened by a single master key (default F6). Each registering mod gets its own toggleable, movable, resizable window.
* Modder API (`Hotline.Api`) - a zero-overhead no-op when Hotline is absent: register a panel with text readouts, action buttons, on/off toggles, a log channel and an optional central hotkey.
* Auto-interception of other mods’ function keys (F1-F12): each polled key is attributed to its mod and surfaced as a clickable button in that mod’s panel.
* Optional full takeover (`SuppressRawFunctionKeys`, default off): a physical function-key press opens the overlay on the owning mod’s panel instead of reaching the mod, so two mods can no longer collide on a key.
* IMGUI windowing with polled input (the path that works for in-game mouse interaction on this IL2CPP build); draggable, resizable, scrollable windows with persisted layouts, near-zero cost while hidden.
* `hotline ...` console: control the overlay, panels, the master key, the central hotkey table and the takeover behaviour from the in-game console.
* A combined log timeline across all mods that report to Hotline.

# Console commands

> Look up every hotline console command with its arguments and effect.

Look up a `hotline` command here. Open the in-game console and type it.

## Overlay

[Section titled “Overlay”](#overlay)

| Command                    | What it does                                                         |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `hotline hud [on\|off]`    | Show or hide the overlay. The master key (default F6) does the same. |
| `hotline hud move <x> <y>` | Move the overlay.                                                    |
| `hotline hud font <n>`     | Set the text size.                                                   |
| `hotline hud reset`        | Reset the overlay.                                                   |

## Panels

[Section titled “Panels”](#panels)

| Command                                                           | What it does                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `hotline panels`                                                  | List every registered panel.                                                                                                                                          |
| `hotline panel <id> [on\|off\|move <x> <y>\|size <w> <h>\|reset]` | Control one panel window. Built-in ids: `overview`, `timeline`.                                                                                                       |
| `hotline act <actionId>`                                          | Run a panel action button.                                                                                                                                            |
| `hotline toggle <toggleId> [on\|off]`                             | Flip a panel toggle.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `hotline slider <sliderId> [value]`                               | Write a panel slider. Omit the value to read it with its range and step. The host clamps and snaps it like a drag. See [Add a slider](/mods/hotline/guides/sliders/). |
| `hotline log [<channel>\|all] [n]`                                | Read the logs.                                                                                                                                                        |

## Hotkeys

[Section titled “Hotkeys”](#hotkeys)

| Command                                | What it does                                                                              |
| -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `hotline keys`                         | List the centrally bound hotkeys.                                                         |
| `hotline intercept [on\|off\|status]`  | Turn interception of other mods’ function keys on or off. `status` lists the caught keys. |
| `hotline intercept suppress [on\|off]` | Full takeover: the raw key opens the overlay instead of reaching the mod.                 |
| `hotline key master <KeyCode>`         | Change the master overlay key, for example `hotline key master F4`.                       |
| `hotline key press <KeyCode> [mod]`    | Send a synthetic press of a caught key to one mod, or to all mods that poll it.           |

# How hotkey interception works

> Look up how Hotline catches other mods' function keys and turns them into panel buttons.

Hotline catches mods that poll a raw function key (F1-F12) and adds a button for each key to that mod’s panel. You trigger any mod’s hotkey from one place, and two mods no longer fight over a key. The mod does not need to use the [Hotline API](/mods/hotline/guides/modder-api/).

## How it works

[Section titled “How it works”](#how-it-works)

1. Hotline wraps the per-frame methods of every other mod (`OnUpdate` and others) to know which mod is running.
2. A Harmony hook on `UnityEngine.Input.GetKeyDown` assigns each polled function key to that mod.
3. Hotline adds a “Press Fx” button to the mod’s panel.

The hook applies to mod code only. The game’s own input is not touched.

## Press a caught key

[Section titled “Press a caught key”](#press-a-caught-key)

Click the “Press Fx” button, or run `hotline key press Fx <mod>`. Hotline sends a one-frame synthetic press that only the owning mod sees. Input is read on the client, so multiplayer is not affected.

## Full takeover

[Section titled “Full takeover”](#full-takeover)

By default the raw key keeps working. Set **`SuppressRawFunctionKeys`** to `true`, or run `hotline intercept suppress on`, for full takeover. A physical function-key press then no longer reaches the mod. It opens the overlay on that mod’s panel, where each key is a button.

## Master key

[Section titled “Master key”](#master-key)

The overlay key (default **F6**) belongs to Hotline and is never caught. If a mod also uses F6, it still gets a button. Pressing F6 opens the overlay on that mod’s panel, and the mod’s raw F6 is blocked so it cannot fire twice.

## One window per mod

[Section titled “One window per mod”](#one-window-per-mod)

A registered panel, forwarded data (for example from Snitch) and caught hotkeys land in one panel when they share the mod’s name.

## Limits

[Section titled “Limits”](#limits)

* Hotline catches only mods that use the legacy `UnityEngine.Input`. Mods on the new Input System are not caught and are not affected.
* The vanilla game binds no function keys, so it is never touched.

# Install Hotline

> Install the Hotline overlay and open it with the F6 key.

Install Hotline and open the overlay with F6.

**You need:** the IL2CPP build of Schedule I and MelonLoader 0.7.3. See [Install](/install/) for MelonLoader. Hotline does not use S1API.

## Steps

[Section titled “Steps”](#steps)

1. With a Thunderstore mod manager (r2modman or Gale), install **Hotline**. MelonLoader comes as a dependency.
2. Without a manager, put `Hotline.dll` in your Schedule I `Mods/` folder.
3. Start the game.

## Check it works

[Section titled “Check it works”](#check-it-works)

Press **F6**. The overlay opens.

![The Hotline overlay with one button per mod panel: My Mod, Yoink (Winch), Snitch (Profiler), Sideload and Timeline (logs)](/img/guides/hotline/overlay.webp)

## Settings

[Section titled “Settings”](#settings)

Settings are in `UserData/MelonPreferences.cfg` under `Hotline_01_Main`.

| Setting                                    | Default | What it does                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Enabled`                                  | `true`  | Master on/off.                                                                              |
| `MasterHotkey`                             | `F6`    | Key that opens and closes the overlay. Any `UnityEngine.KeyCode` name. Hotline reserves it. |
| `InterceptFunctionKeys`                    | `true`  | Detect other mods’ F1-F12 keys and add each as a button in that mod’s panel.                |
| `SuppressRawFunctionKeys`                  | `false` | Full takeover: a physical function key opens the overlay instead of reaching the mod.       |
| `HudFontSize`                              | `12`    | Overlay text size in px.                                                                    |
| `ShowHud`, `HudX`, `HudY`, `WindowLayouts` | managed | Visibility, position and saved window layouts. Hotline writes them.                         |

## Next

[Section titled “Next”](#next)

* [Console commands](/mods/hotline/guides/console-commands/)
* [Add a panel](/mods/hotline/guides/modder-api/)

# Add a panel

> Give your mod a panel in the Hotline overlay with text, buttons, toggles and sliders.

Give your mod its own panel in the Hotline overlay. Players open the overlay with F6 and see your panel as a window. You write no `OnGUI` and no uGUI.

**You need:** Hotline in your test game and a MelonLoader mod project. Players do not need Hotline: every call is a no-op without it.

## Steps

[Section titled “Steps”](#steps)

1. Copy `Hotline.cs` from [ScheduleOne-HotlineExample](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-HotlineExample) into your project. It compiles into your DLL. You can reference `Hotline.Api.dll` instead.

2. Register a panel. Use your mod name as the panel id.

   ```csharp
   using Hotline.Api;   // Hud, Panel, HotlineKey, LogLevel


   Hud.RegisterPanel("MyMod", "My Mod")
      .Text(() => "queue = " + _queue.Count)
      .Action("Reload", Reload)
      .Toggle("Verbose", () => _verbose, v => _verbose = v)
      .Slider("batch size", 1, 64, () => _batch, v => _batch = (int)v, 1)
      .Hotkey("Reload", HotlineKey.F8, Reload)
      .Log();
   ```

3. Optional: put the registration in a static class named `HotlineProbe` with a static `Register()` method. Hotline finds and calls it, so you wire nothing into `OnInitializeMelon`.

## Check it works

[Section titled “Check it works”](#check-it-works)

1. Start the game and press F6. The overlay opens.
2. Open your panel from the Overview window, or run `hotline panel MyMod on`.
3. Run `hotline panels`. `MyMod` is in the list.

![The My Mod panel next to the Hotline overlay, with the queue readout, the Reload button, the Verbose toggle and the batch size slider](/img/guides/hotline/mymod-panel.webp)

## Builder methods

[Section titled “Builder methods”](#builder-methods)

| Method                                                                                                                     | Result                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.Text(Func<string>)`                                                                                                      | Multi-line readout, polled a few times a second.                                                                                   |
| `.Image(Func<int[]>)`                                                                                                      | Raw ARGB pixels, for example a QR code. Use `{ width, height, argb0, argb1, ... }`. Return null or an empty array to show nothing. |
| `.Action(string label, Action run)`                                                                                        | Button. Runs on the main thread.                                                                                                   |
| `.Toggle(string label, Func<bool> get, Action<bool> set)`                                                                  | On/off control.                                                                                                                    |
| `.Slider(string label, double min, double max, Func<double> get, Action<double> set, double step = 0, string unit = null)` | Draggable value. See [Add a slider](/mods/hotline/guides/sliders/).                                                                |
| `.Hotkey(string label, HotlineKey key, Action run)`                                                                        | Central hotkey. Hotline polls it and flags conflicts. `HotlineKey.None` skips the key.                                             |
| `.Log()`                                                                                                                   | Show the panel’s log channel. Write with `.Write("...")` or `Hud.Log("MyMod", "...")`.                                             |

Static calls exist too: `Hud.RegisterPanel`, `RegisterAction`, `RegisterToggle`, `RegisterSlider`, `RegisterText`, `RegisterImage`, `RegisterHotkey`, `Log`.

## Rules

[Section titled “Rules”](#rules)

* Call the API from the Unity main thread. Hotline runs your delegates on the main thread, so they may use game objects.
* Registrations made before Hotline loads are queued. Load order does not matter.
* Your mod may poll a raw `Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.Fx)`. Hotline then adds a button for it to the panel with the same id as your mod name. See [How hotkey interception works](/mods/hotline/guides/how-it-works/).

## Next

[Section titled “Next”](#next)

* [Add a slider](/mods/hotline/guides/sliders/)
* [Console commands](/mods/hotline/guides/console-commands/)
* [API reference](/mods/hotline/api/)

# Add a slider

> Tune a value by dragging it in your Hotline panel or by typing it in the console.

Add a slider to your Hotline panel. You drag it in the overlay or write it with `hotline slider`.

This page uses the **Hotline** API (`Hotline.Api`). For the Snitch API, see the [Snitch slider guide](/mods/snitch/guides/sliders/).

**You need:** a Hotline panel. See [Add a panel](/mods/hotline/guides/modder-api/).

## Steps

[Section titled “Steps”](#steps)

1. Call `.Slider` on your panel.

   ```csharp
   using Hotline.Api;


   Hud.RegisterPanel("Yoink", "Yoink (Winch)")
      .Slider("size", 0.2, 2.0, () => WinchItem.HeldScale, v => WinchItem.HeldScale = (float)v, 0.05, "x")
      .Slider("pull force", 0, 60000, () => Preferences.PullNewtons, v => Preferences.PullNewtons = (float)v, 500, "N");
   ```

2. Pick a range wider than the values you expect. The ends are hard limits.

3. Give every slider in the panel a label that differs in its words. See “Label collisions” below.

The signature:

```csharp
Panel Slider(string label, double min, double max, Func<double> get, Action<double> set,
             double step = 0d, string unit = null)
```

| Parameter     | Meaning                                                               |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`       | Text next to the value. It also makes the slider id.                  |
| `min` / `max` | Ends of the track. `max` must be greater than `min`.                  |
| `get`         | Reads the current value on the main thread while the panel draws.     |
| `set`         | Applies a new value on the main thread.                               |
| `step`        | Snap increment. `0` means continuous.                                 |
| `unit`        | Short suffix after the number, for example `m`, `N`, `deg`. Optional. |

The static form is `Hud.RegisterSlider(panelId, label, min, max, get, set, step, unit)`.

Hotline clamps the value to `[min, max]` and snaps it to `step` before it calls `set`. Your setter needs no range check.

## Check it works

[Section titled “Check it works”](#check-it-works)

1. Press F6 and open the panel. The slider shows its label, live value and a filled track.
2. Drag the knob. It follows the cursor until you release the button.
3. Run `hotline slider Yoink:size`. It prints the value, range and step.
4. Run `hotline slider Yoink:size 0.85`. The value is clamped and snapped like a drag.

![The Yoink (Winch) panel with the size slider at 1.00 x and the pull force slider at 20000 N](/img/guides/hotline/yoink-sliders.webp)

## Label collisions

[Section titled “Label collisions”](#label-collisions)

A slider id is `<panelId>:<slug of the label>`. The slug keeps letters and digits, lowercases them and turns every other run of characters into one hyphen.

| Label                         | Id in panel `Yoink`    |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| `size`                        | `Yoink:size`           |
| `pull force`                  | `Yoink:pull-force`     |
| `size -0.05` and `size +0.05` | both `Yoink:size-0-05` |

Two labels with the same id replace each other. No warning or log line appears, and the first control disappears. Use `size down` and `size up`, not `size -0.05` and `size +0.05`.

## Rules

[Section titled “Rules”](#rules)

* Register from the Unity main thread.
* A call is dropped silently if `max` is not greater than `min`, or if `get` or `set` is null.
* Registering the same id again replaces the slider. Running your registration twice is safe.
* On a Hotline without sliders, the call is a no-op.

## Next

[Section titled “Next”](#next)

* [Console commands](/mods/hotline/guides/console-commands/)
* [API reference](/mods/hotline/api/)

# HotlineExample

> Modder example for Hotline - register a panel in the unified overlay (no-op when Hotline is absent).

|          |                                                                                                  |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Version  | No release yet, documented from `main`                                                           |
| Download | [GitHub](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-HotlineExample)                            |
| Help     | [Discord](https://mods.doodesch.de) · [Report a bug](https://support.doodesch.de/hotlineexample) |

A minimal example mod showing how to give your Schedule I mod a panel in the [Hotline](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Hotline) overlay - a text readout, an action button, a toggle, an optional central hotkey and a log - with a single fluent call. Every call is a zero-overhead no-op when Hotline is not installed, so there is no hard dependency.

## What’s here

[Section titled “What’s here”](#whats-here)

* `Hotline.Api/` - the modder shim. Reference `Hotline.Api.dll`, OR (recommended) drop the single `Hotline.cs` into your mod and compile it in - no extra DLL to ship.
* `HotlineExample/` - the example mod (`Core.cs`): registers a panel and demonstrates the full surface.

## The 10-second version

[Section titled “The 10-second version”](#the-10-second-version)

```csharp
using Hotline.Api;


Hud.RegisterPanel("MyMod", "My Mod")
   .Text(() => "queue = " + _queue.Count)                // a free, multi-line readout
   .Action("Reload", Reload)                             // a button (replaces a debug hotkey)
   .Toggle("Verbose", () => _verbose, v => _verbose = v) // an on/off control
   .Hotkey("Reload", HotlineKey.F8, Reload)              // an optional central hotkey
   .Log();                                               // a log channel
```

That is it - no `OnGUI`, no uGUI, no per-mod hotkey. Hotline draws the window; the player presses its master key (F6) to open the overlay and your panel is there alongside every other mod’s. See `HotlineExample/Core.cs` for the working version, and the [Hotline wiki](https://docs.doodesch.de/mods/hotline/) for the full API.

## Integration

[Section titled “Integration”](#integration)

* **Copy-in source (recommended):** drop `Hotline.Api/Hotline.cs` into your mod project and compile it in. Nothing extra to ship; it binds to the running Hotline host by reflection and is a no-op when Hotline is absent.
* **Reference the DLL:** reference `Hotline.Api.dll`.

Either way it works regardless of load order (registrations queue until the host is up) and adds no hard dependency. If your mod already polls a raw function key, Hotline also auto-detects it and adds it as a button to your panel - but registering a panel like this is the clean way.

# Inkorporated

> Custom tattoo framework for Schedule I - mods add tattoos to the in-game tattoo shop via drop-in packs or a public API.

|                |                                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Latest release | `1.1.4`                                                                                                                                             |
| Download       | [GitHub](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Inkorporated) · [Thunderstore](https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/p/DooDesch/Inkorporated/) |
| Requires       | MelonLoader 0.7.3, S1API Forked 3.2.1                                                                                                               |
| Start here     | [Make a tattoo pack](/mods/inkorporated/guides/getting-started/)                                                                                    |
| API            | [Reference](/mods/inkorporated/api/)                                                                                                                |
| Help           | [Discord](https://mods.doodesch.de) · [Report a bug](https://support.doodesch.de/inkorporated)                                                      |

> The tattoo framework for Schedule I. Inkorporated lets mods add their own PNG tattoos to the in-game tattoo shop - drop a pack folder, or register via the API - and the game treats them exactly like vanilla tattoos: they render on the avatar, persist in saves and sync in co-op. Built on [S1API](https://github.com/ifBars/S1API).

Inkorporated is primarily a **library / dependency**. On its own it adds no tattoos - it’s the thing tattoo packs depend on. Install it alongside a tattoo pack (or flip on the bundled example pack) and the new tattoos show up in the tattoo shop under their placement category (Chest, Left/Right Arm, Face).

## Documentation & example

[Section titled “Documentation & example”](#documentation--example)

tattoos: pack format, the API, authoring + UV alignment, multiplayer/NPCs, troubleshooting.

* 🧩 **[Example repo](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-InkorporatedExample)** - a working, copy-me template showing **both** routes side by side: a no-code content pack and a code mod using the API.

## Features

[Section titled “Features”](#features)

* **Real tattoos, not decals.** Each custom tattoo is registered as an avatar object in the game’s own avatar object library, so it renders, **saves**, and **syncs in multiplayer** just like a built-in tattoo (any client with the same mod + pack sees it; others simply don’t render it - no crash).
* **Two ways to ship tattoos** - a drop-in **pack folder** (PNGs + a tiny `manifest.json`, no code), or a C# **API** for code mods that build textures at runtime.
* **All placements:** chest, left arm, right arm and face.
* **No asset bundles, no engine patching.** Custom textures are loaded from PNG at runtime and wrapped into clones of built-in tattoos - nothing to cook in Unity.
* **Bundled example pack** (off by default) gives players a few ready-made tattoos and authors a working template to copy.

Requirements

| Component   | Version / Source                                                                             |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Schedule I  | IL2CPP, `0.4.7f12` or later                                                                  |
| MelonLoader | `0.7.3+`                                                                                     |
| S1API       | [ifBars/S1API\_Forked](https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/p/ifBars/S1API_Forked/) `3.2.1+` |

Installation

### Recommended: a Thunderstore mod manager

[Section titled “Recommended: a Thunderstore mod manager”](#recommended-a-thunderstore-mod-manager)

Install with r2modman / Gale from the Schedule I community; the dependencies (MelonLoader, S1API) are pulled in automatically. Then install any tattoo pack that lists Inkorporated as a dependency.

### Manual

[Section titled “Manual”](#manual)

1. Install **MelonLoader 0.7.3** for Schedule I.
2. Install **S1API** (its DLLs go in `Mods/` and `Plugins/` per its own instructions).
3. Drop **`Inkorporated.dll`** into your Schedule I `Mods/` folder.
4. Add tattoo packs (see below), or enable the bundled example pack (see Configuration).

## For players: using tattoo packs

[Section titled “For players: using tattoo packs”](#for-players-using-tattoo-packs)

A tattoo pack is just a folder under:

```plaintext
<Schedule I>/UserData/Inkorporated/Packs/<PackName>/
```

containing a `manifest.json` and the PNGs it lists. Mod managers that target this path install packs for you. To see the format, turn on the bundled example pack (Configuration below) and look in `UserData/Inkorporated/Packs/Examples`. Custom tattoos then appear in the tattoo shop, free by default.

## For pack authors: the pack format

[Section titled “For pack authors: the pack format”](#for-pack-authors-the-pack-format)

Create `UserData/Inkorporated/Packs/<YourPack>/manifest.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "My Pack",
  "author": "you",
  "tattoos": [
    { "id": "skull", "name": "Skull", "placement": "chest", "file": "skull.png" },
    { "id": "tear",  "name": "Teardrop", "placement": "face", "file": "tear.png", "price": 250 }
  ]
}
```

* **`placement`**: one of `chest` | `leftarm` | `rightarm` | `face`.
* **`price`**: optional; omit or `0` for “Free”.
* **`file`**: PNG filename relative to the pack folder (defaults to `<id>.png` if omitted).
* **`id`**: unique within your pack.

### Authoring the PNGs (important)

[Section titled “Authoring the PNGs (important)”](#authoring-the-pngs-important)

A tattoo is a **full UV-space skin texture**, not a sticker placed in a box. The body shares one UV unwrap (torso + both arms + legs), the face has its own. Your design’s **opaque pixels must sit at the UV coordinates of the body part you want** - everything else transparent. Get this wrong and the ink lands on the wrong limb.

* Recommended canvas: **2048x2048** for body/arms, **512x512** for face (matches the built-ins). Size only affects sharpness, not placement; there is **no size cap** - you can paint a whole arm sleeve or a full back piece by covering that region’s UV.
* Use the built-in tattoos as alignment references. A DEBUG build of Inkorporated exports every built-in tattoo texture to `UserData/Inkorporated/Templates/` - paint over those to line your art up.

## For mod developers: the API

[Section titled “For mod developers: the API”](#for-mod-developers-the-api)

Reference `Inkorporated.dll` and register early (e.g. in your `OnInitializeMelon`), **before** the tattoo shop UI is built. Tattoos registered later appear the next time that UI is rebuilt.

```csharp
using Inkorporated;                 // API
using Inkorporated.Model;           // TattooPlacement


// From an already-loaded texture:
API.RegisterTattoo("skull", "Skull", TattooPlacement.Chest, myTexture2D, price: 0f, source: "MyMod");


// From a PNG on disk (loaded lazily when first needed):
API.RegisterTattooFromFile("tear", "Teardrop", TattooPlacement.Face, pngPath, source: "MyMod");


// From a PNG embedded in your own DLL (no loading boilerplate - caller assembly is auto-detected):
API.RegisterTattooFromResource("rose", "Rose", TattooPlacement.LeftArm, "MyMod.Assets.rose.png", source: "MyMod");
```

`TattooPlacement` = `Chest | LeftArm | RightArm | Face`. `source` namespaces your ids (used for de-duplication and the registered avatar object id). On Thunderstore, list `DooDesch-Inkorporated` as a dependency.

## Configuration

[Section titled “Configuration”](#configuration)

Settings live in `UserData/MelonPreferences.cfg` under `Inkorporated_01_Main`.

| Setting           | Default | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `LoadExamplePack` | `false` | When on, drops the bundled example pack into `UserData/Inkorporated/Packs/Examples` on startup (if not already there) - a few ready-made tattoos plus a folder/manifest template to copy. Requires a game restart. Never overwrites an existing Examples folder. |

## How it works

[Section titled “How it works”](#how-it-works)

For each custom tattoo, Inkorporated loads the PNG into a `Texture2D`, clones a built-in tattoo of the matching placement with the texture swapped in, and enters the clone in the game’s `AvatarObjectLibrary` under its own id. All tattoos register on the first scene load, before any saved appearance is applied. The shop buttons are added by cloning an existing option in the tattoo-shop UI. From there the game’s own avatar pipeline loads, renders, saves and networks the tattoo like any vanilla one - which is why no asset bundles or render hooks are needed.

Compatibility

* IL2CPP build only (current Steam public branch).
* **Multiplayer:** custom tattoos are transmitted as their avatar object id. Every player needs Inkorporated **and the same pack** for them to render on each other; players without it simply don’t show that tattoo (no desync, no crash).

Credits

* **DooDesch** - mod author.
* **[ifBars/S1API](https://github.com/ifBars/S1API)** - the modding API this is built on (texture loading helpers).

# Inkorporated API

> Look up every public type and member of Inkorporated 1.1.4.

## Use this API

[Section titled “Use this API”](#use-this-api)

Reference `Inkorporated.dll` from your Mods folder:

```xml
<Reference Include="Inkorporated">
  <HintPath>$(ModsDirectory)\Inkorporated.dll</HintPath>
  <Private>false</Private>
</Reference>
```

Mark it optional, so your mod still loads without it:

```csharp
[assembly: MelonOptionalDependencies("Inkorporated")]
```

Without Inkorporated its types are missing too. Call it only after you know it loaded.

First steps: [Make a tattoo pack](/mods/inkorporated/guides/getting-started/).

Example project: [ScheduleOne-InkorporatedExample](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-InkorporatedExample).

Source: [`API.cs`](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Inkorporated/blob/v1.1.4/API.cs) at `v1.1.4`.

# API

> Public, stable entry point for other mods that want to add custom tattoos to the in-game tattoo shop.

```csharp
public static class API
```

Namespace `Inkorporated`

Public, stable entry point for other mods that want to add custom tattoos to the in-game tattoo shop. Register early (e.g. in your mod’s OnInitializeMelon). Tattoos registered after the tattoo-shop UI has already been built will appear the next time that UI is rebuilt.

## Methods

[Section titled “Methods”](#methods)

### RegisterTattoo

[Section titled “RegisterTattoo”](#registertattoo)

```csharp
public static bool RegisterTattoo(
    string id,
    string displayName,
    TattooPlacement placement,
    Texture2D texture,
    float price = 0f,
    string source = "API")
```

Register a tattoo from an already-loaded texture.

| Parameter     |                                                                                         |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`          | Unique id within your `source`.                                                         |
| `displayName` | Name shown on the shop button.                                                          |
| `placement`   | Body region the tattoo applies to.                                                      |
| `texture`     | The tattoo texture (must match the game’s body/face UV layout).                         |
| `price`       | Shop price; 0 shows “Free”.                                                             |
| `source`      | A stable namespace for your mod (defaults to “API”); used for de-duplication and paths. |

**Returns** True if added; false if it duplicated an existing (source, id).

### RegisterTattooFromFile

[Section titled “RegisterTattooFromFile”](#registertattoofromfile)

```csharp
public static bool RegisterTattooFromFile(
    string id,
    string displayName,
    TattooPlacement placement,
    string pngPath,
    float price = 0f,
    string source = "API")
```

Register a tattoo from a PNG file on disk (loaded lazily when first needed).

### RegisterTattooFromResource(string, string, TattooPlacement, string, float, string)

[Section titled “RegisterTattooFromResource(string, string, TattooPlacement, string, float, string)”](#registertattoofromresourcestring-string-tattooplacement-string-float-string)

```csharp
public static bool RegisterTattooFromResource(
    string id,
    string displayName,
    TattooPlacement placement,
    string resourceName,
    float price = 0f,
    string source = "API")
```

Added in `1.1.0`

Register a tattoo from a PNG embedded in YOUR mod’s DLL (the calling assembly), so you don’t have to write the resource-loading boilerplate. `resourceName` is the embedded resource name (e.g. “MyMod.Assets.skull.png”); a trailing-suffix match is accepted, so “skull.png” works too. Loaded lazily when first needed.

### RegisterTattooFromResource(string, string, TattooPlacement, Assembly, string, float, string)

[Section titled “RegisterTattooFromResource(string, string, TattooPlacement, Assembly, string, float, string)”](#registertattoofromresourcestring-string-tattooplacement-assembly-string-float-string)

```csharp
public static bool RegisterTattooFromResource(
    string id,
    string displayName,
    TattooPlacement placement,
    System.Reflection.Assembly assembly,
    string resourceName,
    float price = 0f,
    string source = "API")
```

Added in `1.1.0`

Register a tattoo from a PNG embedded in the given `assembly` (use this overload if the PNG lives in a different assembly than the caller). Loaded lazily when first needed.

> What Inkorporated added to and removed from its public API in each release.

A member listed under a version is callable from that version on. Check “Removed” and “Signature changed” before you raise the version you require: a mod built against the old signature breaks on the new one.

* `API.RegisterTattooFromResource(string, string, TattooPlacement, string, float, string)`

## 1.0.0

First release covered here. 3 public types and members.

# Inkorporated changelog

> Every released version of Inkorporated and what changed in it.

All notable changes to Inkorporated are documented here. This project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).

## \[1.1.4] - 2026-10-15

[Section titled “\[1.1.4\] - 2026-10-15”](#114---2026-10-15)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed)

* Custom tattoos show in the tattoo shop and on your character again, also after loading a save. Schedule I 0.4.7 had stopped drawing them.

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed)

* Runs on Schedule I 0.4.7f12.
* Needs S1API 3.2.1, up from 3.1.1. Update it along with the mod.

### For mod authors

[Section titled “For mod authors”](#for-mod-authors)

* Packs and `API.RegisterTattoo` calls work unchanged. Tattoo ids keep their `Avatar/Layers/Tattoos/custom/...` path.

## \[1.1.3] - 2026-08-01

[Section titled “\[1.1.3\] - 2026-08-01”](#113---2026-08-01)

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-1)

* Runs on Schedule I 0.4.6f11.
* Needs S1API 3.1.1, up from 3.0.5. Update it along with the mod.

## \[1.1.2] - 2026-07-23

[Section titled “\[1.1.2\] - 2026-07-23”](#112---2026-07-23)

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-2)

* The shipped READMEs now link the per-product support page ([support.doodesch.de/inkorporated](https://support.doodesch.de/inkorporated)). No gameplay changes.

## \[1.1.1] - 2026-07-23

[Section titled “\[1.1.1\] - 2026-07-23”](#111---2026-07-23)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-1)

* Custom tattoo prices in the shop now read “$250” like the built-in ones, instead of a bare “250” - the rows use the game’s own money formatting again.

## \[1.1.0] - 2026-06-21

[Section titled “\[1.1.0\] - 2026-06-21”](#110---2026-06-21)

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added)

* `Inkorporated.API.RegisterTattooFromResource(...)` - register a tattoo from a PNG embedded in your mod’s DLL with one call (the calling assembly is detected automatically; a trailing-suffix resource-name match is accepted), so code mods no longer need to write the embedded-resource-loading boilerplate.

## \[1.0.0] - 2026-06-21

[Section titled “\[1.0.0\] - 2026-06-21”](#100---2026-06-21)

Initial release.

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-1)

* Custom tattoo framework for the in-game tattoo shop, built on S1API. Tattoos register through the game’s own `Resources.Load` pipeline, so they render, persist in saves and sync in multiplayer like vanilla.
* Drop-in **pack format**: `UserData/Inkorporated/Packs/<Pack>/manifest.json` + PNGs. Placements `chest`, `leftarm`, `rightarm`, `face`; optional per-tattoo price; transparent PNGs at any size.
* Public **API** (`Inkorporated.API.RegisterTattoo` / `RegisterTattooFromFile`) for code mods, with a `TattooPlacement` enum. Lazy registration so PNG/texture work happens when the shop first opens.
* **Shop integration**: custom tattoos are injected into the matching tattoo-shop category by cloning an existing option, with the game’s own selection/price/persistence handling reused.
* Bundled **example pack** (8 UV-aligned designs across all placements) gated behind the `LoadExamplePack` preference (default off); extracted to disk as a copyable template, never overwriting an existing folder.
* Correct face-vs-body routing (face layers register under a `/Face/` path so the game applies them to the face mesh).
* Debug build only: a built-in-tattoo **UV template exporter** (`UserData/Inkorporated/Templates/`) and a shop layout diagnostic; neither ships in the release.

# Author a tattoo PNG

> Draw a tattoo PNG whose pixels land on the right body part instead of a wrong limb.

Draw a transparent PNG that lands on the body part you want. A tattoo is a full UV-space skin texture, not a sticker.

**You need:** an image editor with layers, and a reference template (step 1).

## Steps

[Section titled “Steps”](#steps)

1. Get a reference. A DEBUG build of Inkorporated exports every built-in tattoo texture to `Schedule I/UserData/Inkorporated/Templates/<placement>/<name>.png`. The PNGs of the example pack are aligned too. A Release build writes no `Templates/` folder.
2. Open the reference for your placement as a bottom layer. Use the same canvas size.
3. Draw your design over the inked area. Put opaque pixels only where the ink goes. Everything else must be transparent.
4. Hide the reference. Export a PNG with real transparency (RGBA). Colour art works, because the layer tint is white by default.
5. Set the matching `placement` in the manifest. See [Pack format](/mods/inkorporated/guides/pack-format/).

## Why alignment matters

[Section titled “Why alignment matters”](#why-alignment-matters)

The body shares one UV unwrap for torso, arms and legs. The face has its own. The avatar shader samples your PNG across that whole UV. A design centered on a blank canvas lands at the middle of the body UV, often across the legs or arms.

## Size and format

[Section titled “Size and format”](#size-and-format)

* Format: PNG, RGBA, transparent background.
* Canvas: 2048x2048 for chest and arms, 512x512 for face.
* There is no size cap. Resolution changes sharpness only, not placement.
* Paint a whole arm UV island opaque for a full sleeve. Cover the torso for a chest piece.

## Face tattoos

[Section titled “Face tattoos”](#face-tattoos)

`placement: face` needs a design drawn to the face UV, not the body UV. The game routes face and body layers by the `/Face/` segment in the resource path. Inkorporated registers face tattoos under `.../custom/Face/...` for you. `chest`, `leftarm` and `rightarm` use the body mesh.

## Check it works

[Section titled “Check it works”](#check-it-works)

The tattoo appears in the shop under its placement tab. Select it. The ink shows on the intended body part.

## Next

[Section titled “Next”](#next)

* [Pack format](/mods/inkorporated/guides/pack-format/)
* [Troubleshooting](/mods/inkorporated/guides/troubleshooting/)

# Make a tattoo pack

> Add your own tattoo to the Schedule I tattoo shop with a manifest.json and a PNG.

Make a tattoo pack: a folder with a `manifest.json` and a PNG. Your tattoo appears in the in-game tattoo shop.

**You need:** Inkorporated and S1API installed. See [Install](/install/) for MelonLoader, S1API and the mod DLL.

## Steps

[Section titled “Steps”](#steps)

1. Create the folder `Schedule I/UserData/Inkorporated/Packs/MyPack/`.

2. Create `manifest.json` in that folder:

   ```json
   {
     "name": "My Pack",
     "author": "you",
     "tattoos": [
       { "id": "skull", "name": "Skull", "placement": "chest", "file": "skull.png" }
     ]
   }
   ```

3. Put `skull.png` next to it. Use a transparent PNG. The opaque pixels must sit at the UV region of the chest. See [Author a tattoo PNG](/mods/inkorporated/guides/authoring-tattoos/).

4. Start the game.

To start from a working pack, set `LoadExamplePack` to `true` under `[Inkorporated_01_Main]` in `UserData/MelonPreferences.cfg`. Restart. Inkorporated writes `UserData/Inkorporated/Packs/Examples/`. It never overwrites an existing folder. Its tattoos also appear in the shop.

## Check it works

[Section titled “Check it works”](#check-it-works)

`MelonLoader/Latest.log` shows `Pack 'MyPack' (...): 1 tattoo(s)`. In the tattoo shop, “Skull” appears in the Chest category.

## Register a tattoo from code

[Section titled “Register a tattoo from code”](#register-a-tattoo-from-code)

Use this path when your own mod ships the tattoo. List Inkorporated as a dependency and register early:

```csharp
using Inkorporated;
using Inkorporated.Model;


// In OnInitializeMelon:
API.RegisterTattooFromFile("skull", "Skull", TattooPlacement.Chest, pngPath, source: "MyMod");
```

A ready project is in the [example repo](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-InkorporatedExample).

## Where files live

[Section titled “Where files live”](#where-files-live)

| Path                                                      | Content                                                |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `UserData/Inkorporated/Packs/<Pack>/`                     | Your packs: folder, `manifest.json`, PNGs              |
| `UserData/Inkorporated/Templates/`                        | UV reference textures. Only a DEBUG build writes them. |
| `UserData/MelonPreferences.cfg`, `[Inkorporated_01_Main]` | The `LoadExamplePack` toggle                           |

## Next

[Section titled “Next”](#next)

* [Pack format](/mods/inkorporated/guides/pack-format/)
* [Author a tattoo PNG](/mods/inkorporated/guides/authoring-tattoos/)
* [Multiplayer, saves and NPCs](/mods/inkorporated/guides/multiplayer-saves-and-npcs/)
