| Component   | Version / Source                                                                    |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Schedule I  | IL2CPP (current Steam public build)                                                 |
| MelonLoader | `0.7.3+`                                                                            |
| S1API       | [ifBars/S1API\_Forked](https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/p/ifBars/S1API_Forked/) |

Installation

### Recommended: a Thunderstore mod manager

[Section titled “Recommended: a Thunderstore mod manager”](#recommended-a-thunderstore-mod-manager)

Install with r2modman / Gale from the Schedule I community; the dependencies (MelonLoader, S1API) are pulled in automatically. Then install any NPC pack or NPC mod that lists Personnel as a dependency.

### Manual

[Section titled “Manual”](#manual)

1. Install **MelonLoader 0.7.3** for Schedule I.
2. Install **S1API** (its DLLs go in `Mods/` and `Plugins/` per its own instructions).
3. Drop **`Personnel.dll`** into your Schedule I `Mods/` folder.
4. Add NPC packs (see below), or enable the bundled example pack (see Configuration).

## For players: using NPC packs

[Section titled “For players: using NPC packs”](#for-players-using-npc-packs)

An NPC pack is just a folder under:

```plaintext
<Schedule I>/UserData/Personnel/Packs/<PackName>/
```

containing a `manifest.json` and any PNGs it references. On startup Personnel logs each loaded pack with the NPC ids it provides. Packs with `autoRegister` bring their NPCs into the world by themselves; older appearance-only packs are used by whatever consumer mod spawns them. In co-op, everyone needs the same packs installed - the same rule as for mods.

## For pack authors: the pack format

[Section titled “For pack authors: the pack format”](#for-pack-authors-the-pack-format)

The comfortable way is the in-game editor **Personify** (a Side Hustle gamemode): design NPCs live on the menu character, then hit Export - it writes a ready-to-publish pack. By hand, create `UserData/Personnel/Packs/<YourPack>/manifest.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "My Pack",
  "author": "you",
  "schemaVersion": 2,
  "autoRegister": true,
  "npcs": [
    {
      "name": "Pale",
      "appearance": {
        "gender": 0.5, "height": 1.0, "weight": 0.4,
        "skinColor": "#8899AA", "hairPath": "", "hairColor": "#101014",
        "faceLayers": [ { "file": "grin.png", "tint": "#FFFFFF" } ]
      },
      "spawn": { "x": -66.4, "y": -2.9, "z": 86.1, "region": "Westville", "physical": true },
      "schedule": [
        { "type": "walkTo", "time": "07:30", "position": [-70.1, -2.9, 80.0] },
        { "type": "stayInBuilding", "time": "09:00", "duration": 240, "building": "Thrifty Threads" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

* An authored `id` is respected (normalized); without one it is derived as `<packname>_<npcname>`. Ids are the save identity - never change them once a pack shipped (use `saveId` when renaming).
* Appearance mirrors the S1API avatar-settings surface; every field is optional and defaults to the game’s baseline. Layers take either a `path` (existing game layer) or a `file` (pack-relative PNG).
* On top of `appearance` there are `spawn`, `schedule`, `customer`, `dealer`, `inventory`, `relationships` and `contact` blocks - the [Pack Format documentation page](https://docs.doodesch.de/mods/personnel/guides/pack-format/) documents every field.
* Enable the example pack (Configuration below) for a complete, working template.

## For mod developers: spawning the NPCs

[Section titled “For mod developers: spawning the NPCs”](#for-mod-developers-spawning-the-npcs)

Reference `Personnel.dll` (add `[assembly: MelonOptionalDependencies("Personnel")]`) and declare one tiny subclass per NPC you want - then spawn it the normal S1API way:

```csharp
public sealed class PaleNpc : Personnel.PersonnelNpc
{
    protected override string DefId => "examples_pale";   // id from an installed pack
}


// wherever you populate the world:
var npc = new PaleNpc();          // S1API builds the prefab, networks and saves it
npc.Position = spawnPoint;        // then use S1API as usual: schedules, dialogue, ...
```

`DefId` must return a constant (S1API builds prefabs from uninitialized instances). Lower-level entry points on `Personnel.API`: `All` / `TryGet(id, out def)` to enumerate definitions, `BuildAvatarSettings(def)` / `ApplyAppearance(avatar, def)` to realise just the look on any avatar, and `ConfigureFromDef(builder, def)` if you keep your own `NPC` subclass. A complete reference consumer lives in the repo as `PersonOfInterest`.

## Configuration

[Section titled “Configuration”](#configuration)

Settings live in `UserData/MelonPreferences.cfg` under `Personnel_01_Main`.

| Setting              | Default | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `LoadExamplePack`    | `false` | When on, drops a small example pack into `UserData/Personnel/Packs/Examples` on startup (if not already there) - ready-made NPCs plus a manifest template to copy. Requires a game restart. Never overwrites an existing Examples folder. |
| `EnableAutoRegister` | `true`  | Kill switch for pack auto-registration. When off, packs with `autoRegister` load as data only and nothing spawns. Requires a game restart.                                                                                                |

## How it works

[Section titled “How it works”](#how-it-works)

Packs are parsed into plain definitions at startup (no Unity objects). When a consumer first uses a definition, Personnel maps it onto S1API’s avatar-settings builder; custom PNG layers are loaded into textures, put on a clone of a built-in tattoo of the same kind, and registered in the game’s avatar object library under the layer path - so the game’s own pipeline renders, saves and networks them like built-in layers. Full NPCs ride entirely on S1API’s prefab/networking machinery via `PersonnelNpc`.

Compatibility

* IL2CPP build only (current Steam public branch).
* **Multiplayer:** NPCs spawned via S1API follow S1API’s networking. Custom PNG layers are referenced by resource-path string - clients need Personnel and the same pack to render them; others simply don’t show that layer (no desync, no crash).

Credits

* **DooDesch** - mod author.
* **[ifBars/S1API](https://github.com/ifBars/S1API)** - the modding API this is built on.

# Personnel API

> Look up every public type and member of Personnel 2.2.2.

## Use this API

[Section titled “Use this API”](#use-this-api)

Reference `Personnel.dll` from your Mods folder:

```xml
<Reference Include="Personnel">
  <HintPath>$(ModsDirectory)\Personnel.dll</HintPath>
  <Private>false</Private>
</Reference>
```

Mark it optional, so your mod still loads without it:

```csharp
[assembly: MelonOptionalDependencies("Personnel")]
```

Without Personnel its types are missing too. Call it only after you know it loaded.

First steps: [Make an NPC pack](/mods/personnel/guides/getting-started/).

Source: [`API.cs`](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Personnel/blob/v2.2.2/API.cs) at `v2.2.2`.

# API

> Public, stable entry point for other mods (e.g.

```csharp
public static class API
```

Namespace `Personnel`

Public, stable entry point for other mods (e.g. Backrooms) that want to consume user-authored NPC definitions. Reference Personnel.dll and declare `[MelonOptionalDependencies("Personnel")]`. The primitive most consumers need is `BuildAvatarSettings` / `ApplyAppearance` - realise a definition’s look onto any live `Avatar`. Definitions are loaded from packs on startup; register your own programmatically via `Register`.

## Properties

[Section titled “Properties”](#properties)

### All

[Section titled “All”](#all)

```csharp
public static IReadOnlyList<NpcDef> All { get; }
```

All loaded NPC definitions (pack-sourced + API-registered).

## Methods

[Section titled “Methods”](#methods)

### TryGet

[Section titled “TryGet”](#tryget)

```csharp
public static bool TryGet(string id, out NpcDef def)
```

Look up a definition by id (case-insensitive).

### Register

[Section titled “Register”](#register)

```csharp
public static bool Register(NpcDef def)
```

Register a definition programmatically (de-duplicated by Source/Id). Returns false on duplicate.

### BuildAvatarSettings

[Section titled “BuildAvatarSettings”](#buildavatarsettings)

```csharp
public static AvatarSettings BuildAvatarSettings(NpcDef def)
```

Realise a definition’s appearance into a vanilla `AvatarSettings`. Registers any custom PNG layers on first use. Call from the main thread (it touches Unity resources).

### ApplyAppearance

[Section titled “ApplyAppearance”](#applyappearance)

```csharp
public static bool ApplyAppearance(Avatar avatar, NpcDef def)
```

Build the definition’s `AvatarSettings` and load it onto a live avatar.

### ApplyDistortion

[Section titled “ApplyDistortion”](#applydistortion)

```csharp
public static void ApplyDistortion(Avatar avatar, NpcDef def)
```

Added in `1.1.0`

Apply a definition’s extreme body distortion (Personify’s Experimental tab: bone scale/hide, mesh hide) onto a live avatar. A separate pass from `ApplyAppearance` since vanilla AvatarSettings has no such concept - call this right after loading the normal appearance.

### Reload

[Section titled “Reload”](#reload)

```csharp
public static void Reload()
```

Rescan the packs folder (drops+reloads pack-sourced defs, keeps API-registered ones).

### ConfigureFromDef

[Section titled “ConfigureFromDef”](#configurefromdef)

```csharp
public static void ConfigureFromDef(NPCPrefabBuilder builder, NpcDef def)
```

Configures an S1API `NPCPrefabBuilder` from a definition - identity + full appearance (+ the def’s spawn position if it has one). This is the one call needed to turn a Personnel definition into a real, networked, save/load-safe S1API NPC. Prefer subclassing `PersonnelNpc` (which calls this for you); call this directly only if you keep your own `NPC` subclass and want to configure it inside its `ConfigurePrefab`.

### AddMapMarker

[Section titled “AddMapMarker”](#addmapmarker)

```csharp
public static void AddMapMarker(GameObject npcRoot)
```

Added in `1.1.0`

Adds a map marker (the game’s own `NPCPoI`) to a live custom NPC so players can find it on the phone map. Client-local and cosmetic - no economy role, no networking. Safe to call once the NPC object exists (e.g. from `PersonnelNpc`’s creation hook); no-ops if the map manager or NPC component is not ready.

A member listed under a version is callable from that version on. Check “Removed” and “Signature changed” before you raise the version you require: a mod built against the old signature breaks on the new one.

## \[2.2.1] - 2026-10-15

[Section titled “\[2.2.1\] - 2026-10-15”](#221---2026-10-15)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-1)

* Custom tattoos and face layers from packs show on NPCs again on game 0.4.7.
* A pack car without a position spawns where its NPC starts, not at the edge of the map.

## \[2.2.0] - 2026-08-13

[Section titled “\[2.2.0\] - 2026-08-13”](#220---2026-08-13)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-2)

* An NPC whose pack sets only a skin colour gets matching eyelids. They fell back to the default tan, which read as pale lids on any dark skin.
* Face layers are placed the way the game reads them: the mouth first, the facial hair second. A pack that listed them in another order had a detail layer drawn in the hair colour.
* Face layers past the fifth are dropped and named in the log. They used to overwrite the facial hair instead.
* Body layers past the eighth are dropped on the S1API prefab path too. Only the runtime path had that ceiling, so a prefab NPC lost a garment with nothing said.

## \[2.1.1] - 2026-08-01

[Section titled “\[2.1.1\] - 2026-08-01”](#211---2026-08-01)

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-2)

* Runs on Schedule I 0.4.6f11.
* Needs S1API 3.1.1, up from 3.0.5. Update it along with the mod.

## \[2.1.0] - 2026-07-30

[Section titled “\[2.1.0\] - 2026-07-30”](#210---2026-07-30)

Writing a schedule meant guessing coordinates, because the game shows none anywhere. Now the console hands them to you.

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added)

* Dev-console commands for pack authors (console has to be enabled in Settings):

  * `personnel pos [HH:MM]` - the spot you are standing on, as `[x, y, z]` or as a finished `walkTo` action for that time.
  * `personnel spawn` - the same spot as a `spawn` block, with `rotationY` and `region` filled in.
  * `personnel route HH:MM` - collects a step per stop in `UserData/Personnel/route.json`; `personnel route show` prints the block ready to paste into `"schedule": [ ... ]`, `clear` starts over.
  * `personnel npcs [filter]` - loaded definitions, and where the physical ones are right now.
  * `personnel help` - the list.

* Results are copied to the clipboard and written to the MelonLoader log, with an in-game notification confirming the command ran.

## \[2.0.0] - 2026-07-22

[Section titled “\[2.0.0\] - 2026-07-22”](#200---2026-07-22)

NPC mods without code: a pack manifest can now describe everything an NPC needs - where it spawns, what it does all day, its economy role - and Personnel spawns it as a real world NPC on its own.

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-1)

* `autoRegister` (pack level) / `spawn.auto` (per NPC): Personnel registers opted-in NPCs as real, networked, saved world NPCs with no consumer mod involved. A kill switch lives in the settings (`EnableAutoRegister`). Packs that already ship a consumer DLL are safe: a compiled NPC class for the same id always wins over the generated one.
* `spawn` grew `rotationY` (spawn yaw), `region` (now actually applied) and `physical`. Non-physical NPCs are phone contacts only - no world body, no pathing cost. Default: physical exactly when the NPC has a schedule.
* `schedule`: full daily schedules in the manifest - `walkTo`, `stayInBuilding`, `sit`, `useVendingMachine`, `useAtm`, `useSlotMachine`, `locationDialogue`, `locationAction`, `driveToCarPark`, `dealSignal`. Times are `"HH:MM"` strings.
* `relationships`: `delta`, `unlocked`, `unlockType`, `connections` (by NPC id).
* `customer`: the whole customer economy - spending, orders per week, preferred day/time, standards, direct approach, first sample, mutual relation requirement, call-police chance, dependence, affinities, preferred properties.
* `dealer`: type, cut, signing fee, home, completed-deals variable, quality tolerances. Definitions with a dealer block now get the proper dealer base prefab (previously manifest dealers were built on the civilian prefab).
* `inventory`: random cash range, startup items (with quantities), clear-each-night.
* `contact`: `mapMarker: false` removes the phone-map marker, `visible: false` (experimental) skips the contact unlock.
* `behavior.aggression`, `maxHealth` and `scale` are now actually applied to spawned NPCs.
* Id stability: an authored `id` in the manifest is respected (previously always derived from folder and name), `packId` pins the derivation prefix, and `saveId` lets a renamed NPC keep matching old saves. `schemaVersion` marks the manifest format (current: 2).
* Distant custom NPCs get a proper billboard impostor instead of a blank one (on S1API builds that support impostor configuration).

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-3)

* Pack and NPC registration order is now deterministic across machines - co-op peers agree on it.
* Contact unlock and map marker are unchanged by default but can be opted out per NPC.

## \[1.1.0] - 2026-07-08

[Section titled “\[1.1.0\] - 2026-07-08”](#110---2026-07-08)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-3)

* Custom NPCs now show their real name in the phone Contacts app (previously ”???”) and can be found on the map. Personnel unlocks each spawned NPC’s contact and gives it a map marker.
* Clothing no longer carries over from one spawned NPC to the next. The game clears only six of its eight avatar layer slots, so an NPC with more layers than that leaves a garment bound to the material for whoever is applied after it.
* A definition asking for more than eight body layers no longer loses one at random. The surplus is dropped deliberately, clothing first, and named in the log.

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-2)

* Opt-in economy roles via a pack’s `behavior.conversation`: `"customer"` or `"dealer"` makes the NPC a real customer or dealer, while the default `"none"` stays a plain, non-economy contact.
* `API.AddMapMarker(GameObject)` to add a map marker to any live custom NPC.

## \[1.0.0] - 2026-07-06

[Section titled “\[1.0.0\] - 2026-07-06”](#100---2026-07-06)

Initial release.

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-3)

* NPC pack loading from `UserData/Personnel/Packs/<PackName>/` (`manifest.json` + optional PNGs), with per-pack log lines listing the loaded NPC ids.
* Deep appearance definitions mirroring the S1API avatar-settings surface: body, skin, hair, face, eyes, eyebrows, clothing layers, accessories, and custom PNG layers loaded from the pack folder.
* Duplicate-proof NPC ids, always derived as `packname_npcname` (normalized); manifest `id` fields are ignored.
* `PersonnelNpc` base class: one tiny subclass per NPC turns a pack definition into a full S1API NPC (prefab, networking, save/load handled by S1API).
* Public API: `All`, `TryGet`, `Register`, `BuildAvatarSettings(def)`, `ApplyAppearance(avatar, def)`, `ConfigureFromDef(builder, def)`, `OnReloaded`, `Reload`.
* Bundled example pack (off by default, `LoadExamplePack`) with two NPCs as a copyable template.
* Mod Manager & Phone App settings integration.

# Add a custom PNG layer

> Ship your own face paint, tattoo or shirt print on a Personnel NPC with a PNG file.

Add your own art to an NPC with a PNG in the pack folder. Custom layers work like [Inkorporated](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Inkorporated) tattoos and follow the same rules.

**You need:** an NPC pack. See [Make an NPC pack](/mods/personnel/guides/getting-started/).

## Steps

[Section titled “Steps”](#steps)

1. Know the rule: the PNG is a full UV-space skin texture, not a sticker. The body shares one UV unwrap for torso, arms and legs. The face has its own. The opaque pixels must sit at the UV position of the target body part. Everything else must be transparent. A shape centered on a blank canvas lands wherever the UV center is, often on the legs or arms.

2. Create the PNG with a transparent background (RGBA). Use 2048x2048 for body layers and 512x512 for face layers. There is no size limit. Resolution changes sharpness only, not placement.

3. Paint over aligned art. The PNGs of the Inkorporated example pack are aligned to the same UVs. So are the files in the `Templates/` folder that a DEBUG build of Inkorporated exports.

4. Put the PNG next to `manifest.json` in the pack folder.

5. Reference it in the manifest. Use `faceLayers` for face art and `bodyLayers` for body art:

   ```json
   "faceLayers": [ { "file": "warpaint.png", "tint": "#FFFFFF" } ],
   "bodyLayers": [ { "file": "sleeve.png",   "tint": "#C0FFEE" } ]
   ```

6. Restart the game.

Colour art works. The default tint is white, and the manifest `tint` multiplies over the PNG.

## Check it works

[Section titled “Check it works”](#check-it-works)

The NPC shows the art on the intended body part. The [Personify](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Personify) editor previews a PNG live on the menu character. Use it to check alignment before you restart the game.

If the art lands on the wrong part, check the UV alignment first. Then check that a face design is in `faceLayers` and a body design is in `bodyLayers`.

## Next

[Section titled “Next”](#next)

* [Pack format](/mods/personnel/guides/pack-format/)
* [Multiplayer and saves](/mods/personnel/guides/multiplayer-and-saves/)
* [Troubleshooting](/mods/personnel/guides/troubleshooting/)

# Make an NPC pack

> Write a manifest.json that adds your own NPC to Schedule I, with no code.

Write a pack folder with one `manifest.json`. Personnel loads it and spawns your NPC in the world.

**You need:** Personnel and S1API installed. See [Install](/install/) for MelonLoader, S1API and the mod DLL.

## Steps

[Section titled “Steps”](#steps)

1. Create the folder `Schedule I/UserData/Personnel/Packs/MyPack/`.

2. Create `manifest.json` in that folder:

   ```json
   {
     "name": "My Pack",
     "author": "you",
     "autoRegister": true,
     "npcs": [
       {
         "id": "mypack_pale",
         "name": "Pale",
         "appearance": { "skinColor": "#8899AA", "hairPath": "Avatar/Hair/Spiky/Spiky" },
         "spawn": { "x": -66.4, "y": -2.9, "z": 86.1, "rotationY": 145, "region": "Westville", "physical": true }
       }
     ]
   }
   ```

3. Set the spawn point. Stand where the NPC must appear. Enable the console in Settings, press the backtick key, and run `personnel spawn`. Paste the result into `spawn`.

4. Optional: add a `schedule`. Walk to each stop and run `personnel route 07:00`. Then run `personnel route show` and paste the steps into `"schedule": [ ... ]`.

5. Restart the game. Pack changes need a restart.

To start from a working pack, set `LoadExamplePack` to `true` under `[Personnel_01_Main]` in `UserData/MelonPreferences.cfg`. Restart. Personnel writes `UserData/Personnel/Packs/Examples/`. It never overwrites an existing folder.

To design the look in a live editor, use [Personify](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Personify). Export the pack and copy the `Personnel/Packs/<name>` folder into `UserData/Personnel/Packs/`.

## Check it works

[Section titled “Check it works”](#check-it-works)

`MelonLoader/Latest.log` lists each pack with its ids:

```plaintext
[Personnel] Pack 'MyPack' (My Pack): 1 NPC(s) [mypack_pale].
```

In game, the NPC stands at the spawn point.

If you do not set `autoRegister`, Personnel only loads the definitions. A mod must then spawn them through the [API](/mods/personnel/api/).

## Next

[Section titled “Next”](#next)

* [Pack format](/mods/personnel/guides/pack-format/)
* [Custom PNG layers](/mods/personnel/guides/custom-png-layers/)
* [Multiplayer and saves](/mods/personnel/guides/multiplayer-and-saves/)
* [Troubleshooting](/mods/personnel/guides/troubleshooting/)
* [API reference](/mods/personnel/api/)

# Keep NPCs working in multiplayer and saves

> Make Personnel NPCs and custom layers stay in sync across co-op players and across save and load.

Follow these rules so Personnel NPCs spawn, sync and save correctly.

**You need:** an NPC pack. See [Make an NPC pack](/mods/personnel/guides/getting-started/).

## Steps

[Section titled “Steps”](#steps)

1. Install the same packs on every player’s machine. This is the same rule as for mods.
2. Spawn NPCs on the host. The host spawns the NPC as a FishNet network object. Clients receive it like any S1API NPC.
3. Keep ids stable. S1API saves NPCs through the game save system, and the definition id is the identity. Never change an id after release. See [Pack format](/mods/personnel/guides/pack-format/#ids-and-saves).
4. Use custom PNG layers only with the pack on every client. The game syncs layers as resource-path strings, not texture bytes. Each client registers the texture from its own copy of the pack.

## Check it works

[Section titled “Check it works”](#check-it-works)

* A player without the pack sees the NPC without the custom art. No desync and no crash.
* After save and load, Personnel registers the texture again from the pack at startup.
* If you remove the pack, the layer disappears from the look without an error.

## Appearance-only mods

[Section titled “Appearance-only mods”](#appearance-only-mods)

`BuildAvatarSettings` and `ApplyAppearance` write plain vanilla `AvatarSettings` onto an avatar. Your mod’s own system decides whether that look syncs or saves. Personnel adds no networking.

## Next

[Section titled “Next”](#next)

* [Custom PNG layers](/mods/personnel/guides/custom-png-layers/)
* [Troubleshooting](/mods/personnel/guides/troubleshooting/)
* [API reference](/mods/personnel/api/)

# Pack format reference

> Look up every manifest.json field of a Personnel NPC pack, from appearance to schedule and economy roles.

Look up the `manifest.json` fields of an NPC pack. A pack is this folder:

```plaintext
Schedule I/UserData/Personnel/Packs/<PackName>/
├── manifest.json
└── *.png              (optional custom layers, referenced by the manifest)
```

Needs Personnel 2.0+ for `autoRegister`, `spawn`, `schedule` and economy roles.

## manifest.json

[Section titled “manifest.json”](#manifestjson)

```json
{
  "name": "My Pack",
  "author": "you",
  "schemaVersion": 2,
  "autoRegister": true,
  "npcs": [
    {
      "id": "mypack_pale",
      "name": "Pale",
      "appearance": {
        "gender": 0.5,
        "height": 1.0,
        "weight": 0.4,
        "skinColor": "#8899AA",
        "hairPath": "Avatar/Hair/Spiky/Spiky",
        "hairColor": "#101014",
        "leftEye":  { "top": 0.5, "bottom": 0.5 },
        "rightEye": { "top": 0.5, "bottom": 0.5 },
        "eyeBallTint": "#FFFFFF",
        "faceLayers": [ { "file": "grin.png", "tint": "#FFFFFF" } ],
        "bodyLayers": [ { "path": "Avatar/Layers/Top/T-Shirt", "tint": "#334455" } ],
        "accessories": [ { "path": "Avatar/Accessories/Feet/Sneakers/Sneakers", "color": "#FFFFFF" } ]
      },
      "behavior": { "aggression": 0.2, "maxHealth": 100, "scale": 1.0 },
      "spawn": {
        "x": -66.4, "y": -2.9, "z": 86.1,
        "rotationY": 145.0,
        "region": "Westville",
        "physical": true
      },
      "contact": { "visible": true, "mapMarker": true },
      "relationships": {
        "delta": 1.5,
        "unlockType": "Recommendation",
        "connections": [ "mypack_other_npc", "jessi_waters" ]
      },
      "customer": {
        "spending": { "min": 300, "max": 900 },
        "ordersPerWeek": { "min": 1, "max": 3 },
        "preferredOrderDay": "Friday",
        "orderTime": "19:30",
        "standards": "Moderate",
        "allowDirectApproach": true,
        "guaranteeFirstSample": false,
        "mutualRelationRequirement": { "min": 1.0, "max": 4.0 },
        "callPoliceChance": 0.05,
        "dependence": { "base": 0.2, "multiplier": 1.0 },
        "affinities": { "marijuana": 0.6, "cocaine": -0.3 },
        "preferredProperties": [ "energizing", "calming" ]
      },
      "inventory": { "cash": { "min": 20, "max": 120 }, "items": [ "baggie" ], "clearEachNight": true },
      "schedule": [
        { "type": "walkTo", "time": "07:30", "position": [-70.1, -2.9, 80.0] },
        { "type": "stayInBuilding", "time": "09:00", "duration": 240, "building": "Thrifty Threads" },
        { "type": "walkTo", "time": "14:00", "position": [-66.4, -2.9, 86.1] }
      ],
      "extensions": { }
    }
  ]
}
```

Every field is optional. A minimal NPC only needs a `name`. Colours are `#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA` hex strings. Personnel logs a warning for an unknown value and skips it. A broken field never removes the whole NPC.

## Ids and saves

[Section titled “Ids and saves”](#ids-and-saves)

* Personnel uses an authored `id` as given, normalized to lowercase `a-z0-9_`.
* Without `id`, Personnel derives `normalize(packId or folder name)_normalize(npc name)`.
* `packId` (top level) fixes the derivation prefix. Renaming the pack folder then keeps the ids.
* Ids must be unique inside a pack. The startup log prints the ids of each pack.
* The id is the save identity. Never change it after you ship the pack.
* To rename, set `saveId` to the OLD id. Existing saves then keep matching.

## Auto-registration

[Section titled “Auto-registration”](#auto-registration)

Set `"autoRegister": true` at top level, or `"auto": true` inside one NPC’s `spawn`. Personnel then registers the NPC as a real S1API world NPC. It is networked, saved and follows its schedule.

* Everyone in a co-op session needs the same packs.
* If a mod ships a compiled class for the same NPC id, the compiled one wins. The log says so.
* The setting `EnableAutoRegister` turns auto-registration off globally.

## spawn

[Section titled “spawn”](#spawn)

| Key           | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `x`, `y`, `z` | Spawn position.                                                                                                                                                         |
| `rotationY`   | Spawn yaw in degrees.                                                                                                                                                   |
| `region`      | `Northtown`, `Westville`, `Downtown`, `Docks`, `Suburbia` or `Uptown`.                                                                                                  |
| `physical`    | `true`: real world body that moves, collides and runs its schedule. `false`: phone contact only, almost no cost. Default: `true` exactly when the NPC has a `schedule`. |
| `auto`        | Overrides the pack’s `autoRegister` for this NPC.                                                                                                                       |

Keep most NPCs of a large pack non-physical. For many physical NPCs, [Siesta](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Siesta) lowers the AI cost.

## schedule

[Section titled “schedule”](#schedule)

An array of actions. `type` decides the other fields. Times are `"HH:MM"` strings, durations are in-game minutes, positions are `[x, y, z]`.

| type                | Fields                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `walkTo`            | `time`, `position`, `faceDestination`, `within`, `warpIfSkipped`                                                                                                               |
| `stayInBuilding`    | `time`, `duration`, `building` (name), `doorIndex`                                                                                                                             |
| `sit`               | `time`, `duration`, `seatSet` (name) or `seatSetPath`, `includeInactive`, `warpIfSkipped`                                                                                      |
| `useVendingMachine` | `time`, `machineGuid` (optional, nearest otherwise)                                                                                                                            |
| `useAtm`            | `time`, `atmGuid` (optional)                                                                                                                                                   |
| `useSlotMachine`    | `time`, `position`, `bet`, `mode` (`single`, `spinCount`, `untilTime`, `untilBroke`, `untilTimeOrBroke`), `spins`, `endTime`, `timeBetweenSpins`. Experimental in multiplayer. |
| `locationDialogue`  | `time`, `position`, `greetingOverride`, `choice`, plus the `walkTo` fields                                                                                                     |
| `locationAction`    | `time`, `position`, `duration`, `action` (`smokeBreak`, `graffiti`, `drinking`, `holdItem`), `equippablePath`, `graffitiRegion`                                                |
| `driveToCarPark`    | `time`, `parkingLot` (name), `vehicle` (name) or `createVehicle: { "code": "shitbox", "position": [x,y,z], "rotationY": 0 }`                                                   |
| `dealSignal`        | No fields. Lets a dealer break its schedule for deals.                                                                                                                         |

* An unknown building or seat name logs a warning. The NPC skips that step.
* `warpIfSkipped: true` places the NPC at the destination when no player was nearby and the step was skipped. Without it the NPC misses the stop and the log says nothing.
* NPCs move only on the navmesh. An unreachable destination leaves the NPC where it was.
* `y` need not be exact. The game samples the navmesh within about 5 units of the destination.

## Console commands for coordinates

[Section titled “Console commands for coordinates”](#console-commands-for-coordinates)

Needs Personnel 2.1+. Enable “Console enabled” in Settings and press the backtick key. Each result goes to your clipboard and to `MelonLoader/Latest.log`.

| Command                   | Result                                                                 |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `personnel pos`           | `[x, y, z]` for any `position` field                                   |
| `personnel pos 07:30`     | A finished `walkTo` action for that time                               |
| `personnel spawn`         | A `spawn` block with `x`, `y`, `z`, `rotationY` and `region` filled in |
| `personnel route 07:30`   | Appends a `walkTo` step to `UserData/Personnel/route.json`             |
| `personnel route show`    | Prints the collected steps, ready to paste into `"schedule": [ ... ]`  |
| `personnel route clear`   | Starts a new route                                                     |
| `personnel npcs [filter]` | Loaded definitions, and where the physical ones are now                |

Vanilla `teleport <property|npc id>` moves you fast, for example `teleport rv` or `teleport jessi_waters`.

Without Personnel 2.1: run `save` in the console, then read `Position` from `%USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\TVGS\Schedule I\Saves\<SteamID>\SaveGame_1\Players\Player_0\Player.json`.

## Roles: customer and dealer

[Section titled “Roles: customer and dealer”](#roles-customer-and-dealer)

A `customer` or `dealer` block gives the NPC that economy role. If both exist, `dealer` wins. Personnel applies only the fields you set. The rest keep the game defaults.

* `customer`: `spending`, `ordersPerWeek`, `preferredOrderDay` (`Monday` to `Sunday`), `orderTime`, `standards` (`VeryLow`, `Low`, `Moderate`, `High`, `VeryHigh`), `allowDirectApproach`, `guaranteeFirstSample`, `mutualRelationRequirement`, `callPoliceChance`, `dependence`, `affinities`, `preferredProperties`.
* `affinities` maps a drug type to a value from -1 to 1. Types: `marijuana`, `methamphetamine`, `cocaine`, `mdma`, `shrooms`, `heroin`.
* `preferredProperties` takes property ids such as `energizing`.
* `dealer`: `type` (`player` or `cartel`), `cut`, `signingFee`, `home` (building name), `completedDealsVariable`, `allowInsufficientQuality`, `allowExcessQuality`.

## contact and relationships

[Section titled “contact and relationships”](#contact-and-relationships)

* `contact.mapMarker: false` removes the phone-map marker.
* `contact.visible: false` skips the contact unlock, so the NPC shows as ”???”. Experimental.
* `relationships.delta` is 0 to 5.
* `relationships.unlocked` is a boolean.
* `relationships.unlockType` is `Recommendation` or `DirectApproach`.
* `relationships.connections` lists NPC ids. Use pack-prefixed ids for pack NPCs and plain ids such as `jessi_waters` for vanilla NPCs.

## Layers

[Section titled “Layers”](#layers)

Each entry in `faceLayers`, `bodyLayers` and `accessories` uses one source:

| Key                    | Meaning                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `path`                 | A Resources path of an in-game layer or accessory. Personify stores these.                                                                      |
| `file`                 | A PNG in the pack folder. Personnel registers it as a custom layer at load. See [Custom PNG layers](/mods/personnel/guides/custom-png-layers/). |
| `tint` (alias `color`) | Hex tint. Default white.                                                                                                                        |

A `file` in `faceLayers` registers on the face mesh. A `file` in `bodyLayers` registers on the body mesh. Accessories take only `path`. Custom accessory meshes are not supported.

## extensions

[Section titled “extensions”](#extensions)

Free-form blocks keyed by consumer name, for example `"backrooms": { ... }`. Personnel passes them through untouched. Each consumer reads its own block.

## Publish a pack

[Section titled “Publish a pack”](#publish-a-pack)

1. Export the pack from [Personify](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Personify). It wraps the pack for Thunderstore with `manifest.json`, README and LICENSE, and your pack under `Personnel/Packs/<name>/`.
2. Add a 256x256 `icon.png`.
3. List `DooDesch-Personnel` as a dependency and upload.

# Troubleshoot Personnel

> Find the cause and fix for a Personnel pack that does not load, spawn or render.

Find your symptom below. Check `MelonLoader/Latest.log` first.

## My pack does not load

[Section titled “My pack does not load”](#my-pack-does-not-load)

Every pack logs one line. A broken pack logs a warning with the file name:

* `manifest has no 'npcs' array`: the JSON root must contain `"npcs": [ ... ]`.
* `failed to read manifest.json`: the JSON is invalid. A trailing comma is the usual cause.
* `an NPC entry has no 'name'`: give every NPC a `name`.

The manifest must be at `UserData/Personnel/Packs/<YourPack>/manifest.json`. Use one folder per pack.

## The log lists my NPCs, but nothing appears in the world

[Section titled “The log lists my NPCs, but nothing appears in the world”](#the-log-lists-my-npcs-but-nothing-appears-in-the-world)

Without `autoRegister`, Personnel only loads definitions. Set `"autoRegister": true`, or let a mod that uses the [API](/mods/personnel/api/) spawn the ids. An NPC with `"physical": false` appears only as a phone contact.

## An NPC does not walk its schedule

[Section titled “An NPC does not walk its schedule”](#an-npc-does-not-walk-its-schedule)

* A step with an invalid `time`, `position` or `type` logs a warning and is skipped.
* An unknown building or seat name logs a warning and the NPC skips that step.
* An unreachable destination leaves the NPC where it stood. Pick a point on the navmesh.
* A step skipped because no player was nearby needs `warpIfSkipped: true`.

## My mod’s spawn fails or uses defaults

[Section titled “My mod’s spawn fails or uses defaults”](#my-mods-spawn-fails-or-uses-defaults)

* `no definition '<id>' found`: the pack is not installed, or the id is wrong. Check the startup log for the exact ids. Without an authored `id`, the id is `packname_npcname`, lowercase.
* Make `DefId` a compile-time constant. Personnel reads it from an uninitialized instance, so a field set in your constructor returns null.
* Spawn after a save is loaded, on the host.

## A custom PNG lands on the wrong limb or shows as a blob

[Section titled “A custom PNG lands on the wrong limb or shows as a blob”](#a-custom-png-lands-on-the-wrong-limb-or-shows-as-a-blob)

The PNG is a full UV-space texture. Align it to the target UV. See [Custom PNG layers](/mods/personnel/guides/custom-png-layers/). Also check the list: `faceLayers` files go to the face mesh, `bodyLayers` files to the body mesh.

## Another player does not see the custom art

[Section titled “Another player does not see the custom art”](#another-player-does-not-see-the-custom-art)

That player needs Personnel and the same pack. See [Multiplayer and saves](/mods/personnel/guides/multiplayer-and-saves/).

## The example pack does not appear

[Section titled “The example pack does not appear”](#the-example-pack-does-not-appear)

Restart the game after you set `LoadExamplePack`. Personnel never overwrites an existing `Packs/Examples` folder. Delete the folder to get a fresh copy.

## Still stuck

[Section titled “Still stuck”](#still-stuck)

Send `MelonLoader/Latest.log` and the pack’s `manifest.json` to support.

# Polyfill

> Keeps older Schedule I mods working after a game update. Puts the names an update took away back into MelonLoader's generated interop assemblies - your mod files are never touched.

|                |                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Latest release | `0.13.16`                                                                                                                                   |
| Download       | [GitHub](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Polyfill) · [Thunderstore](https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/p/DooDesch/Polyfill/) |
| Requires       | MelonLoader 0.7.3                                                                                                                           |
| Help           | [Discord](https://mods.doodesch.de) · [Report a bug](https://support.doodesch.de/polyfill)                                                  |

**Your old mods stopped working after a Schedule I update? Polyfill gets a lot of them running again.**

> ### Do your mods still work?
>
> [Section titled “Do your mods still work?”](#do-your-mods-still-work)
>
> Look them up: **[polyfill.doomods.com](https://polyfill.doomods.com)**
>
> Over 1,300 mods. Pick your game version and see if a mod runs, which version to use and what players wrote about it.
>
> Still broken? Drop your `Latest.log` on the mod’s page there.

The game gets an update. Mods made before it stop working. Polyfill patches the game so they run again.

It patches the game, not your mods. Your own files are never changed, and `polyfillrestore` takes the patch back out.

It cannot save every mod. The index tells you which ones.

Requirements

|                                                        |                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------- |
| [MelonLoader](https://github.com/LavaGang/MelonLoader) | 0.7.3+ - the mod loader |
| Anything else                                          | Nothing                 |

Install

Mod manager: install and it places both files for you.

By hand:

1. `Polyfill.Boot.dll` into `Plugins/`
2. `Polyfill.dll` into `Mods/`

Keep both files installed. The plugin restores compatibility before mods load; the mod runs repairs that need the running game and adds the console commands. MelonLoader ignores the plugin in `Mods/`.

## Console

[Section titled “Console”](#console)

Needs the developer console enabled in the game’s settings.

```plaintext
polyfill                 what it found in your mods at startup
polyfilllist             every mod, with its verdict
polyfillshow <mod>       everything one mod asks for that is missing
polyfillunfixed <mod>    only what cannot be pointed at anything
polyfillexport           write one file with everything, ready to send
polyfillshare on|off     send anonymous reports to the index, or stop
polyfillshare show       print exactly what would be sent
polyfillprobe <type>     ask the runtime whether a name resolves
polyfillrestore          undo every repair, takes effect on the next launch
polyfillregen            have MelonLoader build the game's generated assemblies again
```

After a game update Polyfill notices that MelonLoader rebuilt those assemblies and starts from the new ones. `polyfillregen` is for the case where it says it cannot find an untouched copy of something: it asks MelonLoader to build the whole set again, which takes a few minutes on the next launch.

The full report is written to `UserData/Polyfill/last-run.txt`, and the untouched copy of anything it changed sits next to it as `<name>.dll.polyfill-orig`.

## Settings

[Section titled “Settings”](#settings)

`MelonPreferences.cfg`, category `Polyfill`:

* `Enabled` - off means nothing is read and nothing is changed
* `DryRun` - work out what is missing, write the report, leave the game alone

## What it cannot fix

[Section titled “What it cannot fix”](#what-it-cannot-fix)

* **Behaviour behind an unchanged signature.** A method that kept its name and now does something else.
* **Reordered enum values used as plain numbers.** The compiler erased the type; a `12` is not distinguishable from an array index. It is reported, never rewritten - guessing wrong here writes into your save.
* **A type that moved AND was renamed.** .NET type forwarding matches on the name, so it cannot follow `ScheduleOne.Weather.X` to `ScheduleOne.Core.Weather.X`.
* **Removed with no successor.** A forwarder needs something to point at.
* **Scene and prefab paths.** `transform.Find("UI/HUD/...")` compiles forever and returns null. No rule can find these: they are strings, so nothing reports them and the mod simply does nothing. A named repair for one mod is possible where the old effect is unambiguous - GraphicsMOD’s lighting toggle is one - but that is a hand-written fix per mod, never a rule that keeps paths working.

Everything in that list shows up as a line in the report rather than as a crash.

## The compatibility index

[Section titled “The compatibility index”](#the-compatibility-index)

[polyfill.doomods.com](https://polyfill.doomods.com) lists which mods run on which game version. It is built from reports Polyfill sends, and only if you allow it: Polyfill asks once and sends nothing if you say no.

A report holds your mods with version and author, what was missing and what Polyfill did about it, errors a mod threw and where in its code, and how long you played. Never your name, your save, your folders or the text of an error. The full list: [How this works](https://polyfill.doomods.com/about).

## For mod authors

[Section titled “For mod authors”](#for-mod-authors)

Your mod probably has a page on [polyfill.doomods.com](https://polyfill.doomods.com) already:

* what it is missing on each game version, by name
* errors from players’ sessions, with the method they came from
* a live badge for your README or mod page
* all of it as JSON, no key: [API](https://polyfill.doomods.com/about/api)

Want your mod off the list? [Ask here](https://polyfill.doomods.com/about#withdraw).

## Building

[Section titled “Building”](#building)

```plaintext
dotnet build Boot/Polyfill.Boot.csproj -c Release
dotnet build Report/Polyfill.csproj -c Release
```

Both need DLLs from a Schedule I install that has started once with MelonLoader. Add the two folders to each command:

```plaintext
-p:MelonLoaderPath="<game>/MelonLoader/net6" -p:GameManagedPath="<game>/MelonLoader/Il2CppAssemblies"
```

The plugin only needs the first one. A build without `-p:Version=` calls itself `0.0.0-dev`.

Credits

Schedule I by TVGS. Built on [MelonLoader](https://github.com/LavaGang/MelonLoader) and [Mono.Cecil](https://github.com/jbevain/cecil).

This mod is written with help from generative AI tools (Anthropic Claude, OpenAI Codex).

### For mod authors

[Section titled “For mod authors”](#for-mod-authors-1)

* An error on your mod’s page now carries two frames: your own method, and the frame that threw.
* Errors are no longer misattributed. Every mod claimed the `System` namespace, so any frame from inside .NET was booked against whichever mod was listed first.

[Section titled “\[0.11.7\] - 2026-08-31”](#0117---2026-08-31)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-36)

* Media Player’s app fills the phone screen again. It had been squeezed into a strip at the top since the game rebuilt the screen it borrows.

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-6)

* Polyfill now says when a mod borrows a piece of the game’s own screens. Those mods can pass every check here and still look wrong on your phone.

## \[0.11.6] - 2026-08-31

[Section titled “\[0.11.6\] - 2026-08-31”](#0116---2026-08-31)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-37)

* Mods that open the sleep screen work again. The repair for it shipped in 0.11.3 and never once ran: it looked for the wrong thing and gave up without saying so.
* Mods built on the main menu’s screens load again, LethalLizard’s Mod Manager among them.
* Mods that read or change a dealer’s cut work again.
* When Polyfill says a mod is missing something, it now shows enough of the name to tell it apart from what the game has. Two names that looked identical in the report were not.

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-7)

* polyfill.doomods.com has a “Find this mod” button on every mod, so you can go and get the thing you just read about.

## \[0.11.5] - 2026-08-30

[Section titled “\[0.11.5\] - 2026-08-30”](#0115---2026-08-30)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-38)

* Polyfill stops listing a mod as broken when the game still has everything it asked for. It counted how many arguments a mod named instead of checking which ones.
* Mods that change the object and route pickers on the management clipboard work again. They loaded without complaining and then did nothing.
* Mods that open a storage screen from a container work again. Two of the three ways to open one were repaired and the third was missed.

## \[0.11.4] - 2026-08-29

[Section titled “\[0.11.4\] - 2026-08-29”](#0114---2026-08-29)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-39)

* Another fix for overlay mods: 0.11.3 stopped the crash but drew nothing, so a clock or a crosshair was simply missing. The image is on screen now.
* A repair that cannot do the job says so and steps aside, instead of leaving a mod loaded and silent. `polyfillfixes` shows it as failed and the log gives the reason.

## \[0.11.3] - 2026-08-29

[Section titled “\[0.11.3\] - 2026-08-29”](#0113---2026-08-29)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-40)

* Overlay mods draw again. ClockOverlay and EZCrosshair threw an error every frame instead of drawing, which filled the log and could take the game down with it.
* Mods that open or close the sleep screen work again. 0.4.6 replaced the call they use, and Polyfill now opens and closes it the way the game does.
* Mods that close the pause menu close it. They loaded without complaining and then did nothing.

## \[0.11.2] - 2026-08-28

[Section titled “\[0.11.2\] - 2026-08-28”](#0112---2026-08-28)

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-7)

* The sharing question now names everything that is sent: mod authors, how long you played, and any errors a mod threw. It said “mod names and versions only” and that was less than the truth.
* `polyfillshare on` says the same, and points at `polyfillshare show` so you can read the exact text.

## \[0.11.1] - 2026-08-28

[Section titled “\[0.11.1\] - 2026-08-28”](#0111---2026-08-28)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-41)

* polyfill.doomods.com counted every launch as a separate player. Your PC rolled a new id each time the game started, so six sessions looked like six people.

## \[0.11.0] - 2026-08-28

[Section titled “\[0.11.0\] - 2026-08-28”](#0110---2026-08-28)

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-8)

* polyfill.doomods.com now says whether a mod actually works, not just whether it starts. Polyfill watches your session for errors and reports what it saw when you leave the game.
* The list shows how long people played before answering, so a mod nobody has really used says so instead of looking fine.

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-8)

* Reports go out when you quit, not while the game loads. A mod that starts and then breaks was passing the old check.
* Only the error type and the line it came from are sent. Never the error text, which can contain your save name or a folder path.

## \[0.10.1] - 2026-08-28

[Section titled “\[0.10.1\] - 2026-08-28”](#0101---2026-08-28)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-42)

* The sharing question stops coming back. It appeared on every launch and no button could stop it - the answer was written but never read back.

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-9)

* The compatibility list now says a mod “starts” rather than “works”. Polyfill checks what a mod asks the game for while it loads, which is not the same as playing it.
* Reports say which Polyfill wrote them, so polyfill.doomods.com can show when a mod was fixed by an update rather than by a game change.

## \[0.10.0] - 2026-08-28

[Section titled “\[0.10.0\] - 2026-08-28”](#0100---2026-08-28)

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-9)

* Check whether a mod still works before you install it: polyfill.doomods.com lists what other players reported for your game version.
* Polyfill asks once, on your first launch, whether it may send what it found. Say no and nothing ever leaves your PC.
  * `polyfillshare show` prints exactly what would be sent, `polyfillshare on` and `off` change your mind.
* Only mod names, versions and what Polyfill repaired are sent. Never your name, your save, your folders, or which mods you run together.

### For mod authors

[Section titled “For mod authors”](#for-mod-authors-2)

* `polyfill-check YourMod.dll --game 0.4.6f13` lists what a game update broke in your mod, with no game and no MelonLoader installed.
  * It agreed with the in-game report on all 44 mods the two were run against.
* Your mod’s page on the index names every member the game no longer has, and whether Polyfill bridged it, refused it, or found nothing to point at.

## \[0.9.0] - 2026-08-14

[Section titled “\[0.9.0\] - 2026-08-14”](#090---2026-08-14)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-67)

* Mods stop throwing thousands of errors a session. A type Polyfill put back had its own members skipped, so one ATM reading alone threw once a frame for as long as the game ran.
* OG Backpack saves and loads its contents again, and its station panels work. One dead patch target was taking the whole class with it, five times over.
* Lithium’s shop prices refresh again. 0.4.6 renamed an argument, and Harmony matches those by name.
* Lithium’s drying rack and ATM screens work again.
* A nested type Polyfill put back is nested again. It was written at the top level under a name nothing asks for, so the repair reported success and the mod threw on the type.

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-13)

* `polyfillfixes` gains `split-screen-patches`: where 0.4.6 split a station screen’s `SetIsOpen` into `Open` and `Close`, a patch aimed at the old name runs again from both.
* The report says when a patch will be moved rather than left dead, so a working mod stops being listed as broken.

## \[0.8.0] - 2026-08-14

[Section titled “\[0.8.0\] - 2026-08-14”](#080---2026-08-14)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-69)

* OG Backpack opens with B again. The storage window has three `Open` methods, all three grew an argument in 0.4.6, and the repair answered for the wrong one.
* Mods that patch the mixing or chemistry station screen work again. Those two and two more were renamed in 0.4.6, and a patch aimed at the old name now reaches the method the game calls.
* StackPro talks to other players again. 0.4.6 took the Steam ids off the lobby, and all three are still derivable from what it kept.
* Lithium reads a dealer’s type and an NPC’s walking speed again, and its ATM screen patches apply.
* DealOptimizer finds the counteroffer price box again. It became an `AmountSelector`, and the input field inside it is the same control.

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-13)

* The report stops naming members that were never gone. 0.4.6 moved eight of them onto base classes, where the game finds them anyway; four mods in one report were called blocked over that alone.
* One repair that fails no longer costs the other fifty. An emitter that threw took the whole assembly with it, and the log said only that it had been left alone.

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-14)

* When a member moved to a base class under a new name, the report says which class and which name, so a mod author has an answer rather than a dead end.
* `polyfillfixes` gains `patches-on-grown-overloads`, which moves a mod’s patch onto the method the game calls when the old signature only exists because Polyfill put it back.

## \[0.5.0] - 2026-08-12

[Section titled “\[0.5.0\] - 2026-08-12”](#050---2026-08-12)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-78)

* After a Schedule I update Polyfill starts from the game’s new files. It used to keep writing its copy of the old ones back over them, which broke mods that had been fine.
* Repairs keep working when the game reaches 0.5.0 or 1.0. Version numbers were compared in a way that read 0.5.0 as older than 0.4.6f5, which would have switched the rename history off.
* A repair a person wrote by hand is used before one guessed from spelling. Two similar-looking names could stop the better answer from being used at all.

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-19)

* The report says what Polyfill DID, not only what it found. `polyfillexport` gains a REFUSED section for every repair it had a candidate for and did not trust.
* `polyfillregen` has MelonLoader build the game’s generated files again, for when Polyfill reports that it has no untouched copy of one left.

## \[0.4.3] - 2026-08-12

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-79)

* OverTheCounter’s co-op sync is no longer switched off by a version number. It demanded exactly the SteamNetworkLib it was built with, and the newer one carries everything it calls.
