Installation

### Recommended: a Thunderstore mod manager

[Section titled “Recommended: a Thunderstore mod manager”](#recommended-a-thunderstore-mod-manager)

Install with a mod manager (r2modman / Gale) from the Schedule I community; the dependencies (MelonLoader, S1API) are pulled in automatically.

### Manual

[Section titled “Manual”](#manual)

1. Install **MelonLoader 0.7.3** for Schedule I.
2. Install **S1API** (its DLLs go in `Mods/` and `Plugins/` per its own instructions).
3. Drop **`SideHustle.dll`** into your Schedule I `Mods/` folder.
4. Install one or more gamemode mods that use Side Hustle.

## Configuration

[Section titled “Configuration”](#configuration)

Open the **Settings** tab in the hub to change these in game. They are stored in `UserData/MelonPreferences.cfg` under `SideHustle_01_Main`.

| Setting                    | Default | What it does                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Enabled`                  | `true`  | Show the Side Hustle menu entry. Off hides it without uninstalling (only in the cfg).                              |
| `ShowUninstalledGamemodes` | `true`  | Also list gamemodes you don’t have installed.                                                                      |
| `AskHostOnContinue`        | `true`  | Clicking Continue or a save slot offers to open it as a public lobby.                                              |
| `AcceptStrangerMessages`   | `true`  | Anyone looking at your public lobby can send you a short message.                                                  |
| `MenuStatePanel`           | `true`  | Info column on the right of the main menu (needs Sideload 1.13.0+).                                                |
| `JoinChatPanel`            | `true`  | Chat column on the screens you pass through while joining.                                                         |
| `DeferModsUntilLobby`      | `false` | Load only Side Hustle and Sideload at startup; the rest loads when you host or join. Takes effect after a restart. |
| `AlwaysLoadMods`           | `""`    | File names that load at startup even with `DeferModsUntilLobby` on, comma-separated.                               |

## For mod authors

[Section titled “For mod authors”](#for-mod-authors)

Make your mod show up as a gamemode in a few lines. Reference `SideHustle.dll`, declare it as an optional dependency so your mod still loads if Side Hustle is absent, and register from your `OnInitializeMelon`:

```csharp
[assembly: MelonOptionalDependencies("SideHustle")]


SideHustle.API.Register(new GamemodeDescriptor
{
    Id = "you.yourmode",                 // stable, unique
    DisplayName = "Your Mode",
    Description = "What your gamemode does.",
    Author = "You",
    Support = GamemodeSupport.Singleplayer,   // or Multiplayer / Hybrid
    Surface = GamemodeSurface.MenuSpace,      // overlay on the menu (no save), or World
    OnLaunchSingleplayer = ctx => { /* start your gamemode */ },
    OnExitToHub = ctx => { /* clean up when the player backs out */ }
});
```

For a multiplayer gamemode set `Support` to `Multiplayer` or `Hybrid` and add `OnHostMultiplayer` / `OnJoinMultiplayer`. Side Hustle creates and tracks the lobby and (for `World` gamemodes) boots the session, then hands you a `LaunchContext` with the role (`Host`, `Client` or `Singleplayer`), lobby id, player count and the host’s settings. Re-registering your own `Id` is safe; `Register` logs every problem it finds in a descriptor. Call `ctx.ReturnToHub()` from your gamemode when it finishes to return to the menu.

Since API version 3 (`API.ApiVersion`, `API.Has(...)`) a gamemode can also:

* listen to `SessionStarted` / `SessionEnded` and `PlayerJoined` / `PlayerLeft`, and read `API.Players`;
* show a short message on screen with `API.ShowNotice`;
* send its own messages to the other players with `API.SendToAll` / `API.SendTo` and receive them with `API.OnMessage`, without its own networking code.

`OnExitToHub` runs exactly once per session, also when Side Hustle aborts a session that failed to start. `Examples/SideHustleLink.cs` is a copy-in file that keeps Side Hustle optional, and `Examples/ExampleGamemode` is a complete gamemode to start from. The full reference is on the [docs site](https://docs.doodesch.de/mods/sidehustle/).

Compatibility

* IL2CPP build only (current Steam public branch).
* Works alongside any other MelonLoader/S1API mod. Side Hustle only adds a main-menu entry and the registration API; it does not touch gameplay or saves.

Credits

* **DooDesch** - mod author.
* **[ifBars/S1API](https://github.com/ifBars/S1API)** - the modding API this is built on.

# SideHustle API

> Look up every public type and member of SideHustle 3.0.0.

## Use this API

[Section titled “Use this API”](#use-this-api)

Reference `SideHustle.dll` from your Mods folder:

```xml
<Reference Include="SideHustle">
  <HintPath>$(ModsDirectory)\SideHustle.dll</HintPath>
  <Private>false</Private>
</Reference>
```

Mark it optional, so your mod still loads without it:

```csharp
[assembly: MelonOptionalDependencies("SideHustle")]
```

Without SideHustle its types are missing too. Call it only after you know it loaded.

First steps: [Add a gamemode](/mods/sidehustle/guides/getting-started/).

Source: [`Api/API.cs`, `Api/ApiFeatures.cs`, `Api/GamemodeDescriptor.cs`, `Api/GamemodeTypes.cs`, `Api/LaunchContext.cs`, `Api/ModPolicy.cs`, `Api/Registry.cs`, `Api/SessionTypes.cs`, `Api/SettingDescriptor.cs`, `Api/WorldHygiene.cs`, `Multiplayer/MultiplayerInfo.cs`](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-SideHustle/blob/v3.0.0/Api/API.cs) at `v3.0.0`.

# API

> Public, stable entry point for mods that want to appear as a gamemode in Side Hustle's main-menu list.

```csharp
public static class API
```

Namespace `SideHustle`

Public, stable entry point for mods that want to appear as a gamemode in Side Hustle’s main-menu list. Register early (e.g. in your mod’s OnInitializeMelon). Registration is load-order independent, so it does not matter whether Side Hustle or your mod loads first. Reference SideHustle.dll and declare `[assembly: MelonOptionalDependencies("SideHustle")]` so the hub loads first and your mod still loads cleanly if it is absent.

## Properties

[Section titled “Properties”](#properties)

### ApiVersion

[Section titled “ApiVersion”](#apiversion)

```csharp
public static int ApiVersion { get; }
```

Added in `3.0.0`

The version of this API surface. Rule: it goes up by one with every release that ADDS public API, and never for a fix. 1 = the 1.x hub (Register, descriptor basics), 2 = the 2.x additions (host settings, presets, mod policy, world hygiene flags, KickPlayer), 3 = Side Hustle 2.5.0 (validation, lifecycle events, players, notices, gamemode messages, `Has`).

A property, not a const: a const is copied into the consumer at ITS compile time and would report the version the consumer was built against instead of the one running. Reading this on a Side Hustle older than 2.5.0 throws `MissingMethodException`; the copy-in `SideHustleLink` shim reads it by reflection and returns 0 there.

### IsReady

[Section titled “IsReady”](#isready)

```csharp
public static bool IsReady { get; internal set; }
```

True once Side Hustle’s own OnInitializeMelon has run. `Ready` fires at the same moment.

### Registered

[Section titled “Registered”](#registered)

```csharp
public static IReadOnlyList<GamemodeDescriptor> Registered { get; }
```

A snapshot of the registered gamemodes. Since 2.5.0 this is a copy: registering or removing a gamemode later does not change a list you already hold.

### CurrentSession

[Section titled “CurrentSession”](#currentsession)

```csharp
public static LaunchContext CurrentSession { get; }
```

Added in `3.0.0`

The running gamemode session, or null. Set just before `SessionStarted` and cleared just before `SessionEnded`. Since 2.5.0.

### Players

[Section titled “Players”](#players)

```csharp
public static IReadOnlyList<SessionPlayer> Players { get; }
```

Added in `3.0.0`

The players in the current session as a snapshot copy (empty outside a session). A singleplayer session holds only the local player. Display names follow the session alias where one is known. Since 2.5.0.

### MaxMessageBytes

[Section titled “MaxMessageBytes”](#maxmessagebytes)

```csharp
public static int MaxMessageBytes { get; }
```

Added in `3.0.0`

The largest payload `SendToAll(string, string, byte[])` and `SendTo(ulong, string, string, byte[])` accept, in bytes. Since 2.5.0.

## Methods

[Section titled “Methods”](#methods)

### Has

[Section titled “Has”](#has)

```csharp
public static bool Has(string feature)
```

Added in `3.0.0`

True when this Side Hustle supports the named feature. Use the constants on `ApiFeatures`; matching is case-insensitive and an unknown name is false. Exists since 2.5.0 (API version 3): on an older Side Hustle the method itself is missing, so call it through the `SideHustleLink` shim or guard it.

### Register

[Section titled “Register”](#register)

```csharp
public static void Register(GamemodeDescriptor descriptor)
```

Register (or replace, by `Id`) a gamemode. Replacing an existing id is allowed and makes hot-reload / double-registration safe. Since 2.5.0 the descriptor is checked here and every problem is logged with the gamemode id and the field name; nothing is rejected that worked before. A second registration of the same id from a DIFFERENT mod is logged as a warning and still replaces the first.

### Unregister

[Section titled “Unregister”](#unregister)

```csharp
public static bool Unregister(string id)
```

Remove a previously registered gamemode. Returns true if one was removed.

### KickPlayer

[Section titled “KickPlayer”](#kickplayer)

```csharp
public static bool KickPlayer(
    ulong steamId64,
    string reason = "Kicked by host")
```

Added in `1.5.3`

Host-only: kick the connected player with this Steam id (id64) from the current session. A no-op on a client or if no such player is connected, and never kicks the host itself. Returns true if a player was kicked. Reusable by any gamemode that manages a Side Hustle lobby.

### ShowNotice

[Section titled “ShowNotice”](#shownotice)

```csharp
public static void ShowNotice(string text, float seconds = 4f)
```

Added in `3.0.0`

Show a short notice to the local player. In the world it is the game’s own notification popup (titled with the running gamemode’s name) and stays `seconds`; in the menu it is the hub’s toast, whose duration is fixed. Safe from any thread: calls off the main thread are queued to the next frame. Since 2.5.0.

### SendToAll(string, string, byte\[])

[Section titled “SendToAll(string, string, byte\[\])”](#sendtoallstring-string-byte)

```csharp
public static bool SendToAll(
    string gamemodeId,
    string channel,
    byte[] payload)
```

Added in `3.0.0`

Send bytes to every other player in the current session (not to yourself). Reliable, over Steam P2P on Side Hustle’s own channel; at most `MaxMessageBytes` bytes. Returns false, with a log line, when there is no session lobby or the message is refused. Off the main thread it is queued and returns true. Since 2.5.0.

### SendToAll(string, string, string)

[Section titled “SendToAll(string, string, string)”](#sendtoallstring-string-string)

```csharp
public static bool SendToAll(string gamemodeId, string channel, string text)
```

Added in `3.0.0`

Send UTF-8 text to every other player in the current session. Same rules as the byte overload. Since 2.5.0.

### SendTo(ulong, string, string, byte\[])

[Section titled “SendTo(ulong, string, string, byte\[\])”](#sendtoulong-string-string-byte)

```csharp
public static bool SendTo(
    ulong steamId,
    string gamemodeId,
    string channel,
    byte[] payload)
```

Added in `3.0.0`

Send bytes to one player of the current session by Steam id. The target must be in the session’s lobby; sending to yourself is refused. Same rules as `SendToAll(string, string, byte[])`. Since 2.5.0.

### SendTo(ulong, string, string, string)

[Section titled “SendTo(ulong, string, string, string)”](#sendtoulong-string-string-string)

```csharp
public static bool SendTo(
    ulong steamId,
    string gamemodeId,
    string channel,
    string text)
```

Added in `3.0.0`

Send UTF-8 text to one player of the current session. Same rules as the byte overload. Since 2.5.0.

### OnMessage

[Section titled “OnMessage”](#onmessage)

```csharp
public static void OnMessage(
    string gamemodeId,
    Action<SessionMessage> handler)
```

Added in `3.0.0`

Receive the messages sent for `gamemodeId` (any channel - read `Channel`). Handlers run on the main thread. Only packets from members of the current session’s lobby are delivered; the sender id comes from Steam, never from the payload. Since 2.5.0.

### OffMessage

[Section titled “OffMessage”](#offmessage)

```csharp
public static bool OffMessage(
    string gamemodeId,
    Action<SessionMessage> handler)
```

Added in `3.0.0`

Remove a handler added with `OnMessage`. Returns true if it was registered. Since 2.5.0.

# ApiFeatures

> Feature names for `Has`.

```csharp
public static class ApiFeatures
```

Namespace `SideHustle`

Added in `3.0.0`

Feature names for `Has`. Ask for a feature instead of comparing version numbers: it says exactly what you need, and it stays true in every later release. Every name here is true on the Side Hustle that ships it. The constants are compiled into your mod, so pass them to `Has`; do not read them to learn what is running.

# SideHustle API changes

> What SideHustle added to and removed from its public API in each release.

A member listed under a version is callable from that version on. Check “Removed” and “Signature changed” before you raise the version you require: a mod built against the old signature breaks on the new one.

# GamemodeDescriptor

> Everything a gamemode mod tells Side Hustle about itself.

```csharp
public sealed class GamemodeDescriptor
```

Namespace `SideHustle`

Everything a gamemode mod tells Side Hustle about itself. Pass one of these to `Register` (usually from your mod’s OnInitializeMelon). Only `Id`, `DisplayName` and the launch callback for your `Support` mode are required; every multiplayer field is optional so a singleplayer-only mod registers minimally.

## Fields

[Section titled “Fields”](#fields)

### Id

[Section titled “Id”](#id)

```csharp
public string Id
```

Stable, unique key (e.g. “doodesch.inkubator”). Used for de-duplication and, later, lobby filtering.

### DisplayName

[Section titled “DisplayName”](#displayname)

```csharp
public string DisplayName
```

Name shown in the gamemode list.

### Description

[Section titled “Description”](#description)

```csharp
public string Description
```

Short one-line description shown under the name.

### Author

[Section titled “Author”](#author)

```csharp
public string Author
```

Author shown in the list (optional).

### Icon

[Section titled “Icon”](#icon)

```csharp
public Sprite Icon
```

Icon sprite for the list row. If null, Side Hustle builds one from `IconTex`.

### IconTex

[Section titled “IconTex”](#icontex)

```csharp
public Texture2D IconTex
```

Icon texture; Side Hustle wraps it in a Sprite when `Icon` is null.

### IconResource

[Section titled “IconResource”](#iconresource)

```csharp
public string IconResource
```

Added in `3.0.0`

Name of a PNG embedded in your mod’s assembly (the manifest resource name, e.g. “YourMod.icon.png”). Used only when `Icon` and `IconTex` are both null: the hub loads it into `IconTex` the first time it draws the row, so you need no Unity image code. A name that does not resolve is logged together with the resource names the assembly does have. Since 2.5.0.

Embed the PNG as `<AssemblyName>.hub-icon.png` (csproj: `<EmbeddedResource Include="icon.png" LogicalName="YourMod.hub-icon.png" />`) and the hub finds it without this field, and also while the boot gate holds your mod back, when none of your code has run yet.

### Support

[Section titled “Support”](#support)

```csharp
public GamemodeSupport Support
```

Which play modes this gamemode supports.

### Surface

[Section titled “Surface”](#surface)

```csharp
public GamemodeSurface Surface
```

Whether the gamemode runs as a menu overlay or needs the game world.

### DownloadUrl

[Section titled “DownloadUrl”](#downloadurl)

```csharp
public string DownloadUrl
```

Added in `2.0.0`

Where to get this mod (its Thunderstore/Nexus/GitHub page). When set, Side Hustle advertises this gamemode’s live public lobbies to players who do NOT have it installed, with a “Download Mod” button that opens this page. Null = still advertised by name (see `Advertise`) but with no download link. Only links on known mod hosts (Thunderstore, Nexus, GitHub) are opened.

### Advertise

[Section titled “Advertise”](#advertise)

```csharp
public bool Advertise
```

Added in `2.0.0`

When true (default), this gamemode’s PUBLIC lobbies are advertised in the Side Hustle menu of players who do not have it installed, so they can discover it. Set false to stay invisible to non-installers - e.g. a work-in-progress gamemode you do not want discovered during development. This only affects that discovery listing; the gamemode is always fully hostable and joinable by people who have it.

### BlockVanillaQuests

[Section titled “BlockVanillaQuests”](#blockvanillaquests)

```csharp
public bool BlockVanillaQuests
```

Added in `1.5.0`

When true, Side Hustle blocks every vanilla quest from starting for the duration of the session (a Harmony prefix on Quest.Begin). Keeps a clean slate - no tutorial/dealer quest chains, phone prompts, or NPC waypoints fighting the gamemode. Quests are host-authoritative so this matters on the host. Default false.

### AllowedQuestTitles

[Section titled “AllowedQuestTitles”](#allowedquesttitles)

```csharp
public string[] AllowedQuestTitles
```

Added in `1.5.0`

Quest titles EXEMPT from `BlockVanillaQuests` - e.g. a gamemode’s own guide quest. Their `Quest.Begin` is allowed through even while vanilla quests are blocked. Default none.

### SkipIntro

[Section titled “SkipIntro”](#skipintro)

```csharp
public bool SkipIntro
```

Added in `1.5.0`

When true, Side Hustle skips the new-game intro cutscene + character-creator (sets the player’s HasCompletedIntro before the intro gate runs), so players drop straight into the world. Default false.

### ForceNewGame

[Section titled “ForceNewGame”](#forcenewgame)

```csharp
public bool ForceNewGame
```

Added in `1.5.0`

Has no effect. Side Hustle boots a clean scratch world (clears the scratch folder and copies DefaultSave) on every World launch anyway, and never touches a real save slot. Kept so mods that set it still load. Default false.

### BlockSaveDuringSession

[Section titled “BlockSaveDuringSession”](#blocksaveduringsession)

```csharp
public bool BlockSaveDuringSession
```

Added in `1.5.0`

When true, Side Hustle blocks every vanilla save (both SaveManager.Save overloads) for the duration of the session. A gamemode runs on a throwaway scratch world and mutates transient state (teleports, locked doors, swapped appearances); persisting that to disk would corrupt the save. The Save button still appears but does nothing. Saving works normally again once the session ends. Default false.

### SuppressNpcCombatReactions

[Section titled “SuppressNpcCombatReactions”](#suppressnpccombatreactions)

```csharp
public bool SuppressNpcCombatReactions
```

Added in `1.5.0`

When true, Side Hustle stops NPCs from reacting to hunter/player GUNFIRE for the session (no panic/flee/cover, no civilian police-call, no WANTED pursuit, no bystander weapon-impact) - so a gamemode can fire weapons without derailing the NPC schedule. Purely subtractive (prefixes on NPCAwareness NoiseEvent/VisionEvent for the gunshot/discharge cases, NPC.SendImpact, and the ranged-weapon aim scan); every other NPC awareness (footsteps, deals, vandalism) is untouched. Default false.

### DisableVanillaPlayerDeath

[Section titled “DisableVanillaPlayerDeath”](#disablevanillaplayerdeath)

```csharp
public bool DisableVanillaPlayerDeath
```

Added in `1.5.0`

When true, Side Hustle cancels all vanilla PLAYER death for the session (prefix on PlayerHealth.TakeDamage + SendDie) - players cannot die to real weapon damage while the session runs. Use this when elimination is the gamemode’s own concern (e.g. a host-validated catch) and vanilla death + medical-centre respawn would eject a player from the play area. Damage to NPCs/props is untouched. Default false.

### OnLaunchSingleplayer

[Section titled “OnLaunchSingleplayer”](#onlaunchsingleplayer)

```csharp
public Action<LaunchContext> OnLaunchSingleplayer
```

Invoked to start singleplayer. Required for Singleplayer/Hybrid gamemodes.

### OnHostMultiplayer

[Section titled “OnHostMultiplayer”](#onhostmultiplayer)

```csharp
public Action<LaunchContext> OnHostMultiplayer
```

Invoked to start hosting a multiplayer session. Optional.

### OnJoinMultiplayer

[Section titled “OnJoinMultiplayer”](#onjoinmultiplayer)

```csharp
public Action<LaunchContext> OnJoinMultiplayer
```

Invoked to join a multiplayer session. Optional.

### OnExitToHub

[Section titled “OnExitToHub”](#onexittohub)

```csharp
public Action<LaunchContext> OnExitToHub
```

Invoked when Side Hustle tears the gamemode down (e.g. the player backs out). Optional.

### Policy

[Section titled “Policy”](#policy)

```csharp
public ModPolicy Policy
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Optional policy controlling which other mods may stay loaded while this gamemode runs. Null = no restriction (default). See `ModPolicy`.

### DefaultRequiredModsOnly

[Section titled “DefaultRequiredModsOnly”](#defaultrequiredmodsonly)

```csharp
public bool DefaultRequiredModsOnly
```

Added in `1.5.3`

When true, the Host form defaults the mod-set choice to “Required mods only” (an isolated profile with just this gamemode’s mods) instead of “Current installed mods” - e.g. a multiplayer gamemode that wants everyone on an identical, clean set. The host can still switch it before starting. Only takes effect when `Policy` is declared and would actually change the set (and is not blocked). Default false.

### HostSettings

[Section titled “HostSettings”](#hostsettings)

```csharp
public SettingDescriptor[] HostSettings
```

Added in `1.4.0`

Optional host-configurable settings. Side Hustle renders these as a form on the Host screen and ships the chosen values to your launch callbacks via `Multiplayer`’s config blob. Null = none. See `SettingDescriptor`.

### Presets

[Section titled “Presets”](#presets)

```csharp
public SettingPreset[] Presets
```

Added in `1.5.0`

Optional one-click presets for `HostSettings`. Side Hustle shows a picker above the form; selecting a preset cascades its values into the matching controls (the host can still tweak after). Null/empty = no picker. See `SettingPreset`.

## Properties

[Section titled “Properties”](#properties)

### AllowsSingleplayer

[Section titled “AllowsSingleplayer”](#allowssingleplayer)

```csharp
public bool AllowsSingleplayer { get; }
```

True when this descriptor can be launched in singleplayer.

### AllowsMultiplayer

[Section titled “AllowsMultiplayer”](#allowsmultiplayer)

```csharp
public bool AllowsMultiplayer { get; }
```

True when this descriptor exposes multiplayer (host/join).

# GamemodeSupport

> Which multiplayer modes a gamemode supports.

```csharp
public enum GamemodeSupport
```

Namespace `SideHustle`

Which multiplayer modes a gamemode supports. Side Hustle uses this to decide whether selecting the gamemode launches straight into singleplayer or first shows the Singleplayer / Host / Join choice.

## Fields

[Section titled “Fields”](#fields)

### Singleplayer

[Section titled “Singleplayer”](#singleplayer)

```csharp
Singleplayer
```

Singleplayer only. Selecting it launches immediately.

### Multiplayer

[Section titled “Multiplayer”](#multiplayer)

```csharp
Multiplayer
```

Multiplayer only. Selecting it shows Host / Join.

### Hybrid

[Section titled “Hybrid”](#hybrid)

```csharp
Hybrid
```

Both. Selecting it shows Singleplayer / Host / Join.

# GamemodeSurface

> Where a gamemode runs.

```csharp
public enum GamemodeSurface
```

Namespace `SideHustle`

Where a gamemode runs. `MenuSpace` gamemodes build their own overlay on top of the main menu and never load a save (e.g. the Inkubator tattoo editor). `World` gamemodes need the actual game world, so Side Hustle boots a throwaway save before handing control over.

## Fields

[Section titled “Fields”](#fields)

### MenuSpace

[Section titled “MenuSpace”](#menuspace)

```csharp
MenuSpace
```

Runs as an overlay in the menu scene; no save is loaded.

### World

[Section titled “World”](#world)

```csharp
World
```

Needs the loaded game world; Side Hustle boots a throwaway save first.

# LaunchContext

> Passed to a gamemode's launch callback.

```csharp
public sealed class LaunchContext
```

Namespace `SideHustle`

Passed to a gamemode’s launch callback. Carries who is launching (host / client / singleplayer) and, for multiplayer, the lobby id. The gamemode calls `ReturnToHub` when it is finished so Side Hustle can restore the menu.

## Properties

[Section titled “Properties”](#properties)

### Descriptor

[Section titled “Descriptor”](#descriptor)

```csharp
public GamemodeDescriptor Descriptor { get; internal set; }
```

The descriptor being launched.

### IsHost

[Section titled “IsHost”](#ishost)

```csharp
public bool? IsHost { get; internal set; }
```

true = host, false = client, null = singleplayer.

### LobbyId

[Section titled “LobbyId”](#lobbyid)

```csharp
public ulong LobbyId { get; internal set; }
```

Steam lobby id for multiplayer; 0 for singleplayer.

### IsSingleplayer

[Section titled “IsSingleplayer”](#issingleplayer)

```csharp
public bool IsSingleplayer { get; }
```

True when this is a singleplayer launch.

### Role

[Section titled “Role”](#role)

```csharp
public SessionRole Role { get; }
```

Added in `3.0.0`

Who the local player is in this session; the same information as `IsHost` as an enum. Since 2.5.0.

### PlayerCount

[Section titled “PlayerCount”](#playercount)

```csharp
public int PlayerCount { get; internal set; }
```

Added in `1.1.0`

Players currently in the lobby (1 for singleplayer).

### HostName

[Section titled “HostName”](#hostname)

```csharp
public string HostName { get; internal set; }
```

Added in `1.1.0`

The host’s display name: their session alias when they set one on the Host form, else their Steam persona. On a client it is read from the lobby (`sh_host_name`), which the host writes the same way. Null for singleplayer.

### HasPassword

[Section titled “HasPassword”](#haspassword)

```csharp
public bool HasPassword { get; internal set; }
```

Added in `1.1.0`

True if the lobby was created with a password.

### Multiplayer

[Section titled “Multiplayer”](#multiplayer)

```csharp
public Multiplayer.MultiplayerInfo Multiplayer { get; internal set; }
```

Added in `1.1.0`

The full multiplayer payload (max players, gamemode name, the host’s free-form config blob, …). Null for singleplayer. Use this to pass gamemode-specific settings from host to clients.

## Methods

[Section titled “Methods”](#methods)

### ReturnToHub

[Section titled “ReturnToHub”](#returntohub)

```csharp
public void ReturnToHub()
```

Call this from your gamemode when it is done (e.g. the player clicks “Back”). Side Hustle restores the main menu and re-shows the hub. Only the first call counts: once the session was ended - by this call or by Side Hustle aborting it - later calls are ignored and logged.

# ModPolicy

> An optional per-gamemode policy that controls which OTHER mods are active while the gamemode runs.

```csharp
public sealed class ModPolicy
```

Namespace `SideHustle`

Added in `1.2.0`

An optional per-gamemode policy that controls which OTHER mods are active while the gamemode runs. When a gamemode with a policy is launched, Side Hustle restarts the game into a temporary, isolated profile that loads ONLY the allowed mods, after a confirmation that lists exactly what changes, then continues into the gamemode; leaving the gamemode restarts back to your full mod set. Your installed mods are never renamed, moved or deleted - the profile is a throwaway sandbox - so mod managers stay in sync and a normal launch always loads everything.

Mods are matched by their MelonLoader display name OR their DLL file name (case-insensitive, “.dll” optional). You never need to list the essentials - they are always kept: MelonLoader, S1API, Side Hustle, this gamemode’s own mod, the Mod Manager & Phone App, and (for multiplayer gamemodes) the multiplayer libraries. Mods that a kept mod depends on are kept too.

## Fields

[Section titled “Fields”](#fields)

### AllowedMods

[Section titled “AllowedMods”](#allowedmods)

```csharp
public string[] AllowedMods
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Extra mods that are allowed to remain loaded alongside this gamemode. Everything loaded that is neither allowed, required, nor an essential (or a dependency of a kept mod) gets disabled.

### RequiredMods

[Section titled “RequiredMods”](#requiredmods)

```csharp
public string[] RequiredMods
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Mods this gamemode needs. If present but disabled they are enabled; if a required mod is not installed at all the player is told to install it first. Required mods are implicitly allowed.

# MultiplayerInfo

> The multiplayer payload carried on `Multiplayer`.

```csharp
public sealed class MultiplayerInfo
```

Namespace `SideHustle.Multiplayer`

Added in `1.1.0`

The multiplayer payload carried on `Multiplayer`. Populated by Side Hustle from the Steam lobby’s namespaced metadata (the `sh_*` keys). The host fills it from its host options; a joining client reads it back from the lobby. `ConfigBlob` is a free-form string the host writes (lobby key `sh_config`) so a gamemode can ship its own settings to clients with no extra netcode.

# SettingDescriptor

> One host-configurable setting a gamemode exposes.

```csharp
public sealed class SettingDescriptor
```

Namespace `SideHustle`

Added in `1.4.0`

One host-configurable setting a gamemode exposes. Side Hustle renders these as a form on the Host screen, then ships the chosen values to the gamemode (host and clients) via the launch context’s config blob - see `HostSettings` and `MultiplayerInfo`’s getters.

Every value is stored as a string under `Key`. Keep keys short (the whole blob rides on Steam lobby metadata) and stable (they are the wire format your gamemode reads back).

Optional one-line help shown under the label.

Optional category name. The host form renders a section header whenever the category changes between consecutive settings, so order settings by category. Null/empty = no header for that setting.

The control to render.

# SettingPreset

> A named bundle of host-setting values a gamemode can offer as a one-click preset (e.g.

```csharp
public sealed class SettingPreset
```

Namespace `SideHustle`

Added in `1.5.0`

A named bundle of host-setting values a gamemode can offer as a one-click preset (e.g. “Classic Hunt”). Side Hustle shows a preset picker above the settings form; selecting one CASCADES its `Values` into the matching controls (matched by `Key`), which the host can then still tweak. Values use the same wire format as the controls: a Slider’s number, a Toggle’s “1”/“0”, a Segmented’s stored value. Keys with no matching control are ignored (forward-compatible with not-yet-built settings).

## Fields

[Section titled “Fields”](#fields)

### Name

[Section titled “Name”](#name)

```csharp
public string Name
```

Added in `1.5.0`

Display name shown in the picker (e.g. “Classic Hunt”). Required.

### Hint

[Section titled “Hint”](#hint)

```csharp
public string Hint
```

Added in `1.5.0`

Optional one-line description shown under the picker while this preset is selected.

### Values

[Section titled “Values”](#values)

```csharp
public System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary<string, string> Values
```

Added in `1.5.0`

The setting values this preset applies, keyed by `Key`.

### Experimental

[Section titled “Experimental”](#experimental)

```csharp
public bool Experimental
```

Added in `1.5.0`

When true the picker marks this preset as experimental (a badge + sorted to the back) - use it for presets whose headline mechanic is not fully built yet.

### Recommended

[Section titled “Recommended”](#recommended)

```csharp
public string Recommended
```

Added in `1.5.0`

Optional human-readable player-count recommendation shown in the picker (e.g. “Best for 2-6”).

### MinPlayers

[Section titled “MinPlayers”](#minplayers)

```csharp
public int MinPlayers
```

Added in `1.5.0`

Player-count range this preset suits best. When the lobby size falls in \[`MinPlayers`, `MaxPlayers`] the form may auto-select it on open. 0 = unspecified.

### MaxPlayers

[Section titled “MaxPlayers”](#maxplayers)

```csharp
public int MaxPlayers
```

Added in `1.5.0`

### Mode

[Section titled “Mode”](#mode)

```csharp
public string Mode
```

Added in `1.5.0`

Canonical “mode” this preset represents (e.g. “Infection”). When the host tweaks a preset, the effective mode shown to joiners becomes “Custom - {Mode}”. Defaults to `Name` when null.

### DefaultSelected

[Section titled “DefaultSelected”](#defaultselected)

```csharp
public bool DefaultSelected
```

Added in `1.5.0`

When true the form opens on this preset, overriding the player-count best-fit. Used for a saved “Custom” preset that should be pre-selected next time the host opens the form.

# WorldHygiene

> Ready-made sets of the world hygiene flags on `GamemodeDescriptor`, so a World gamemode does not have to know which five booleans belong together.

```csharp
public static class WorldHygiene
```

Namespace `SideHustle`

Added in `3.0.0`

Ready-made sets of the world hygiene flags on `GamemodeDescriptor`, so a World gamemode does not have to know which five booleans belong together. Each method sets the flags on the descriptor you pass and returns it, and only ever switches flags ON: anything you set yourself stays set. Since 2.5.0.

## Methods

[Section titled “Methods”](#methods)

### CleanWorld

[Section titled “CleanWorld”](#cleanworld)

```csharp
public static GamemodeDescriptor CleanWorld(
    GamemodeDescriptor descriptor,
    params string[] allowedQuestTitles)
```

Added in `3.0.0`

A clean scratch world: vanilla quests blocked (except `allowedQuestTitles`), the intro skipped and saving blocked for the session. Fits most World gamemodes.

### Arena

[Section titled “Arena”](#arena)

```csharp
public static GamemodeDescriptor Arena(
    GamemodeDescriptor descriptor,
    params string[] allowedQuestTitles)
```

Added in `3.0.0`

`CleanWorld` plus no NPC reactions to gunfire and no vanilla player death - for a gamemode whose players shoot and whose eliminations are its own (the set PropHunt uses).

# SideHustle changelog

> Every released version of SideHustle and what changed in it.

All notable changes to Side Hustle are documented here. This project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).

## \[3.0.0] - 2026-10-16

[Section titled “\[3.0.0\] - 2026-10-16”](#300---2026-10-16)

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added)

* A new hub beside the vanilla menu: last gamemode, public co-op, every gamemode with its actions, one lobby board, hosting inline, Settings and a catalogue of released gamemodes.
* Every launch shows a live status with Cancel. A failed start names the reason instead of “Session ended”.
* Lobby board: search, filters, sort and auto refresh. The last results show at once when you open it.
* Mod syncs can be cancelled and show progress per mod, with one restart overlay instead of two.
* Profiles get a Switch button on every row.

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed)

* One click starts a gamemode you last played solo, and after a session the hub opens on it for a rematch. Right-click a row for its lobbies.
* Host again opens your last lobby without the form and keeps your mod mode, also for a vanilla co-op save. Host with defaults skips the form too.
* The host form remembers players, visibility, lobby name, Discord invite and mod mode per gamemode.
* Needs Sideload 1.33.1 or newer. A mod manager pulls it in.
* Joining skips the consent screen and the install checklist when there is nothing to decide. A gamemode you do not have opens its lobbies with Download.

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed)

* Gamemodes the mod gate holds back show their own icon when the mod ships one.

### For mod authors

[Section titled “For mod authors”](#for-mod-authors)

* Session events: `SessionStarted`, `SessionEnded`, `PlayerJoined`, `PlayerLeft`, plus `CurrentSession` and `Players` with roles.
* `SendToAll`, `SendTo` and `OnMessage` carry your own messages between players, up to `MaxMessageBytes`.
* `ShowNotice` puts a short line on screen.
* `Register` checks your descriptor and logs what is wrong. `ApiVersion` and `Has(feature)` tell you what this Side Hustle offers.
* `Examples/` holds a working gamemode and the `SideHustleLink` shim for a soft dependency.

## \[2.4.2] - 2026-08-13

[Section titled “\[2.4.2\] - 2026-08-13”](#242---2026-08-13)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-1)

* Side Hustle loads again after 2.4.1, which quietly needed a newer S1API than it asked for and broke the lobby list on installs that had not updated.
* The package asks for S1API 3.1.15 now, so a mod manager pulls a version that matches.

## \[2.4.1] - 2026-08-13

[Section titled “\[2.4.1\] - 2026-08-13”](#241---2026-08-13)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-2)

* Non-friends can join your hosted lobby again. Since game version 0.4.6f12 every lobby stayed friends-only and joiners got “Authentication failed”.
* The fix sits with the host, so joining a public lobby needs its host on 2.4.1 or later.

## \[2.4.0] - 2026-08-08

[Section titled “\[2.4.0\] - 2026-08-08”](#240---2026-08-08)

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-1)

* Your mods can wait for a lobby instead of loading at startup, so joining somebody’s session stops meaning quit first. Switch it on with `DeferModsUntilLobby`.
  * `AlwaysLoadMods` names what has to be there before a lobby exists: a bridge, an overlay, a profiler.
* Joining a synced lobby skips the restart. The host’s mods load out of the package cache while you stay on the screen you were on.
  * A mod already running at a different version than the session wants still costs one. The log names the mod and both versions.
* The gamemode list shows installed gamemodes that have not loaded yet, with the name, version and author their own file declares. One click loads and starts it.

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-1)

* The Lobby app’s icon on your phone is white instead of teal.

## \[2.3.1] - 2026-08-08

[Section titled “\[2.3.1\] - 2026-08-08”](#231---2026-08-08)

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-2)

* The Lobby app offers “Publish again” when your mod list is not on the lobby. Nobody can join until it is.

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-3)

* Other players can join your session again. A large synced mod list left no room on the lobby for the checksum joiners check it against, so every sync failed.
* The mod requirement switches back on after you switch it off. It re-publishes the list instead of refusing with “nothing to check”.
* Holding the seats stepper stops lagging. The number moves at once and Steam hears about it once, 0.4s after your last click.
* A rename Steam refuses keeps what you typed and says so. The field used to come back empty.
* The Publish row says your session is already listed instead of offering a button that answers “could not”.

## \[2.3.0] - 2026-08-08

[Section titled “\[2.3.0\] - 2026-08-08”](#230---2026-08-08)

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-3)

* The main menu shows a column on the right: sessions listed, how many take players, the mod profile you booted into, and whether anyone messaged you. Switch it off with `MenuStatePanel`.
* A Lobby app on your phone changes what used to need a new session: name, join password, public or friends only, seats, mod requirement, publishing. Host only, and it applies to the next person who joins.
* Lobby cards get a Chat button next to Join, and the join screens carry that conversation down the right, so a mod you cannot download becomes a question instead of a dead end.
  * It only shows for hosts who take messages. Switch yours off with `AcceptStrangerMessages`, mute one person from the app, or hide the column with `JoinChatPanel`.
* Lobby cards say which branch the host plays on, IL2CPP in green or Mono in red. The two cannot play together, and nothing on the card used to tell you before you tried.
* The Rejoining screen gets a Cancel button after eight seconds. It leaves the host’s lobby so you stop holding a seat, and your synced mods stay set up.

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-4)

* Joining a lobby published from the pause menu works. It was never marked ready for players, so you installed the host’s mods, restarted, and landed on your own main menu.
* A join that cannot work stops early: lobbies taking no players are marked in the browser, and a join that never starts gives up after 15 seconds with the reason on screen.
* The manual install list says in one short line why a mod cannot be downloaded. A mod the host built themselves looked exactly like one still on its way.
* Backing out of a lobby you were checking leaves it behind. Its mod list kept loading and threw that lobby’s sync screen over whatever you picked next, seconds later.
* The Publish button stays out of gamemode rounds. Pressing it while hosting one rewrote the round’s own lobby details, and unpublishing then made the lobby impossible to join.

## \[2.2.9] - 2026-08-07

[Section titled “\[2.2.9\] - 2026-08-07”](#229---2026-08-07)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-5)

* The log stays readable. Opening the gamemode list wrote the same “hid 10 save-slot controls” line thirty times in a third of a second, and the lobby poll repeated “advertised lobbies: 0 found” every few seconds. Both now write one line when something actually changes.

## \[2.2.8] - 2026-08-07

[Section titled “\[2.2.8\] - 2026-08-07”](#228---2026-08-07)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-6)

* Removing a mod from a profile now takes its libraries with it. Taking Hash out removed Sideload too, correctly, and then put Sideload’s Jint, AngleSharp and Esprima back from your global UserLibs folder - the mod was gone and its libraries stayed. A library follows the package that brought it, and anything that came from outside a package is still left alone.

## \[2.2.7] - 2026-08-07

[Section titled “\[2.2.7\] - 2026-08-07”](#227---2026-08-07)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-7)

* Joining after the mod-sync restart works even when your MelonPreferences.cfg has a broken line in it. One bad line anywhere in that file, from any mod, made the game forget which lobby it was going back to - so it restarted and left you in the menu. The lobby is now remembered next to the profile instead, and the log says when your config could not be read.

## \[2.2.6] - 2026-08-06

[Section titled “\[2.2.6\] - 2026-08-06”](#226---2026-08-06)

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-2)

* The preset picker in a host form says where its values come from. On your saved settings it reads “your last settings are loaded”, on a named preset “fills in every setting below”. It used to ask “new host? pick one, then Start”, which explained neither the arrows next to it nor that moving off a preset rewrites every row underneath.

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-8)

* A setting whose description runs past two lines shows its name again. In PropHunt’s host form the play-area radius, the auto-start toggle and the sewer goblin toggle appeared as a description with no title, because the row was pinned to one height and the wrapped text pushed the name out of it.

## \[2.2.5] - 2026-08-06

[Section titled “\[2.2.5\] - 2026-08-06”](#225---2026-08-06)

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-4)

* The wait while mods download now shows what it is doing: every mod the host runs is listed, and the bar moves one step per mod that finished and passed its hash check.
* A notice tells you the game is about to restart, on both routes - joining a gamemode you do not own, and matching a host’s mods. The finished mod list stays readable behind it.
* After the restart the screen says it is rejoining and shows how long it has been looking for the lobby, instead of an idle main menu while nothing appears to happen.
* A mod that could not be fetched is named on screen with the reason, so you can tell whether to try again or install it by hand.

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-9)

* The bar no longer sits at zero when every mod is already in the cache, and the game no longer closes itself with nothing on screen.
* Matching a host’s mods restarted with no message at all. Only the gamemode route ever showed one, which is why the notice looked like it appeared at random.

## \[2.2.4] - 2026-08-06

[Section titled “\[2.2.4\] - 2026-08-06”](#224---2026-08-06)

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-5)

* Joining a session checks your mods against the host’s first. If the sets differ you get the list and the choice: match the host and restart, or join as you are. Before, you joined with everything you had loaded, and a mod the host never allowed could break the round for everybody.

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-3)

* Public lobbies keep working on the Schedule I 0.4.6f12 beta. That update moves the “must be friends with the host” rule into the connection handshake, so the old bypass no longer reaches it; Side Hustle now asks the game for the open mode it already has instead. Nothing changes on 0.4.6f11.

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-10)

* A session that ends badly tells you why at the main menu instead of dropping you there in silence. The message survives the restart that some of those failures need.
* Being sent back to the menu also leaves the lobby. You could end up in the menu while Steam still had you seated in a session you were no longer in.
* The `Export` and `Import` buttons are gone from the gamemode and session lists. They belong to the game’s save slots, which those lists are built from.
* Hosting a gamemode that needs a restart says so on screen while it happens, instead of the game appearing to close itself.
* The lobby browser stops showing games nobody can join. A lobby published with the in-game Publish button stayed on the website for as long as the game was open, frozen at one player, because leaving to the menu never withdrew it.
* Quitting the game takes your lobby off the site right away instead of leaving it there for another minute and a half.
* A lobby that vanished from the site while you were still hosting it comes back on its own. Restarting the backend used to drop every listing, and only re-hosting put yours back.

## \[2.2.3] - 2026-08-03

[Section titled “\[2.2.3\] - 2026-08-03”](#223---2026-08-03)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-11)

* Lobbies with more than five players work. The extra seats were always there to take, but the fifth client and everyone after them just never arrived, stuck on “Loading world…” with nothing happening.
* A join that fails now drops you back at the main menu. Previously the loading screen stayed up with no way out and you had to kill the game.
* The lobby seat comes free again when a join is abandoned, instead of staying blocked by someone who never got in.
* Slower machines get the time they need. The cut-off used to be a flat 95 seconds, which killed loads that were healthy and merely slow - the reason weaker PCs hit this so much more often.

## \[2.2.2] - 2026-08-01

[Section titled “\[2.2.2\] - 2026-08-01”](#222---2026-08-01)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-12)

* Clicking a save in the main menu loads it again. Since Schedule I 0.4.6f11 it did nothing at all: no load, no prompt, no error. The “Host this save publicly?” prompt had cancelled the load and was then drawn behind the menu, so there was nothing left to click.
* If that prompt ever fails to appear again, the save just loads. It no longer leaves you on a menu that ignores you.

## \[2.2.1] - 2026-08-01

[Section titled “\[2.2.1\] - 2026-08-01”](#221---2026-08-01)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-13)

* The log no longer fills with “Steamworks is not initialized” while you sit in the menu without Steam. The browser checks first and says once that it stays empty until Steam is up. 0.4.6f11 made playing without Steam a normal state, and the browser was still asking it for lobbies every 15 seconds.

## \[2.2.0] - 2026-08-01

[Section titled “\[2.2.0\] - 2026-08-01”](#220---2026-08-01)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-14)

* Side Hustle works on Schedule I 0.4.6f11. That update renamed the main menu screen and replaced the game’s Steam lobby layer, so 2.1.3 has no menu entry there and no working multiplayer.
* Your hosted lobby shows up in the server browser again, with the mod list joiners check theirs against. The lobby’s Steam id moved in 0.4.6; the old spot still exists and always answers zero, and the browser entry, the website listing and the mod sync all key off that id.
* Players who are not on your Steam friends list can join your public lobby again. Vanilla drops them with “Not friends with host” a few seconds after they connect; Side Hustle switches that off while it hosts, and the switch moved in 0.4.6.
* A new lobby opens with every seat a cap mod gives it, FullHouse or BiggerLobbies, instead of the vanilla four.
* The invite button is back for everyone in the lobby, not the host alone, and the display name you set for a session reaches the other players again.

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-4)

* Side Hustle needs S1API 3.1.1. 3.0.5 predates the game update; a mod manager pulls the new one in for you.

## \[2.1.3] - 2026-07-28

[Section titled “\[2.1.3\] - 2026-07-28”](#213---2026-07-28)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-15)

* Joining a lobby whose mod list was too big for Steam said “Sync unavailable” and could never do anything else. A host in that position clears the chunk count so joiners fall back to the backend copy - but it also cleared the hash, and the hash is the only thing a joiner can verify that copy against, so the copy was refused. The fallback was dead in exactly the case it exists for. The hash is sixteen characters and fits when the manifest does not, so it is published either way now. Hosts need this version; joiners see the difference as soon as the host has it.
* Mod names written in CamelCase are split before searching Nexus. “BigPimpin” found nothing there while “Big Pimpin” finds the mod, and a spaced query already matches a run-together title, so this only ever helps. Acronyms stay whole: “SIAKImperium” becomes “SIAK Imperium”. The website’s lobby pages do the same.

## \[2.1.2] - 2026-07-28

[Section titled “\[2.1.2\] - 2026-07-28”](#212---2026-07-28)

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-5)

* The Thunderstore build now downloads nothing at all. 2.1.1 stopped it fetching from GitHub and was rejected again, so this build also stops it downloading packages from Thunderstore itself. What that costs on Thunderstore, and only there: mod sync never installs anything on its own, every mod lands on the checklist with a direct link, and the “Add from Thunderstore” browser is gone from Mod Profiles - a browser that lists the whole community index and then cannot install is worse than no button, so the profile screen says to use a mod manager instead. Profiles built from mods you already have work unchanged.
* The package index and mod icons are still fetched. They are a JSON catalogue and PNGs, not executable code.
* The builds on GitHub and Nexus are unaffected and keep every download.

## \[2.1.1] - 2026-07-27

[Section titled “\[2.1.1\] - 2026-07-27”](#211---2026-07-27)

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-6)

* The Thunderstore build no longer downloads mods from GitHub releases. Thunderstore does not allow a package to fetch executable code from outside Thunderstore, which is a fair rule and one this mod’s sync was breaking, so the build published there is compiled without that fetch: no endpoint, no release reader, no archive scanner in the DLL at all. Mods hosted on GitHub take the same route Nexus mods already take - a checklist with a direct link, you download it, Side Hustle picks it up from your Downloads folder and verifies the hash. Thunderstore’s own packages still download automatically.
* Nothing changes for the builds on GitHub and Nexus; those keep the automatic GitHub download.

## \[2.1.0] - 2026-07-27

[Section titled “\[2.1.0\] - 2026-07-27”](#210---2026-07-27)

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-7)

* The messenger left home. Side Hustle carried its own phone app for lobby chat; that app is now [WhatsDab](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-WhatsDab) - a mod of its own, and a requirement of this one, so a mod manager installs it for you and nothing about the feature disappears. It got better on the way out: both phone orientations, a typing indicator, right-click to step back the way the vanilla apps do, and an interface written as three web files instead of 780 lines of panel code. Side Hustle is a gamemode hub again, and the chat is maintained where it belongs.

### Removed

[Section titled “Removed”](#removed)

* 1270 lines of chat code (transport, store, contacts, two screens and a notifier) and the embedded app icon. Nothing else in Side Hustle used them.

## \[2.0.1] - 2026-07-26

[Section titled “\[2.0.1\] - 2026-07-26”](#201---2026-07-26)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-16)

* Downloads that land in their own folder are picked up now. If your browser saves a mod to `Downloads\SomeMod\SomeMod.dll`, the checklist finds it there too, not just directly in Downloads.
* A mod that could not be downloaded now says why. A checklist row that appears after the consent screen promised an automatic install tells you what happened: Thunderstore refused the file, or the host runs a different build than the one on Thunderstore (same version number, different file - ask them for theirs).
* A hiccup on Thunderstore’s side no longer sends a mod to the checklist. A 5xx answer is retried once before giving up, which is what a “502” during a join used to cost you.

## \[2.0.0] - 2026-07-26

[Section titled “\[2.0.0\] - 2026-07-26”](#200---2026-07-26)

Play modded multiplayer with anyone - mods sync themselves, join a gamemode you don’t even have installed, and chat in-game.

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-6)

* **Join a gamemode you don’t have installed.** A public gamemode lobby now advertises the exact mod files a joiner needs (the gamemode’s own mod, whatever its policy requires, with version and hash). In the Side Hustle menu such a lobby is no longer a dead “not installed” entry: pick “Join (installs the mods)”, confirm, and Side Hustle fetches them from Thunderstore - anything it can’t fetch gets the same checklist with a direct Nexus link - installs them into a session profile, restarts and drops you into that lobby. Your own mods stay exactly where they are.
* **Mod Profiles - an in-game mod manager.** A new “Mod Profiles” entry on the main menu lets you keep separate, isolated sets of mods and switch between them (the game restarts into the one you pick). Build a profile from your installed mods, or browse and install straight from Thunderstore - dependencies included. Your real Mods folder is never touched, so external managers like r2modman keep working exactly as before. Side Hustle picks which profile to load at startup (a short prompt you can skip); pick “Full mod set” any time to go back to everything.
* **Vanilla Co-op with mod sync.** Host your own normal savegame as a public lobby (from the menu, or when you click Continue), and anyone can find it and join. When they do, Side Hustle compares their mods to yours and, if they differ, offers to set up a matching profile automatically - download from Thunderstore, restart, and drop straight back into your game. Mods that can’t be fetched automatically get a simple checklist with a download link and an “open folder” button. You choose per-session whether to require synced mods.
* **Sync your mod settings too (optional).** As a host you can pick which mods’ settings to apply to everyone who joins - it only affects the session, never their real settings, and anything that looks like a secret is left off by default.
* **Side Hustle Messenger.** A new phone app for chatting with the other players in your lobby - a shared lobby chat and private one-to-one conversations, with unread badges and native message notifications.
* **GitHub mods download themselves too.** Mods whose download link points at a GitHub repository are fetched automatically from the repo’s releases (hash-verified against the host’s exact file), so fewer mods end up on the manual checklist.
* **Hands-free manual installs.** For mods that still need a browser download (e.g. Nexus), the checklist now watches your Downloads folder (and Vortex’s download folder, if you use Vortex): click the link, download the file, done - Side Hustle spots it, verifies it and installs it on its own. An “Open next link” button walks you through the list, each mod ticks off live with a toast, and if you grab the wrong version the row tells you exactly which one the host runs. Files with the right content are also reused across rejoins.
* **See what’s being played right now.** The Side Hustle menu now also lists gamemodes you do NOT have installed that have live public lobbies, so you can discover new things to play. Opening one shows a “Download Mod” button (Host and Join stay greyed out until you install the mod). You can turn this off under “Show gamemodes you don’t have” in the settings.
* **For gamemode authors:** a gamemode can declare a `DownloadUrl` (shown as the “Download Mod” link, opened in the Steam overlay) and set `Advertise = false` to keep its public lobbies out of that discovery list - e.g. while a mode is still in development. Advertising is on by default and only ever lists public lobbies.

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-8)

* **Manual downloads land on the mod’s own Nexus page.** For a mod the host could not give a download link for, Side Hustle now looks the name up on Nexus: when it identifies exactly one published Schedule I mod, the checklist button opens that mod’s page directly (“Open Nexus”) instead of a search results list. Ambiguous names (“Mod Manager”) and mods that aren’t on Nexus still open the search, exactly as before. The same lookup gives a gamemode you don’t have installed a working “Find it on Nexus” button when its host advertised no link.

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-17)

* **Gamemode sessions show up on the public lobby list.** A hosted gamemode lobby now also lists itself on the Side Hustle website (public lobbies only - a friends-only session stays off it), with its gamemode, player count and what mods a joiner would need. Only vanilla co-op lobbies did that before.
* **Your lobby name survives the “Required mods only” restart.** Hosting a gamemode that curates its mod set restarts the game first, and the name (and the chosen preset label) you typed on the host form was dropped in the process - the lobby then showed up as just your player name, in the browser and on the website.
* **Synced mods no longer arrive without their shared libraries.** A mod whose Thunderstore package ships (or depends on) a shared library - PropHunt needs SteamNetworkLib, for example - was installed as a lone DLL, so the joiner ended up with a mod that could not load and an error every frame. The sync now fetches those library packages too and puts them into the session profile’s own `Plugins`/`UserLibs`, seeded from your global ones, so your real install is still never written to.

### Notes

[Section titled “Notes”](#notes)

* Side Hustle now ships a small startup helper (`SideHustle.Boot`) that it installs into your `Plugins` folder on first run. To fully remove Side Hustle, delete that file and the `SideHustle_Profiles` folder alongside the game.
* Downloads only ever come from Thunderstore’s official CDN or a mod’s own GitHub releases, and every downloaded file is verified against the host’s manifest hash before it is used. Mods are never sent between players directly.
* Side Hustle only ever reads your Downloads and Vortex folders - nothing there is moved or deleted.

## \[1.7.0] - 2026-07-10

[Section titled “\[1.7.0\] - 2026-07-10”](#170---2026-07-10)

Set a custom display name for multiplayer sessions.

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-7)

* **Custom display name (privacy).** Each gamemode has its own “Your name” field on its Host / Join screen. Fill it in before opening or joining a lobby and other players see that name - the in-game nametag over your character, scoreboards, and the server browser - instead of your Steam name. Leave it empty to use your Steam name. Per gamemode, per session, and never saved.

## \[1.6.0] - 2026-07-09

[Section titled “\[1.6.0\] - 2026-07-09”](#160---2026-07-09)

Native bigger lobbies - Side Hustle now raises the co-op player cap on its own.

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-8)

* **Bigger co-op lobbies, built in.** Side Hustle now seats far more than the vanilla 4 players by itself (default up to 32), and the host player-count slider opens up to match. No separate lobby mod required.

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-9)

* Larger lobbies no longer rely on the external BiggerLobbies mod. If you still run BiggerLobbies, the two cooperate and the higher cap wins.

## \[1.5.3] - 2026-07-08

[Section titled “\[1.5.3\] - 2026-07-08”](#153---2026-07-08)

A multiplayer-focused update - public lobbies work with anyone, plus host controls, friend invites and smoother mod-set switching.

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-9)

* **Play with anyone, not just friends.** Schedule I normally kicks a joining player who isn’t on the host’s Steam friends list a few seconds after they connect - so public sessions were effectively friends-only. While you host a Side Hustle gamemode that kick is lifted, so friends and non-friends alike can join your public (or password-protected) lobbies. Normal co-op outside Side Hustle is unaffected.
* **Kick players.** The host can remove a player from the session from the gamemode’s UI (a reusable framework control, so any gamemode can offer it).
* **Clients can invite friends too.** The Steam friend-invite (+) button in the pause-menu lobby panel now shows for everyone in the lobby, not just the host, and works past four seats (with BiggerLobbies).
* **A heads-up before a “Required mods only” host restarts the game.** Instead of restarting instantly, a short countdown appears (Restart now / Cancel) and restarts on its own when the timer runs out - so the restart is never a surprise.
* **Gamemodes can default to “Required mods only”.** A gamemode can ask the Host form to pre-select the isolated “required mods only” set (the host can still switch it), so a mode that wants everyone on an identical set gets it by default.

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-18)

* **“Required mods only” re-hosting is now solid.** Hosting a gamemode with only its required mods, returning to the menu, then hosting again now works reliably: each launch builds a fresh isolated profile (a locked leftover can never block it), the gamemode list comes back on its own, and a quick re-host no longer times out.

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-10)

* **Better connection routing for public lobbies.** Public P2P connections now allow all connection routes and warm up Steam’s relay, so a join picks the best available path instead of falling back to relay-only.

## \[1.5.0] - 2026-07-03

[Section titled “\[1.5.0\] - 2026-07-03”](#150---2026-07-03)

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-10)

* **Gamemode presets.** Gamemodes can now ship named presets (like “Classic Hunt”) that show up as a picker at the top of the host setup form. Pick one and it fills in all the settings for you - you can still tweak anything afterwards. The form auto-selects whichever preset best fits your lobby size, a preset can suggest a player count, and one whose headline mechanic isn’t finished yet is flagged EXPERIMENTAL so you know what you’re getting.
* **Name your lobby.** The host form has a lobby name field now, and that name (plus the mode you picked) shows on the server-browser cards, so joiners can tell sessions apart at a glance.
* **Session-hygiene flags for gamemode authors.** A gamemode can opt into a handful of world-cleanup switches instead of reinventing them: skip the new-game intro and character creator, stop vanilla quests from auto-starting (with an allow-list for your own guide quest), block saving for the session so a throwaway world never overwrites a real save, keep NPCs from reacting to gunfire, and turn off vanilla player death when the gamemode runs its own elimination. All opt-in, all off by default.
* **A heads-up when versions don’t match.** When you join a session, Side Hustle compares your build of the gamemode against the host’s and warns you - in the log and right on the browser card - if they differ. It’s the classic “we’re all on different versions” bug, now easy to spot. It only warns; it never stops you joining.

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-11)

* **Host form polish.** Settings can be grouped under section headers, there’s a new compact dropdown for one-of-many choices, and the settings list scrolls with a smooth mouse-wheel glide.

## \[1.4.0] - 2026-06-26

[Section titled “\[1.4.0\] - 2026-06-26”](#140---2026-06-26)

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-11)

* **Host configuration screen.** Hosting a multiplayer gamemode now opens a native-style setup form: pick the exact player count (up to the lobby cap), a public or private (friends-only) lobby with an optional password, and any settings the gamemode itself exposes - sliders, toggles, choices and text fields - all handed to the gamemode at launch.
* **Restyled server browser.** The Join screen lists open lobbies as cards (host, player count, gamemode, and a lock for password-protected lobbies); a locked lobby asks for the password before joining.

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-12)

* **The mod policy is now a per-session choice on the host form.** When you host a gamemode that declares which other mods it works with, the setup form offers “Current installed mods” (the default - keep your full set) or “Required mods only” (run just the gamemode’s mods in an isolated profile, after a confirmation listing the changes). Nothing in your real Mods folder is ever renamed, moved or deleted (junctions/hardlinks, no admin needed), so your mod manager stays in sync. Joining a session never changes your mods - that is the host’s choice.

## \[1.3.0] - 2026-06-26

[Section titled “\[1.3.0\] - 2026-06-26”](#130---2026-06-26)

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-13)

* **Conflict-free mod sets are now fully non-destructive.** When a gamemode declares which other mods it works with, Side Hustle launches it in a temporary, isolated profile that loads only those mods - your installed mods are never disabled, renamed, moved or deleted, so your mod manager stays in sync and a normal launch always loads everything. Leaving the gamemode restarts back to your full set. The confirmation still lists exactly what changes before anything happens, and a “Restore my mods” entry returns you to your full set at any time.

## \[1.2.0] - 2026-06-25

[Section titled “\[1.2.0\] - 2026-06-25”](#120---2026-06-25)

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-12)

* **Conflict-free mod sets.** A gamemode can declare which other mods it works with (a mod policy). When you launch it, Side Hustle shows exactly which mods it will pause and enable, then - on your confirmation - launches the gamemode in its own mod set. When you leave the gamemode your normal mods are restored. A “Restore my mods” entry is there if you ever need to put everything back yourself.

## \[1.1.0] - 2026-06-25

[Section titled “\[1.1.0\] - 2026-06-25”](#110---2026-06-25)

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-13)

* **Multiplayer launch.** Multiplayer and hybrid gamemodes now show a Singleplayer / Host / Join choice in the menu. Hosting opens a public lobby (with a player-count picker); bigger lobbies are supported with BiggerLobbies.
* **Public server browser.** Browse and join open sessions for a gamemode, filtered so each gamemode only lists its own lobbies.
* **World gamemodes.** Gamemodes that need the actual game world get a throwaway session booted for them, outside your five save slots - your real saves are never created or touched.
* **Richer launch context.** Gamemodes receive the host/client role, lobby id, player count, host name and the host’s settings when they launch.
* Play-mode badge (Singleplayer / Multiplayer / SP + MP) on each gamemode in the list, optional per-gamemode icons, and a recently-played ordering so your last gamemodes appear first.

## \[1.0.1] - 2026-06-24

[Section titled “\[1.0.1\] - 2026-06-24”](#101---2026-06-24)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-19)

* The “Side Hustle” menu entry could be added more than once (showing duplicate entries) when the main menu re-initialised during loading. Injection is now idempotent, so exactly one entry appears.

## \[1.0.0] - 2026-06-24

[Section titled “\[1.0.0\] - 2026-06-24”](#100---2026-06-24)

Initial release.

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-14)

* A “Side Hustle” entry on the main menu that lists every installed gamemode mod (name, description, author) and launches the selected one without loading a savegame.
* Public, load-order-independent registration API (`SideHustle.API.Register` with `GamemodeDescriptor` / `LaunchContext`) for mods to appear as gamemodes.
* Singleplayer launch flow with a clean return to the menu (`LaunchContext.ReturnToHub`).
* Multiplayer host/join and a server browser are shown but disabled, ready for a later update.
* `Enabled` setting (MelonPreferences) to hide the menu entry without uninstalling.

# Add a gamemode

> Register your mod as a gamemode so it shows in the Side Hustle hub with its own Host, Join and Solo buttons.

Register your mod as a gamemode. It then shows as a row in the Side Hustle hub, and the player starts it from there.

**You need:** Side Hustle 3.0, a MelonLoader mod project.

## Steps

[Section titled “Steps”](#steps)

1. Reference `SideHustle.dll` from your game’s `Mods` folder. Do not copy it into your output.

   ```xml
   <Reference Include="SideHustle">
     <HintPath>path\to\Schedule I\Mods\SideHustle.dll</HintPath>
     <Private>false</Private>
   </Reference>
   ```

   Your project also needs `UnityEngine.CoreModule`, because the descriptor has `Sprite` and `Texture2D` fields.

2. Copy [`SideHustleLink.cs`](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-SideHustle/blob/main/Examples/SideHustleLink.cs) into your project. It keeps your mod working when Side Hustle is not installed.

3. Mark Side Hustle as an optional dependency, once in any file:

   ```csharp
   [assembly: MelonOptionalDependencies("SideHustle")]
   ```

4. Put every Side Hustle type in its own class. Your `MelonMod` class must not mention one.

   ```csharp
   using SideHustle;


   internal static class Gamemode
   {
       internal static GamemodeDescriptor Build() => new GamemodeDescriptor
       {
           Id = "you.yourmode",                     // stable and unique
           DisplayName = "Your Mode",
           Description = "What your gamemode does.",
           Author = "You",
           Support = GamemodeSupport.Singleplayer,  // or Multiplayer, Hybrid
           Surface = GamemodeSurface.MenuSpace,     // MenuSpace = overlay on the menu, World = loads a world
           OnLaunchSingleplayer = Start,
           OnExitToHub = ctx => CleanUp(),
       };


       private static void Start(LaunchContext ctx) { /* build your overlay or start your mode */ }
       private static void CleanUp() { /* remove everything you built */ }
   }
   ```

   A method that names a Side Hustle type fails before its first line when `SideHustle.dll` is missing. A `try`/`catch` inside that method does not help.

5. Register from `OnInitializeMelon`:

   ```csharp
   public override void OnInitializeMelon()
   {
       SideHustleLink.TryRegister(() => Gamemode.Build(), LoggerInstance);
   }
   ```

6. Call `ctx.ReturnToHub()` when your mode ends, for example on a Back button. Side Hustle then shows the menu and the hub again.

## Add an icon

[Section titled “Add an icon”](#add-an-icon)

Embed a PNG as `<AssemblyName>.hub-icon.png`. The hub finds it without any code:

```xml
<EmbeddedResource Include="icon.png" LogicalName="YourMod.hub-icon.png" />
```

The hub shows this icon also while the boot gate holds your mod back and none of your code has run. For another resource name, set `IconResource` on the descriptor. `Icon` (a `Sprite`) and `IconTex` (a `Texture2D`) win over both.

## Check it works

[Section titled “Check it works”](#check-it-works)

The log shows:

```plaintext
Gamemode registered: 'Your Mode' (you.yourmode).
```

Your row is in the hub. Click Solo, and `OnLaunchSingleplayer` runs.

![The Side Hustle hub with the "Your Mode" row selected: icon, name, author and the Host, Join and Solo buttons](/img/guides/sidehustle/hub-your-mode.webp)

A problem in the descriptor is logged with the gamemode id and the field name.

## Next

[Section titled “Next”](#next)

* [Add host settings](/mods/sidehustle/guides/host-settings/)
* [React to players and send messages](/mods/sidehustle/guides/sessions-and-messages/)
* [Run your gamemode in the game world](/mods/sidehustle/guides/world-gamemodes/)
* [Example gamemode](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-SideHustle/tree/main/Examples/ExampleGamemode)
* [API reference](/mods/sidehustle/api/)

# Add host settings

> Let the host set round time, teams or any other value on the Host form and read it on every player.

Give the host a form with your settings. Side Hustle sends the chosen values to every player, so you write no netcode.

**You need:** a registered gamemode with `Support` set to `Multiplayer` or `Hybrid`. See [Add a gamemode](/mods/sidehustle/guides/getting-started/).

## Steps

[Section titled “Steps”](#steps)

1. Add `HostSettings` to your descriptor. Each entry is one control on the Host form.

   ```csharp
   HostSettings = new[]
   {
       new SettingDescriptor
       {
           Key = "round_time", Label = "Round time", Category = "Rounds",
           Type = SettingType.Slider, Min = 60, Max = 900, Step = 30, WholeNumbers = true,
           Unit = "s", Default = "300",
       },
       new SettingDescriptor
       {
           Key = "teams", Label = "Teams", Category = "Rounds",
           Type = SettingType.Segmented, Options = new[] { "Two", "Four" }, Values = new[] { "2", "4" },
           Default = "2",
       },
       new SettingDescriptor
       {
           Key = "friendly_fire", Label = "Friendly fire", Hint = "Team mates can hurt each other.",
           Type = SettingType.Toggle, Default = "0",
       },
   },
   ```

   * `Key` is the wire format. Keep it short and never rename it. All values travel in Steam lobby data, which has a size limit.
   * The form shows a section header each time `Category` changes. Sort your settings by category.
   * Every value is a string. A toggle stores `"1"` or `"0"`. A segmented or dropdown control stores the entry of `Values`, or the label when `Values` is null.

2. Optional: add `Presets`. The host picks one, and its values fill the matching controls.

   ```csharp
   Presets = new[]
   {
       new SettingPreset
       {
           Name = "Quick round", Hint = "Short rounds, two teams.", Recommended = "Best for 2-6",
           MinPlayers = 2, MaxPlayers = 6,
           Values = new Dictionary<string, string> { ["round_time"] = "120", ["teams"] = "2" },
       },
   },
   ```

   * A preset whose `MinPlayers` to `MaxPlayers` range fits the lobby size can be selected when the form opens. `DefaultSelected = true` always selects it.
   * When the host changes a value, joiners see the mode as “Custom - Quick round”. Set `Mode` to use another name.
   * `Experimental = true` adds a badge and sorts the preset to the end.
   * A key without a matching setting is ignored.

3. Read the values in your launch callbacks. Host and clients get the same values.

   ```csharp
   OnHostMultiplayer = ctx => StartRound(ctx),
   OnJoinMultiplayer = ctx => StartRound(ctx),


   static void StartRound(LaunchContext ctx)
   {
       var mp = ctx.Multiplayer;
       int roundTime = mp.GetInt("round_time", 300);
       int teams = mp.GetInt("teams", 2);
       bool friendlyFire = mp.GetBool("friendly_fire");
       string mode = mp.Mode;   // "Quick round", "Custom - Quick round" or null
   }
   ```

   `GetInt` and `GetFloat` parse with the invariant culture. `GetBool` reads `"1"` and `"true"` as true.

## Check it works

[Section titled “Check it works”](#check-it-works)

1. Click Host on your row and open the full form.

2. Your settings show under their category headers. With `Presets`, the preset picker is above them.

   ![The full Host form with a Rounds section: a Round time slider at 300 s, a Two/Four Teams choice and a Friendly fire toggle with its hint](/img/guides/sidehustle/host-form.webp)

3. Host, then join with a second instance. Log `roundTime` on both: the values are the same.

## Next

[Section titled “Next”](#next)

* [React to players and send messages](/mods/sidehustle/guides/sessions-and-messages/)
* [`SettingDescriptor` in the API reference](/mods/sidehustle/api/)

# Make your mod sync to other players

> Publish your mod so Side Hustle can install it on a joining player automatically and find it from a lobby.

Give your mod a download source Side Hustle can use. A player who joins a lobby without your mod then gets it installed, or gets a direct link.

**You need:** a released mod. For the gamemode fields, a registered gamemode.

## How Side Hustle finds your mod

[Section titled “How Side Hustle finds your mod”](#how-side-hustle-finds-your-mod)

The host lists every loaded mod with its version and SHA256 hash. For each mod it picks one source:

| Source                                                      | What the joining player gets                |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| Thunderstore has a package with the installed version       | Automatic install                           |
| `downloadLink` points at a GitHub repository                | Automatic download from its releases        |
| `downloadLink` points at Nexus, Thunderstore or doodesch.de | A checklist entry with that link            |
| No usable source                                            | Nothing. The player joins without your mod. |
