| The 14 shipped Sideload apps                              | 0.1 percent                    |
| Showcase: React 19 + Tailwind v4, through the Vite plugin | 1.9 percent                    |
| A Tailwind v3 build, raw                                  | 8.2 percent                    |
| A Tailwind v4 build, raw                                  | 12.7 percent                   |

`@doodesch/sideload-vite` rewrites web CSS into the spelling this engine reads: logical properties to physical, nesting flattened, Tailwind’s five-slot shadow chain reduced to the layer that gets drawn. It takes Tailwind v4 from 12.7 to 1.9 percent lost. See [Dev loop and testing](/mods/sideload/guides/dev-loop-and-testing/) and [Build your first app](/mods/sideload/guides/your-first-app/).

## Next

[Section titled “Next”](#next)

* [JavaScript, DOM and events](/mods/sideload/guides/javascript-dom-and-events/)
* [Clipping and scrolling](/mods/sideload/guides/clipping-and-scrolling/)
* [Troubleshooting](/mods/sideload/guides/troubleshooting/)

# Hot reload and test your app

> Edit a page live in the game, inspect it, preview it in Chrome and test it headless.

Edit your page while the game runs, and test it without launching the game. Hot reload needs a development build.

## Hot reload

[Section titled “Hot reload”](#hot-reload)

1. Create the folder `Mods/<appId>/` before the page first builds.

2. Put your web files in it:

   ```plaintext
   Mods/mystash/index.html
   Mods/mystash/app.css
   Mods/mystash/app.js
   ```

3. Save a file. The page rebuilds about 250 ms after the last write.

Rules:

* **The folder must exist at first build.** If the F9 overlay says “not watching - create Mods// to edit live”, quit, create the folder and relaunch.
* **A leftover folder outranks a fresh build.** Every file in it wins over the embedded copy, so rebuilding your mod changes nothing. Copy the bundle in after every build, or delete the folder.
* **A reload drops the script engine.** JS state and listeners start over.
* C# changes need a rebuild and a game restart. An editor’s UTF-8 BOM is stripped.

`npm run dev` in a project from `@doodesch/create-sideload-app` writes the bundle into `Mods/<appId>/` on every save, so the folder is never stale. See [Build your first app](/mods/sideload/guides/your-first-app/).

## Check it works

[Section titled “Check it works”](#check-it-works)

Press **F9**. For each mounted page it shows fps, viewport size and scale, box / rule / wired counts, render count with the last render time, reload count, the script status with its last error, and whether the watcher runs.

The render count should rise once per change. A count that climbs every frame means something rebuilds the page every frame. A repaint is not a render, so a pan driven by `transform` keeps the count flat. A pan written as `left`/`top` adds one per frame. See [JavaScript, DOM and events](/mods/sideload/guides/javascript-dom-and-events/).

**Ctrl+F10** outlines every box in magenta and every text leaf in cyan.

`[Sideload/layout]` in the log is a rect dump after every render: `x y w h right bottom` per node, plus the compiled text of leaves. Use it when a box has the wrong size. The font list is dumped once per session; it shows valid `font-family` names.

## Console commands

[Section titled “Console commands”](#console-commands)

Debug builds only, typed into the game’s dev console. The console needs `Settings.ConsoleEnabled` and the host role. Both are a live toggle in the settings window.

| Command                                   | What it does                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sideloadkeys`                            | lists every key claim in offer order, and whether the gate is open                                                                                    |
| `sideloadkey <key>`                       | delivers that press down the real path, gate included - `sideloadkey Enter`                                                                           |
| `sideloadwheel [notches] [appId]`         | turns the wheel over the newest page through the real raycast and names what took the notch. Negative scrolls down                                    |
| `sideloadsurface [off\|<width> <height>]` | mounts the selftest bundle in a panel at the middle of the screen, at the size you pick                                                               |
| `sideloadgamma [hex]`                     | for every mounted page, names the canvas, its render mode and camera, and what a colour turns into on the way to the shader - `sideloadgamma #3a3d42` |

## Read the log first

[Section titled “Read the log first”](#read-the-log-first)

When a page loads, Sideload names every rule it could not use, once per app, with the lost value (needs 1.12+):

```plaintext
[Sideload] my-app: 4 Deklaration(en) wirkungslos - der Browser befolgt sie, diese Engine nicht:
    'padding: 1rem' - der Wert ist fuer diese Engine unlesbar, die Deklaration faellt weg.
    'align-items: baseline' wird gelesen und dann ignoriert - es passiert nichts.
    '@media (min-width: 640px)' wird uebersprungen - der ganze Block darin ist wirkungslos.
    Listener auf 'change' - dieses Ereignis stellt Sideload nie zu, der Handler laeuft nie.
```

It reads the whole stylesheet. It stays on after the first build, so a style your script writes at runtime is named the first time it happens.

## Chrome DevTools

[Section titled “Chrome DevTools”](#chrome-devtools)

Set the `DevTools` preference to attach the real Chrome inspector to a page in the game. You get the console, evaluate, the Elements tree with computed styles, and `Page.reload`, which re-reads your files. Sideload speaks the DevTools protocol on `127.0.0.1`.

| Setting                 | Default | What it does                                                                                                                             |
| ----------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DevTools`              | `false` | The gate. Off means nothing listens. Anything that reaches the port can run code in your pages, so leave it off unless you build an app. |
| `DevToolsPort`          | `9333`  | The loopback port. Change it only on a clash. Clamped 1024-65535.                                                                        |
| `DevToolsAutoOpen`      | `true`  | Opens Chrome or Edge at the landing page once the first page mounts. Off writes the address to the log.                                  |
| `DevToolsFrontend`      | empty   | Path to your own DevTools frontend. Overrides the settings below.                                                                        |
| `DevToolsFetchFrontend` | `true`  | Downloads the frontend once per machine (about 4.5 MB) for offline use. Never runs while `DevTools` is off.                              |

## Browser preview

[Section titled “Browser preview”](#browser-preview)

The same `app.js` and `app.css` run in Chrome against a stand-in bridge. This tests structure, copy, state and flow without a game launch. Write `preview.html`:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="sideload-preview.css">
<script type="module">
import { mount } from './sideload-preview.js';
import { call, ready, scenarios } from './s1-mock.js';


mount({ title: 'WhatsDab', appId: 'whatsdab', call, ready, scenarios });
</script>
```

Copy the shared files in with `node sync.mjs` from `Workspace/tools/sideload-preview`. The [reference app](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-WhatsDab/tree/main/Assets/whatsdab) is a finished example.

Do not hand-write the compatibility rules. `sideload-preview.css` holds the engine’s numbers, such as the 15px base, and a test compares them with the engine.

**The fence.** A browser `Element` has about three hundred members. The engine’s wrapper has under seventy. `el.append(child)` works in Chrome and does nothing in the game, with no error. The shell proxies your elements and names the first use of anything the engine lacks. It also shadows globals the engine never installs: `navigator`, `location`, `getComputedStyle`, `matchMedia`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `MutationObserver`. Findings go to the console and to a panel under the stage. The allowlist is generated from `Sideload/Script/DomApi.cs`.

Check the preview still starts:

```plaintext
cd Workspace/tools/sideload-preview
npm install && npm run smoke
```

This boots every bundle against a headless DOM in about a second and applies every named scenario.

Chrome lays out with its own engine. The preview proves your logic and roughly the look, not exact pixels. Check layout in the headless tests below and in the game.

## Fail the build on a new CSS loss

[Section titled “Fail the build on a new CSS loss”](#fail-the-build-on-a-new-css-loss)

The loss report also runs offline over a folder of stylesheets. A build can refuse to finish when the result gets worse:

```plaintext
dotnet run --project Workspace/Tests/Sideload.Tests -v q --nologo -- \
    --corpus MyMod/Assets/myapp --baseline MyMod/Assets/myapp/css.baseline --fail-on all --quiet
```

It parses and cascades with the engine’s own code. Exit code 0 means nothing new. Exit code 2 means it named something and the build should stop.

| Flag                      | What it does                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--corpus <folder>`       | Every `.css` under it, recursively. Required.                                                                                                          |
| `--baseline <file>`       | The losses already accepted. Anything not in it is new.                                                                                                |
| `--update-baseline`       | Writes that file from today’s run. Do this once, then shrink it.                                                                                       |
| `--fail-on <kind[,kind]>` | `all`, or any of `unknown-property`, `value-rejected`, `value-ignored`, `selector-rejected`, `at-rule-skipped`, `dead-event-listener`. Off by default. |
| `--quiet`                 | Prints one line per new finding and nothing otherwise.                                                                                                 |
| `--json <file>`           | Machine-readable run: one record per finding with `kind`, `subject`, `detail`, `file`, `count` and a `message`.                                        |
| `--out <file.md>`         | The full table as Markdown instead of stdout.                                                                                                          |

Run `--update-baseline` once before you turn the gate on. Feed the JSON into a Vite build like this:

```js
for (const d of JSON.parse(report).diagnostics)
  if (d.new) this.warn(`${d.file}: ${d.message} (${d.count}x)`);
```

With **[`@doodesch/sideload-vite`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@doodesch/sideload-vite)** most losses never reach the gate. The plugin rewrites logical properties to physical, flattens nesting and collapses Tailwind’s five-slot shadow chain.

## Headless tests

[Section titled “Headless tests”](#headless-tests)

Run your page’s JavaScript against your real C# handlers with no Unity, in about a second. Create a `net8.0` console project that links your mod’s logic files, embeds `app.js` as a resource, and runs it on the same Jint version with a stand-in `document`, `s1` and `console`.

```csharp
var app = new AppHarness();                       // runs app.js against the real handlers
app.Click(app.El("add"));
app.Input(app.El("entry"), "wire up the phone");
Check.Eq("1", app.El("count").TextContent);
```

* Keep the MelonMod entry point free of logic. Put handlers and data in their own files with **no engine reference**, so the suite compiles them without Unity. Put game-dependent code in a separate folder behind an interface.
* **A new `s1.call` name needs a case in the fake bridge’s switch.** Otherwise the call returns `""` with no warning and the test passes on the wrong state.
* Assert on behaviour, then break the code on purpose. A test that stays green after you delete its line tests nothing.
* Headless tests cannot cover layout, text measurement, painting or TextMeshPro. Check visuals in the game.

A working suite is `Workspace/Tests/WhatsDab.Tests` in the [development monorepo](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-WhatsDab).

## Next

[Section titled “Next”](#next)

* [Troubleshooting](/mods/sideload/guides/troubleshooting/)
* [CSS and layout reference](/mods/sideload/guides/css-and-layout/)

# Install Sideload

> Install Sideload for players, or add its one-file API to your own mod project.

Install Sideload because another mod needs it. On its own it adds nothing to the game.

**You need:** Schedule I (IL2CPP, current Steam build) and MelonLoader 0.7.3 or newer. See [Install](/install/).

## Steps for players

[Section titled “Steps for players”](#steps-for-players)

1. With r2modman or Gale: install Sideload from Thunderstore. Dependencies are placed for you.
2. By hand: install MelonLoader 0.7.3, then put `Sideload.dll` in `Schedule I/Mods/`.

`Sideload.dll` contains the HTML parser and the script engine. Nothing else is needed.

If you upgrade from 1.10.0 or older, `AngleSharp.dll`, `Jint.dll` and `Esprima.dll` may remain in `UserLibs/` or `Mods/`. Sideload uses them if present. You can delete them.

Sideload does not use S1API. It patches `HomeScreen.Start` itself.

## Steps for mod authors

[Section titled “Steps for mod authors”](#steps-for-mod-authors)

1. Add `Sideload.cs` to your project as source. Do not reference Sideload.

   ```xml
   <Compile Include="path\to\Sideload.cs" Link="Sideload.Api.cs" />
   ```

2. Get the file from [`Sideload.Api/Sideload.cs`](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Sideload/blob/main/Sideload.Api/Sideload.cs).

The file has no references (no MelonLoader, Unity or IL2CPP interop). It finds the host by reflection. Your mod ships as one DLL and works with or without Sideload. Referencing `Sideload.Api.dll` behaves the same but adds a second assembly for players to install.

Two optional npm packages (MIT):

| Package                                                                                        | Use                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`@doodesch/create-sideload-app`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@doodesch/create-sideload-app) | `npx @doodesch/create-sideload-app my-app` creates the bundle, C# mod, Vite build and types |
| [`@doodesch/sideload-vite`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@doodesch/sideload-vite)             | The Vite plugin alone, for an existing project                                              |

## Settings

[Section titled “Settings”](#settings)

Settings are in `UserData/MelonPreferences.cfg` under `Sideload_01_Main`.

* `AppKeys` is on by default. It lets an app open from a key it asked for while the phone is in the pocket. Sideload ignores the key while you type, while paused, and in a station, shop or the console. Set it off and no app gets a key.
* All other settings are developer tools and are off by default.

## Check it works

[Section titled “Check it works”](#check-it-works)

Start the game. `MelonLoader/Latest.log` lists Sideload under the loaded mods.

## Next

[Section titled “Next”](#next)

* [Build your first app](/mods/sideload/guides/your-first-app/)
* [Keys and typing](/mods/sideload/guides/keys-and-typing/)
* [Dev loop and testing](/mods/sideload/guides/dev-loop-and-testing/)

# JavaScript, DOM and events reference

> Look up the script engine, globals, DOM members and events available to a Sideload page.

Look up what JavaScript a Sideload page can use. The engine is Jint with every experimental feature on.

## The language

[Section titled “The language”](#the-language)

**ES2015 through ES2024.** Classes with `#private` fields, optional chaining, nullish coalescing, destructuring, template literals, generators, `async`/`await` syntax, spread, `replaceChildren`, `at(-1)`. Nothing is transpiled or polyfilled.

## Globals

[Section titled “Globals”](#globals)

`document`, `s1`, `console`, `fetch`, `Promise`, `FormData`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, `clearTimeout`, `clearInterval`, `requestAnimationFrame`, `cancelAnimationFrame`, `devicePixelRatio`, `addEventListener`, `removeEventListener`, `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, and `window`, `self` and `globalThis`, which are all three the global object itself.

`localStorage` and `sessionStorage` use the same store as `s1.storage`. Timers run on the Unity main thread and never race with your C#.

There is no `navigator` and there is no file access. The element wrapper has under seventy members against a browser’s three hundred. `dataset`, `scrollTop`, `offsetWidth`, `insertAdjacentHTML`, `append` and `prepend` are among the ones missing. A missing member returns nothing and does not throw, so a bad call fails silently. The browser preview names such calls - see [Dev loop and testing](/mods/sideload/guides/dev-loop-and-testing/).

## Engine limits

[Section titled “Engine limits”](#engine-limits)

* **250 ms budget per handler.** The engine aborts a slower handler and logs the error with `file:line`.
* **A page is refused before rendering** if it has more than 20000 elements or 200 nesting levels.
* **One script engine per page.** A reload drops it, so JS state and listeners start over.

## document

[Section titled “document”](#document)

```js
document.getElementById('entry')
document.querySelector('.thread.on')
document.querySelectorAll('.bubble')
document.createElement('div')
document.addEventListener('back', fn)     // binds at <body>
```

## element

[Section titled “element”](#element)

```js
el.textContent          el.className        el.id            el.value
el.appendChild(child)   el.replaceChildren()                 el.remove()
el.setAttribute(n, v)   el.getAttribute(n)  el.removeAttribute(n)
el.classList.add/remove/toggle/contains
el.style.backgroundColor = '#5E6AD2'   // any property, camelCase or the CSS spelling
el.style.cssText = 'left: 4px; top: 8px'
el.querySelector(sel)   el.querySelectorAll(sel)
el.addEventListener(type, fn)
el.focus()              // an input or textarea; ignored on anything else
el.scrollToEnd()        // host-only method, not in a browser
el.rect()               // { x, y, width, height } in css pixels, from the top left of the screen
```

* **`replaceChildren()` takes no arguments.** It clears the element. Append the new children yourself.
* **There is no `style.setProperty`.** Assign the property. `el.style.borderColor` and `el.style['border-color']` reach the same declaration.
* **`el.rect()` is the whole geometry surface** (needs Sideload 1.12+). There is no `getBoundingClientRect`, `offsetWidth`, `clientHeight` or scroll offset. The frame is the screen’s top left, the same one `position: fixed` uses. It reflects the last render, so a box created in the current handler reads as zeroes.
* **`el.focus()` works before the field exists.** The render that creates the field grants the focus. To keep the caret in a box, use `data-typing` - see [Keys and typing](/mods/sideload/guides/keys-and-typing/).

Every mutation marks the subtree dirty. The renderer merges a frame’s changes into one rebuild. Never call a render function.

## Repaint or rebuild

[Section titled “Repaint or rebuild”](#repaint-or-rebuild)

A rebuild recreates every GameObject on the page, at about **0.5 ms per box**. A 200-box page takes about 100 ms. That is fine for a click and a hitch at 60 times a second.

Writing one of these properties repaints a single box. The layout and objects stay the same:

```plaintext
transform
background   background-color   background-image
border-color
border-radius   and the four per-corner longhands
box-shadow
```

Everything else rebuilds, including `cssText`. `color` and `opacity` rebuild on purpose: both are inherited, and a repaint would leave descendants with the old value.

For anything that moves at 60 Hz (pan, zoom, slide-in), write `transform`:

```js
// hitches: left is a layout property, so every frame rebuilds the page
world.style.left = x + 'px';


// does not: one box, repainted
world.style.transform = 'translate(' + x + 'px, ' + y + 'px) scale(' + zoom + ')';
```

When you place many boxes at once, each `el.style.left = ...` re-parses the element’s inline block. A hundred markers with two writes each is two hundred parses. That can exceed the 250 ms budget, abort the render and leave the app empty. Write the attribute once:

```js
el.setAttribute('style', 'left:' + x.toFixed(1) + 'px;top:' + y.toFixed(1) + 'px');
```

## Events

[Section titled “Events”](#events)

Eleven types are dispatched. Any other type (`pointerdown`, `change`, `focus`, `blur`, `keyup`, `mousemove`) never fires. The log names such a listener.

| Event               | Where       | Carries                                                                       | Raised when                                                                 |
| ------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `click`             | the element | `e.offsetX/offsetY`, `e.normX/normY`                                          | the player clicks a wired element                                           |
| `input`             | the control | `e.value`                                                                     | the text in an `input`/`textarea` changed                                   |
| `keydown`           | the control | `e.key`, `e.value`, `e.ctrlKey/shiftKey/altKey`, `e.repeat`, `e.hasSelection` | Enter in a single-line field, plus every key the field named in `data-keys` |
| `dragstart`         | the element | the offsets                                                                   | a drag begins on an element the page listens to                             |
| `drag`              | the element | the offsets, `e.deltaX/deltaY`                                                | the pointer moved during that drag                                          |
| `dragend`           | the element | the offsets                                                                   | the drag ended                                                              |
| `wheel`             | the element | `e.wheelDelta`                                                                | a wheel notch over an element the page listens to                           |
| `back`              | document    | `e.source`, cancellable                                                       | right-click or Escape                                                       |
| `orientationchange` | document    | `e.value`                                                                     | the phone turned, after the page was laid out again                         |
| `mouseenter`        | the element | -                                                                             | the pointer arrived on it                                                   |
| `mouseleave`        | the element | -                                                                             | the pointer left it                                                         |

* `mouseenter` and `mouseleave` do not bubble. Pair them with `el.rect()` to place a hover tooltip. `:hover` cannot do that, because it cannot change layout.
* `keydown` reaches a field for Enter only, unless the field names more keys in `data-keys="Tab ArrowUp Ctrl+R"`. See [Keys and typing](/mods/sideload/guides/keys-and-typing/).
* Events bubble to the document in registration order per node. `stopPropagation()` ends the walk.
* The event object has `type`, `target`, `currentTarget`, `value`, `key`, `ctrlKey`, `shiftKey`, `altKey`, `repeat`, `hasSelection`, `source`, `offsetX`, `offsetY`, `normX`, `normY`, `deltaX`, `deltaY`, `wheelDelta`, `defaultPrevented`, `preventDefault()` and `stopPropagation()`. A field an event does not carry is zero or an empty string, never undefined.
* **A hit target exists only** on elements that a state rule targets, on `button`/`a`/`input`/`textarea`, and on elements with a **click**, **drag** or **wheel** listener. The pointer passes through everything else.
* The wiring is decided at render. A listener added to an element already on screen, with no other change, starts working at the next rebuild.

## Where the pointer landed

[Section titled “Where the pointer landed”](#where-the-pointer-landed)

`click` carries `e.offsetX` / `e.offsetY` in the element’s own CSS pixels from its top-left, and `e.normX` / `e.normY` as a 0..1 fraction of its width and height. Prefer the fractions: they survive resizing and turning the phone. A zero-sized box reports 0, never `NaN`.

```js
map.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
  const worldX = e.normX * WORLD_WIDTH;
  const worldY = e.normY * WORLD_HEIGHT;
  s1.call('map.mark', worldX.toFixed(1) + ',' + worldY.toFixed(1));
});
```

## drag and wheel

[Section titled “drag and wheel”](#drag-and-wheel)

A `dragstart`, `drag` or `dragend` listener makes an element draggable. A `wheel` listener makes it take the wheel. Both gestures are **taken away from the scroll area the element sits in**: a draggable row cannot be scrolled past by dragging it, and a wheel-taking box stops the list under it from scrolling. Put the listeners on the thing that pans, not on every row.

```js
let x = 0, y = 0;


viewport.addEventListener('drag', (e) => {
  x += e.deltaX;
  y += e.deltaY;
  world.style.transform = 'translate(' + x.toFixed(1) + 'px, ' + y.toFixed(1) + 'px)';
});


viewport.addEventListener('wheel', (e) => {
  zoom *= e.wheelDelta > 0 ? 0.9 : 1.1;
  apply();
});
```

* `e.deltaX` / `e.deltaY` are the pointer movement since the previous event, in CSS pixels, y down. They are zero on `dragstart` and `dragend`. They are measured against the page, so moving the dragged element does not feed back.
* `e.wheelDelta` is one notch. It is positive when the wheel turns toward the player (list scrolls down, conventionally zoom out). That is the sign of a browser’s `deltaY`.
* A drag that ends on its own element does not also raise a click.

## back: right-click and Escape

[Section titled “back: right-click and Escape”](#back-right-click-and-escape)

Right-click and Escape both mean back. Calling `preventDefault()` keeps your app open:

```js
document.addEventListener('back', (e) => {
  if (!deepInside()) return;   // nothing to go back to, so Sideload closes the app
  e.preventDefault();
  goUpOneLevel();
});
```

Without a listener, back closes the app. **An app with panes, tabs or a detail view that has no listener traps the player one level deep.**

In landscape a two-pane app shows both panes, so back must close it. Check the orientation:

```js
document.addEventListener('back', (e) => {
  if (s1.orientation !== 'portrait' || pane !== 'detail') return;
  e.preventDefault();
  showList();
});
```

`e.source` is `"rightClick"` or `"escape"`.

## orientationchange

[Section titled “orientationchange”](#orientationchange)

`@media` moves boxes, but only your script knows which pane the player should land on after a turn. The event fires after the page is laid out at the new shape, so reading sizes in it is safe.

```js
document.addEventListener('orientationchange', (e) => {
  if (e.value === 'portrait') showDetail();
  render();
});
```

## console

[Section titled “console”](#console)

`console.log`, `.info`, `.warn`, `.error`. Output goes to the MelonLoader log prefixed with your app id, and to an attached Chrome DevTools console. The F9 overlay keeps errors.

## Patterns

[Section titled “Patterns”](#patterns)

Build an element in one expression:

```js
const el = (tag, className, text) => {
  const node = document.createElement(tag);
  if (className) node.className = className;
  if (text != null) node.textContent = String(text);
  return node;
};
```

* Use `for (const x of xs)` so each handler closes over its own item. A `var` loop shares the last one.
* Do not call `scrollToEnd()` on every render. The host restores scroll offsets across a rebuild. Call it only when the content grew: remember the identity and item count you last pinned, and return early when neither moved.

## Next

[Section titled “Next”](#next)

* [Keys and typing](/mods/sideload/guides/keys-and-typing/)
* [CSS and layout reference](/mods/sideload/guides/css-and-layout/)
* [Troubleshooting](/mods/sideload/guides/troubleshooting/)

# Handle keys and typing

> Read keys in a focused field, open your app with a key, and keep the keyboard in your box.

Every key is a game binding: W walks, 1-9 swap slots, Escape leaves. Pick the mechanism that gets a key handed to your app.

| You want                                   | Use                        | Scope                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| a key while the player types in your field | `data-keys` on the input   | that field, while it has the caret                     |
| a key that opens your app                  | `app.OnKey(...)` in C#     | anywhere the game lets the player take their phone out |
| typing to land in your box without a click | `data-typing` on the input | your app, while that box is on screen                  |

A focused `<input>` sets `GameInput.IsTyping`, and that flag stops the game reading the keyboard. Without a focused field, typing “hello” walks the player around.

## Read keys in a focused field

[Section titled “Read keys in a focused field”](#read-keys-in-a-focused-field)

1. Name the keys on the input:

   ```html
   <input id="prompt" data-keys="Tab ArrowUp ArrowDown Ctrl+R">
   ```

2. Listen for `keydown` on that element. It carries `e.key`, `e.ctrlKey` / `e.shiftKey` / `e.altKey`, `e.repeat` and `e.hasSelection`. `e.hasSelection` tells Ctrl+C as copy from Ctrl+C as interrupt.

Rules:

* Only named keys are dispatched, and only they are taken from the field. A page with no `data-keys` behaves as before. `Ctrl+Backspace` can delete a word while plain Backspace stays the field’s own.
* **Modifiers match exactly.** `Tab` fires for a bare Tab, not Shift+Tab. Declare both to get both. A page that names only `ArrowUp` leaves Shift+Up free to select text.
* **A declared key is always swallowed.** `preventDefault()` cannot un-move a caret. To keep the caret moving, do not declare the arrows.
* A held key repeats after 0.35 s, then every 0.06 s, then every 0.03 s after 1.2 s. `data-reject-first` on the field keeps a dead key from opening a fresh line.

**Key names:** letters, digits, `F1`-`F12`, `Tab`, `Backspace`, `Delete`, `Insert`, `Home`, `End`, `PageUp`, `PageDown`, `ArrowUp`, `ArrowDown`, `ArrowLeft`, `ArrowRight`, `Space`. Modifiers are `Ctrl`, `Shift` and `Alt`, joined with `+`.

Punctuation is not allowed, because it sits on different physical keys on different layouts. `Enter` and `Escape` are refused with a log line. Enter already arrives as `keydown` from the field’s submit, and Escape arrives as `back`.

## Open the app with a key

[Section titled “Open the app with a key”](#open-the-app-with-a-key)

`data-keys` needs a page on screen. To open the app, claim the key in C# (needs Sideload 1.10+):

```csharp
Apps.Register("whatsdab", "WhatsDab.Assets.whatsdab")
    .OnKey("Enter", key => QuickChat());


private static bool QuickChat()
{
    if (!Online) return false;      // nothing to write to - let somebody else have Enter
    if (!app.Show()) return false;  // the game refused the phone


    app.Emit("chat.compose", "everyone");
    return true;
}
```

* `AppHandle.CanClaimKeys` is false on older hosts, where `OnKey` does nothing. Check it when the key is the only way in, especially with `NoIcon()`.
* Key spelling matches `data-keys`. Separate several keys with spaces or commas. `Enter` is allowed and `Escape` is not.
* Return `false` to pass the press to the next app that wants the key. The argument is the key that fired.
* **Two apps, one key:** the app that notified the player most recently gets it. An app that never notified sorts last. A single claimant wins from the first press.
* **An app on screen owns every key it claimed.** No other app is offered them.

The key is read only where the game’s own phone key works. It is not read:

* while the player is typing, including in your focused fields
* while paused, asleep, dead or arrested
* while another screen owns the view: a station, a shop, dialogue, the rename dialog, the developer console

The player switch is `AppKeys` in `MelonPreferences.cfg`, on by default. `Enter` also answers the number pad.

## Keep the keyboard in your box

[Section titled “Keep the keyboard in your box”](#keep-the-keyboard-in-your-box)

```html
<input class="entry" id="entry" data-typing placeholder="Write a message">
```

While the field is painted and its app is shown, the caret returns to it whenever nothing else holds one. Use it for chat, search and other type-first screens.

* **Painted only.** A pane hidden with `display: none` does not hold the keyboard.
* **App shown only.** An app that is open but back in the player’s pocket does not take the keyboard. Sideload also lets go if the app stops being visible while it holds the caret.
* **Nothing selected only.** A control the player clicked keeps the caret, so your search box and the game’s console and dialogs stay usable. Clicking a non-field (row, list, button) selects nothing, and that press brings the keyboard back.

While a field has the caret, the game ignores Escape, right-click and the phone key. Sideload reads the game’s exit actions itself and delivers `back` on the first press. You need no code for this.

## Do not poll the keyboard

[Section titled “Do not poll the keyboard”](#do-not-poll-the-keyboard)

A mod that polls `Input.GetKeyDown` gets none of the above. It fires while the player names a save and fights other mods for the key.

## Check it works

[Section titled “Check it works”](#check-it-works)

| What you see                                        | Cause                                                                              |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| the key never fires                                 | refused at parse time - look for `[Sideload] '<app>' asked for the key` in the log |
| the key fires nowhere useful                        | another app claimed it and notified more recently, or the app on screen owns it    |
| the key does nothing at a station or in the console | the gate is shut wherever the phone key is refused                                 |
| `OnKey` does nothing at all                         | Sideload older than 1.10 - check `AppHandle.CanClaimKeys`                          |
| typing walks the player around                      | no `data-typing`, or the field is not painted in this layout                       |
| the caret will not stay in the box                  | something else is selected: a clicked control or a game screen                     |

## Next

[Section titled “Next”](#next)

* [JavaScript, DOM and events](/mods/sideload/guides/javascript-dom-and-events/)
* [Phone integration](/mods/sideload/guides/phone-integration/)
* [API reference](/mods/sideload/api/)

# Add phone features to your app

> Add an icon, orientation, badge, notifications and a key shortcut to your app on the in-game phone.

Use the phone features around your page: icon, orientation, badge, notifications, key and images. To render a page outside the phone, see [Surfaces](/mods/sideload/guides/surfaces/).

**You need:** a registered app (`AppHandle`). See [Build your first app](/mods/sideload/guides/your-first-app/).

## Set the icon

[Section titled “Set the icon”](#set-the-icon)

1. Put `icon.png` in your bundle: square, 256x256, transparent outside the rounded square. Without it the app gets a flat colored square.
2. The caption is `iconLabel` from `Apps.Register`. It defaults to the title.

## Open the app from code, with no icon

[Section titled “Open the app from code, with no icon”](#open-the-app-from-code-with-no-icon)

Use `.NoIcon()` when the way in is somewhere else, such as a world object. The app still has its panel, page and exit key.

```csharp
Apps.Register("reflash-messages", "Reflash.Assets.reflash-messages", "Messages").NoIcon();
```

Open and close it from code:

```csharp
app.Open();              // same as pressing the icon
app.Close();             // back to the home screen
bool open = app.IsOpen;
```

* `Open()` closes any other open app and turns the phone to this app’s orientation. The page is built on the first open.
* It does not take the phone out of the pocket. A phone raised later shows your app. `IsOpen` is true in that state; `IsOnScreen` also requires the phone to be up.
* Before the app is on a phone, `Open()` does nothing. The log says `open: '<id>' is not on a phone`. The home screen is built when the gameplay scene starts.
* Set `NoIcon()` during init. Set later, it applies from the next spawn (a scene change).

Needs Sideload 1.1.0+. On an older host, both calls do nothing and the icon appears anyway. Check first:

```csharp
if (!AppHandle.CanOpenProgrammatically)
{
    LoggerInstance.Error("Sideload 1.1.0 or newer is required - not registering.");
    return;
}
```

## Show the icon only sometimes

[Section titled “Show the icon only sometimes”](#show-the-icon-only-sometimes)

Call `Icon(bool)` while the game runs.

```csharp
app.Icon(consoleIsOn);   // show or hide the square
```

* Call it every time you evaluate the condition. The phone is rebuilt on every scene load, so do not cache “already showing”.
* It is safe in an update loop.
* The first `Icon(true)` creates the square. Hiding only deactivates it, so it returns to its place.

## Support both orientations

[Section titled “Support both orientations”](#support-both-orientations)

1. Name the orientations in preference order. The first one is the opening orientation.

   ```csharp
   .Orientation("landscape")               // landscape only
   .Orientation("landscape", "portrait")   // both, opens landscape
   .Orientation("portrait", "landscape")   // both, opens portrait
   // no call                              -> landscape only
   ```

2. Style both in one sheet.

   ```css
   @media (orientation: portrait) {
     .app { flex-direction: column; }
     .sidebar { width: 100%; flex: 1; }
     .detail { display: none; }
     .app.on-detail .sidebar { display: none; }
     .app.on-detail .detail { display: flex; }
   }
   ```

* Do not build a turn button. The player turns the phone with the game’s rotate keys (Q and E by default, gamepad triggers too). Sideload adds a “Rotate Phone” hint while a turnable app is open.
* Sideload remembers the choice per app. Do not store it.
* A turn lays the page out again. The document, script, scroll positions and field contents stay.
* `s1.setOrientation(v)` turns the phone from the page. It is refused with a log line if the app never declared that orientation. `s1.orientation` reads the current one.
* A two-pane split rarely fits 400 px. In portrait, use push navigation: the script marks the visible pane, the stylesheet hides the other. Use `orientationchange` and `back` (see [JavaScript, DOM and events](/mods/sideload/guides/javascript-dom-and-events/)).

## Set an unread badge

[Section titled “Set an unread badge”](#set-an-unread-badge)

```csharp
app.Badge(unreadCount);   // zero clears it
```

Counts above 99 show as “99+”. Set it when your count changes, not on a timer. The value survives a phone rebuild.

## Send a notification

[Section titled “Send a notification”](#send-a-notification)

```csharp
app.Notify("Jessi Waters", "on my way");
```

This raises the game’s own slide-in notification with your app icon. It does nothing if the app is not on a phone yet. It interrupts the player, so use `Badge` for anything that can wait.

Skip it when the player already sees your app:

```csharp
if (!app.IsOnScreen) app.Notify(sender, text);
```

`IsOnScreen` is true when your app is the open app and the phone is up.

## Open the app with a key

[Section titled “Open the app with a key”](#open-the-app-with-a-key)

1. Register the key in your mod. `OnKey` fires with the phone still in the pocket.

   ```csharp
   app.OnKey("Enter", _ => Online && app.Show());
   ```

2. Order the calls inside the handler: `Show()` first, then `Emit()`.

   ```csharp
   internal static bool QuickChat()
   {
       if (!_source.Online) return false;   // let another app have Enter
       if (!_app.Show()) return false;      // the game refused the phone


       _app.Emit("chat.compose", "everyone");
       return true;
   }
   ```

3. In the page, call `focus()` on your field when the event arrives.

* Call `Show()` before `Emit()`. The page is built on first open. Before that, nothing listens, so an early `Emit` is lost. `Show()` builds the page synchronously.
* Use `Show()`, not `Open()`. `Open()` picks the app but leaves the phone down, so the app is open and invisible. `Show()` raises the phone first, so the first layout uses the real viewport.
* Return `false` to decline. The press then goes to the next app that wants the same key. Decline when you cannot help the player.
* A `focus()` before the field is painted is granted when the field is rendered.

Key ownership, where keys are read, and caret rules are on [Keys and typing](/mods/sideload/guides/keys-and-typing/).

## Show images

[Section titled “Show images”](#show-images)

For a file in your bundle:

```html
<img class="mark" src="glyph.png" alt="">
```

```css
.mark { width: 20px; height: 20px; color: #FFFFFF; }
```

* Set both width and height. Layout cannot read the PNG size, so an image without both is empty.
* The aspect ratio stays inside the box. `color` tints the image.

For a picture your mod makes at runtime, pass PNG bytes and use the `s1://` name:

```csharp
app.Image("avatar/" + steamId, pngBytes);   // null or empty bytes remove it
```

```html
<img class="avatar" src="s1://avatar/76561198000000001">
```

Sprites are cached per app. The same name replaces the picture.

## Look up what a page cannot do

[Section titled “Look up what a page cannot do”](#look-up-what-a-page-cannot-do)

| You want                          | Result                                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Read or set a scroll offset       | No. `scrollToEnd()` is the only scroll member. The host restores offsets after a rebuild when the content looks the same.                                               |
| Know where a box is               | Yes, with Sideload 1.12+. `el.rect()` gives `{ x, y, width, height }` in CSS pixels from the screen’s top left. It shows the last render, so a new box reads as zeroes. |
| Know the app opened or closed     | Not from the page. `orientationchange` is the only state signal. Your mod can use `app.IsOpen` and `app.IsOnScreen`.                                                    |
| Get a key other than Enter        | Name it in `data-keys` on a text field. It arrives as `keydown`. Enter and Escape are refused: they already arrive as `keydown` and `back`.                             |
| Get a key while the app is closed | From your mod: `app.OnKey(...)`.                                                                                                                                        |
| Type without a click first        | Yes. Set `data-typing` on the field.                                                                                                                                    |
| Focus a control from script       | Only `input` and `textarea`, with `el.focus()`.                                                                                                                         |
| Clipboard, files, time zone       | No. There is no `navigator`.                                                                                                                                            |

If the page cannot do it, ask whether your mod can, behind an `s1.call`.

## Check it works

[Section titled “Check it works”](#check-it-works)

The icon, badge and notification appear on the phone. The log shows a line for each refused call, such as the `open:` message above.

## Next

[Section titled “Next”](#next)

* [Surfaces](/mods/sideload/guides/surfaces/)
* [Keys and typing](/mods/sideload/guides/keys-and-typing/)
* [The bridge](/mods/sideload/guides/the-bridge/)
* [API reference](/mods/sideload/api/)

# Render a page in your own panel

> Mount a Sideload page in any RectTransform, such as a menu column or a machine panel.

Render a page where there is no phone: a main menu column, a machine panel or a wall board. A surface uses the same renderer, CSS subset and `s1.call` / `s1.on` channel as a phone app.

**You need:** Sideload 1.13.0+, a bundle with `LogicalName` resources (see [Build your first app](/mods/sideload/guides/your-first-app/)), and a `RectTransform` to draw into.

A surface has no home-screen icon, no turnable orientation, no badge and no notifications. For those, register an app.

## Steps

[Section titled “Steps”](#steps)

1. Mount the page.

   ```csharp
   using Sideload.Api;


   Surfaces.Mount(myPanel, "sidehustle-menu", "SideHustle.Assets.menu")
           .OnCall("menu.state", _ => StateJson())
           .Emit("ready");
   ```

   | Argument          | Meaning                                                                                                                           |
   | ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   | `hostRect`        | Your `UnityEngine.RectTransform`. Typed `object` so the shim compiles without a Unity reference. Pass the RectTransform directly. |
   | `id`              | Unique across apps and surfaces. It is also the folder under `Mods/` that overrides the bundle.                                   |
   | `bundlePrefix`    | Embedded-resource prefix of your web files.                                                                                       |
   | `designShortSide` | Default 0. See step 2.                                                                                                            |
   | `hostAssembly`    | Assembly that holds the bundle. Defaults to the caller’s.                                                                         |

   `Mount` returns a `SurfaceHandle` with chainable `OnCall`, `Emit`, `AllowHost` and `Unmount`.

2. Choose `designShortSide`. A wrong value makes everything the wrong size.

   * `0` maps one CSS pixel to one device unit. Use it for a panel that uGUI has already laid out.
   * A number such as `400` scales the page against that width. A phone-app stylesheet then renders unchanged.

3. Remount when the panel is rebuilt. A surface ends when its `RectTransform` is destroyed, so a scene reload needs nothing else.

   ```csharp
   if (!Surfaces.IsMounted("sidehustle-menu")) Mount();
   ```

4. Keep a fallback for hosts without surfaces. `Surfaces.Available` is false on Sideload 1.12.0 and older, and `Mount` then returns a handle whose calls do nothing.

   ```csharp
   if (Surfaces.Available) MountThePage();
   else BuildTheOldPanel();
   ```

## Check it works

[Section titled “Check it works”](#check-it-works)

The page draws inside the panel at the size you expect. `Surfaces.IsMounted(id)` returns true. It returns false once the panel is destroyed.

![A Sideload page mounted on a 600x400 panel over the game, drawn by the sideloadsurface 600 400 command](/img/guides/sideload/surface-panel.webp)

[Section titled “Next”](#next)

* [CSS and layout](/mods/sideload/guides/css-and-layout/)

# Call C# from the page and back

> Send strings between your page and your mod with s1.call, Emit, storage and fetch.

Move data between your page and your C# mod. Strings cross in both directions. Use JSON for structured data. No CLR object reaches the script and no script object reaches your mod.

**You need:** a registered app. See [Build your first app](/mods/sideload/guides/your-first-app/).

| Direction                | C#                                         | JS                                       |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------- |
| page asks the mod        | `app.OnCall("name", arg => answer)`        | `const s = s1.call('name', 'arg')`       |
| mod tells the page       | `app.Emit("name", payload)`                | `s1.on('name', payload => ...)`          |
| page keeps its own state | -                                          | `s1.storage.get/set/remove/clear`        |
| page reaches the network | `app.AllowHost("api.example.com")`         | `fetch(url, init).then(...)`             |
| phone orientation        | `app.Orientation("landscape", "portrait")` | `s1.orientation`, `s1.setOrientation(v)` |
| player pressed back      | -                                          | `document.addEventListener('back', ...)` |

## Steps

[Section titled “Steps”](#steps)

### 1. Answer a call from the page

[Section titled “1. Answer a call from the page”](#1-answer-a-call-from-the-page)

1. Register handlers on the app. Handlers are scoped to your app id, so two mods can both own `list`.

   ```csharp
   app.OnCall("items.list", _ => string.Join("\n", Items))
      .OnCall("items.add", Add)
      .OnCall("items.clear", _ => { Items.Clear(); return "ok"; });
   ```

2. Call it from the page. `s1.call` is synchronous. It runs your handler on the Unity main thread in the same frame, so it can touch game state. Do not `await` it.

   ```js
   const raw = s1.call('items.list');
   ```

A call with no handler returns `""` and logs a warning. A handler that throws returns `""` and logs the exception. The page sees only the empty string, so show a message for it.

### 2. Push an event to the page

[Section titled “2. Push an event to the page”](#2-push-an-event-to-the-page)

1. Emit from `OnUpdate`, when something changed. Do not emit on a timer.

   ```csharp
   public override void OnUpdate()
   {
       if (_revision == _pushed) return;
       _pushed = _revision;
       _app?.Emit("items.changed", Items.Count.ToString());
   }
   ```

2. Subscribe in the page.

   ```js
   s1.on('items.changed', render);
   ```

Keep the payload small. Send “something changed” and let the page ask for the data.

Never call `Emit` inside an `OnCall` handler. It re-enters the script engine while the engine is still on the stack.

### 3. Send structured data

[Section titled “3. Send structured data”](#3-send-structured-data)

`Sideload.Api` has no JSON writer. Write one, or copy the 60-line [`Json.cs`](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-WhatsDab/blob/main/Chat/Json.cs) from WhatsDab. The page has `JSON.parse`.

```csharp
app.OnCall("chat.threads", _ =>
    Json.Array()
        .Item(Json.Object().Add("id", t.Id).Add("name", t.Name).Add("unread", t.Unread))
        .Close());
```

```js
const threads = JSON.parse(s1.call('chat.threads') || '[]');
```

For a simple list, use a newline-separated string. For several inbound arguments, use one separator character. Reject a payload that contains a second one:

```csharp
int split = raw.IndexOf('\n');
if (split <= 0) return "error";
string id = raw.Substring(0, split), text = raw.Substring(split + 1);
if (text.IndexOf('\n') >= 0) return "error";
```

### 4. Keep page state in s1.storage

[Section titled “4. Keep page state in s1.storage”](#4-keep-page-state-in-s1storage)

`s1.storage` holds strings by name. It writes one JSON file per app at `UserData/Sideload/<appId>.json`.

```js
const tab = s1.storage.get('tab', 'players');
s1.storage.set('tab', 'items');
s1.storage.remove('tab');
```

It is not the game save. Use it for UI state such as the last tab or a draft. Keep world data in your mod behind an `s1.call`.

Do not store the phone orientation here. Sideload remembers it per app.

`localStorage` and `sessionStorage` write to the same store.

### 5. Allow a network host and fetch

[Section titled “5. Allow a network host and fetch”](#5-allow-a-network-host-and-fetch)

A page reaches no host until your mod allows it.

```csharp
Apps.Register("mystash", "MyMod.Assets.mystash")
    .AllowHost("api.example.com")
    .AllowHost("*.cdn.example.com");
```

* `*.example.com` covers one label under it, not `example.com` itself.
* Ports are ignored.
* The scheme must be https, except for `127.0.0.1` and `localhost`.
* Every redirect hop is checked again.
* Limits: 10 s timeout, 4 MB response, 8 requests in flight.
* A blocked request rejects with the exact `AllowHost` call that is missing.

Never `await` a fetch. It blocks the thread that delivers the answer and freezes the game. Use `.then()` and `.catch()`:

```js
fetch('https://api.example.com/status')
  .then(r => r.json())
  .then(data => render(data))
  .catch(e => console.error('status failed:', e));
```

## What a page cannot reach

[Section titled “What a page cannot reach”](#what-a-page-cannot-reach)

There is no `navigator`, no file access and no clipboard. Timers are the four standard ones plus `requestAnimationFrame`. `window` is an alias for the global object. For anything else, put it behind an `s1.call`. Your mod is ordinary C# with the whole game in reach.

For limits that `s1.call` cannot fix, see [Phone integration](/mods/sideload/guides/phone-integration/).

## Check it works

[Section titled “Check it works”](#check-it-works)

The page shows the string your handler returned. When an event is emitted, the `s1.on` callback runs. Failures appear in `MelonLoader/Latest.log`.

[Section titled “Next”](#next)

* [Phone integration](/mods/sideload/guides/phone-integration/)

# Troubleshooting Sideload apps

> Match what you see in your Sideload app to its cause and fix.

Find your symptom below. Check `MelonLoader/Latest.log` first.

## No icon on the phone

[Section titled “No icon on the phone”](#no-icon-on-the-phone)

The log should show `app registered: <id>`. If it is missing, `Apps.Register` never ran, usually because the mod threw earlier. If it is there, look for `spawned on the phone`.

## The page is blank and the log says `index.html not found in bundle or override`

[Section titled “The page is blank and the log says index.html not found in bundle or override”](#the-page-is-blank-and-the-log-says-indexhtml-not-found-in-bundle-or-override)

The `LogicalName` in your csproj does not match the `bundlePrefix` you passed to `Apps.Register`. Set `LogicalName` explicitly, because MSBuild mangles folder names otherwise. The two must agree exactly.

## No page builds and the log says `runtime dependency not found in UserLibs or next to the mod`

[Section titled “No page builds and the log says runtime dependency not found in UserLibs or next to the mod”](#no-page-builds-and-the-log-says-runtime-dependency-not-found-in-userlibs-or-next-to-the-mod)

Sideload 1.10.0 or older ships AngleSharp, Jint and Esprima as separate DLLs, and one is missing. Update to 1.11+. See [Installation](/mods/sideload/guides/installation/).

## Everything stacks vertically

[Section titled “Everything stacks vertically”](#everything-stacks-vertically)

Every box is a flex column. Add `flex-direction: row`.

## A list will not scroll and pushes everything off screen

[Section titled “A list will not scroll and pushes everything off screen”](#a-list-will-not-scroll-and-pushes-everything-off-screen)

Add `min-height: 0` next to its `flex: 1`. The automatic minimum is the content height.

## A rule does nothing

[Section titled “A rule does nothing”](#a-rule-does-nothing)

Read the log. Sideload names each unusable rule once per app:

```plaintext
[Sideload] my-app: 4 Deklaration(en) wirkungslos - der Browser befolgt sie, diese Engine nicht:
    'padding: 1rem' - der Wert ist fuer diese Engine unlesbar, die Deklaration faellt weg.
    'align-items: baseline' wird gelesen und dann ignoriert - es passiert nichts.
    '@media (min-width: 640px)' wird uebersprungen - der ganze Block darin ist wirkungslos.
    Listener auf 'change' - dieses Ereignis stellt Sideload nie zu, der Handler laeuft nie.
```

Five things get named: a property with no case, an unreadable value, a value read then ignored by layout, a rejected selector, and a listener on an event that is never dispatched. The whole stylesheet is scanned on first load. Then check [CSS and layout reference](/mods/sideload/guides/css-and-layout/).

## `margin: 0 auto` does not centre

[Section titled “margin: 0 auto does not centre”](#margin-0-auto-does-not-centre)

Auto margins are zero. Use `justify-content` or `align-self`.

## A `:hover` rule that changes size does nothing

[Section titled “A :hover rule that changes size does nothing”](#a-hover-rule-that-changes-size-does-nothing)

State rules repaint and do not re-lay-out. Colours work, geometry does not.

## Contents draw outside a box with `overflow: hidden`

[Section titled “Contents draw outside a box with overflow: hidden”](#contents-draw-outside-a-box-with-overflow-hidden)

Sideload older than 1.1 does not clip with `hidden`. Update.

## A child’s square corner draws over its parent’s rounded one

[Section titled “A child’s square corner draws over its parent’s rounded one”](#a-childs-square-corner-draws-over-its-parents-rounded-one)

The clip is an axis-aligned rectangle. Give the child the same radius, or inset it. See [Clip and scroll content](/mods/sideload/guides/clipping-and-scrolling/).

## Nothing scrolls sideways

[Section titled “Nothing scrolls sideways”](#nothing-scrolls-sideways)

There is no horizontal scroll area. Move the strip with a `transform` inside an `overflow: hidden` box.

## A character renders as an empty box

[Section titled “A character renders as an empty box”](#a-character-renders-as-an-empty-box)

The game’s font atlases carry Latin text only. Arrows, checkmarks, dingbats and `…` come out as tofu. Write the word, or use three full stops.

## Every word breaks after one character

[Section titled “Every word breaks after one character”](#every-word-breaks-after-one-character)

The page was laid out while its panel was hidden, so text measured about ten times too short. Sideload refuses to build off screen. If you see this, something forces a render on a hidden view.

## The list jumps to the bottom while the player reads further up

[Section titled “The list jumps to the bottom while the player reads further up”](#the-list-jumps-to-the-bottom-while-the-player-reads-further-up)

`scrollToEnd()` ran on a render that changed nothing the reader cares about. The host restores scroll offsets across a rebuild. Call it only when the content grew.

## Typing into a field swallows characters

[Section titled “Typing into a field swallows characters”](#typing-into-a-field-swallows-characters)

Report it. The engine keeps the control across a rebuild, so this should not happen.

## Typing in the app moves the player

[Section titled “Typing in the app moves the player”](#typing-in-the-app-moves-the-player)

No field has the caret, so every letter is a game binding. Put `data-typing` on the input. If it is there, the field is not painted in the current layout or is not a real `input`/`textarea`. See [Handle keys and typing](/mods/sideload/guides/keys-and-typing/).

## The caret will not stay in the box

[Section titled “The caret will not stay in the box”](#the-caret-will-not-stay-in-the-box)

Something else is selected: a control the player clicked, or a game screen. `data-typing` never takes the caret from either.

## A key claimed with `OnKey` never fires

[Section titled “A key claimed with OnKey never fires”](#a-key-claimed-with-onkey-never-fires)

Check three causes in order. The key was refused at parse time (the log says `[Sideload] '<app>' asked for the key ...`). The app on screen owns that key and did not claim it. Sideload is older than 1.10, where `OnKey` does nothing (`AppHandle.CanClaimKeys` tells you). A key that does nothing at a station, a shop or the console is correct.

## Escape needs two presses

[Section titled “Escape needs two presses”](#escape-needs-two-presses)

Update to Sideload 1.10+. Older versions lose the press while a field has the caret.

## `addEventListener('change', ...)` never fires

[Section titled “addEventListener('change', ...) never fires”](#addeventlistenerchange--never-fires)

Only `click`, `input`, `keydown`, `mouseenter`, `mouseleave`, `dragstart`, `drag`, `dragend`, `wheel`, `back` and `orientationchange` exist. The log names a listener on any other type.

## A click never arrives

[Section titled “A click never arrives”](#a-click-never-arrives)

A hit target exists only on elements that a state rule targets, on `button`/`a`/`input`/`textarea`, and on elements with a **click**, **drag** or **wheel** listener. A `mousedown` listener does not count.

## A list stopped scrolling after a drag or wheel listener went on a row

[Section titled “A list stopped scrolling after a drag or wheel listener went on a row”](#a-list-stopped-scrolling-after-a-drag-or-wheel-listener-went-on-a-row)

Both gestures are taken from the scroll area the element sits in. Move the listener to the thing that pans.

## A drag ends and the click handler fires too

[Section titled “A drag ends and the click handler fires too”](#a-drag-ends-and-the-click-handler-fires-too)

A drag on a draggable element suppresses the click. If the click fires, the dragged element is not the clicked element.

## The pan hitches and the F9 render count climbs every frame

[Section titled “The pan hitches and the F9 render count climbs every frame”](#the-pan-hitches-and-the-f9-render-count-climbs-every-frame)

The page rebuilds every frame, at about 0.5 ms per box. Write `transform` instead of `left`/`top`. The list of properties that repaint is in [JavaScript, DOM and events](/mods/sideload/guides/javascript-dom-and-events/).

## The app cannot be closed with right-click

[Section titled “The app cannot be closed with right-click”](#the-app-cannot-be-closed-with-right-click)

Your `back` handler takes the event every time. In landscape a two-pane app has nothing to step back from, so check `s1.orientation` first. See [JavaScript, DOM and events](/mods/sideload/guides/javascript-dom-and-events/).

## Turning the phone lands on the wrong pane

[Section titled “Turning the phone lands on the wrong pane”](#turning-the-phone-lands-on-the-wrong-pane)

`@media` cannot decide that. Listen for `orientationchange` and pick the pane the player was looking at.

## `app.Open()` does nothing and the log says `open: '<id>' is not on a phone`

[Section titled “app.Open() does nothing and the log says open: '\<id>' is not on a phone”](#appopen-does-nothing-and-the-log-says-open-id-is-not-on-a-phone)

The app is not spawned yet. The home screen is built when the gameplay scene starts, so `Open()` from mod init or the main menu has nothing to open.

## An iconless app cannot be reached

[Section titled “An iconless app cannot be reached”](#an-iconless-app-cannot-be-reached)

`NoIcon()` removes the only door Sideload provides. Call `Open()` from your own entry point. On an older host the icon appears anyway and `Open()` does nothing. Check `AppHandle.CanOpenProgrammatically` before you register.

## Editing a file changes nothing

[Section titled “Editing a file changes nothing”](#editing-a-file-changes-nothing)

Either the watcher never started (the `Mods/<appId>/` folder must exist before first launch), or a stale `Mods/<appId>/` folder overrides your new bundle. The F9 overlay says which. See [Hot reload and test your app](/mods/sideload/guides/dev-loop-and-testing/).

## The game freezes when the app opens

[Section titled “The game freezes when the app opens”](#the-game-freezes-when-the-app-opens)

Something used `await` on a promise the host settles later, usually `await fetch(...)`. Jint blocks the main thread inside `await`. Use `.then()` / `.catch()`. Sideload logs a warning at load when it sees the pattern.

## `s1.call` returns an empty string

[Section titled “s1.call returns an empty string”](#s1call-returns-an-empty-string)

No handler is registered under that app id and name (logged as a warning), or the handler threw (logged as an exception). Both look the same from the page, so treat `""` as a real answer.

## A page refuses to render and says it is too large

[Section titled “A page refuses to render and says it is too large”](#a-page-refuses-to-render-and-says-it-is-too-large)

The page has over 20000 elements or 200 nesting levels. A loop is probably building nodes without clearing.

## Getting help

[Section titled “Getting help”](#getting-help)

Attach `MelonLoader/Latest.log`. `[Sideload]` lines carry the app id, and a script error carries `file:line`. For a visual problem add an F9 screenshot and the `[Sideload/layout]` dump for the box.

[support.doodesch.de/sideload](https://support.doodesch.de/sideload)

# Build your first app

> Build a small app with HTML, CSS and JavaScript and see its icon on the in-game phone.

Build a phone app from a web page and a few lines of C#. Its icon appears on the in-game phone.

**You need:** Schedule I with MelonLoader 0.7.3, Sideload installed, and the .NET SDK. Node.js is needed only for the scaffolder.

## Fast route: the scaffolder

[Section titled “Fast route: the scaffolder”](#fast-route-the-scaffolder)

1. Create the project.

   ```plaintext
   npx @doodesch/create-sideload-app my-app --template preact
   cd my-app
   npm install
   ```

2. Start the dev build. It rebuilds on save and copies the bundle to `Mods/<appId>/`, so no game restart is needed.

   ```plaintext
   npm run dev
   ```

3. Point it at your game once with `--deploy "D:/.../Schedule I/Mods"`. It remembers the path.

4. Fill in the two `PATH\TO` hints in the csproj (MelonLoader and `Sideload.cs`). The mod compiles to one DLL with the bundle embedded.

Templates: `preact` (default), `react`, `vanilla`. The script engine parses your framework each time a page opens, so bundle size is a load-time cost.

| Template  | Bundle | Load   | Mount 100 rows |
| --------- | ------ | ------ | -------------- |
| `preact`  | 14 kB  | 37 ms  | 53 ms          |
| `react`   | 139 kB | 113 ms | 54 ms          |
| `vanilla` | 0      | 0      | -              |

To add Sideload to an existing Vite project:

```plaintext
npm install -D @doodesch/sideload-vite
```

```js
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';
import { sideload } from '@doodesch/sideload-vite';


export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [sideload({ appId: 'myapp', deploy: 'D:/games/Schedule I/Mods' })],
});
```

Both packages are MIT and live under `tools/` in the Sideload repo. `examples/showcase` there is a full React 19, Tailwind v4 and TypeScript app.

## Steps: by hand

[Section titled “Steps: by hand”](#steps-by-hand)

### 1. Lay out the project

[Section titled “1. Lay out the project”](#1-lay-out-the-project)

```plaintext
MyMod/
  MyMod.csproj
  Core.cs
  Assets/mystash/index.html
  Assets/mystash/app.css
  Assets/mystash/app.js
  Assets/mystash/icon.png     optional
```

`icon.png` is a square PNG, 256x256, transparent outside the rounded square. Without it the app gets a flat colored square derived from its id.

### 2. Write MyMod.csproj

[Section titled “2. Write MyMod.csproj”](#2-write-mymodcsproj)

The project needs MelonLoader and the shim as source. It needs no Unity reference and no Sideload reference.

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">


  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net6.0</TargetFramework>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <LangVersion>latest</LangVersion>
    <RootNamespace>MyMod</RootNamespace>
    <AssemblyName>MyMod</AssemblyName>
  </PropertyGroup>


  <ItemGroup>
    <Reference Include="MelonLoader">
      <HintPath>path\to\MelonLoader.dll</HintPath>
      <Private>false</Private>
    </Reference>
  </ItemGroup>


  <ItemGroup>
    <Compile Include="path\to\Sideload.cs" Link="Sideload.Api.cs" />
  </ItemGroup>


  <!-- The LogicalName prefix is the bundlePrefix you pass to Apps.Register. -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <EmbeddedResource Include="Assets/mystash/*">
      <LogicalName>MyMod.Assets.mystash.%(Filename)%(Extension)</LogicalName>
    </EmbeddedResource>
  </ItemGroup>


</Project>
```

Keep the `LogicalName`. Without it MSBuild mangles the resource names, `Apps.Register` finds no files, and the app is blank with no error.

### 3. Register the app in Core.cs

[Section titled “3. Register the app in Core.cs”](#3-register-the-app-in-corecs)

```csharp
using MelonLoader;
using Sideload.Api;


[assembly: MelonInfo(typeof(MyMod.Core), "MyMod", "1.0.0", "You")]
[assembly: MelonGame("TVGS", "Schedule I")]


namespace MyMod
{
    public class Core : MelonMod
    {
        private static readonly List<string> Items = new List<string>();
        private static AppHandle _app;
        private static int _revision;
        private static int _pushed = -1;


        public override void OnInitializeMelon()
        {
            _app = Apps.Register(
                id: "mystash",                          // also the folder under Mods/ that overrides the bundle
                bundlePrefix: "MyMod.Assets.mystash",   // the LogicalName prefix from the csproj
                title: "Stash",
                iconLabel: "Stash");


            _app.OnCall("items.list", _ => string.Join("\n", Items))
                .OnCall("items.add", text =>
                {
                    if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(text) || text.IndexOf('\n') >= 0) return "error";
                    Items.Add(text.Trim());
                    _revision++;
                    return "ok";
                });
        }


        public override void OnUpdate()
        {
            if (_revision == _pushed) return;
            _pushed = _revision;
            _app?.Emit("items.changed", Items.Count.ToString());
        }
    }
}
```

Register in `OnInitializeMelon`, without checks. A call made before Sideload loads is queued and replayed when the host appears. Every call is a no-op when Sideload is absent.

Do not call `Emit` inside an `OnCall` handler. Emit from your update loop, as above.

### 4. Write index.html

[Section titled “4. Write index.html”](#4-write-indexhtml)

Leave out `<html>`, `<head>` and `<body>`. The parser adds them.

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="app.css">


<div class="screen">
  <header class="bar">
    <span class="title">Stash</span>
    <span class="badge" id="count">0</span>
  </header>


  <div class="list" id="items"></div>


  <div class="row">
    <input class="field" id="entry" placeholder="Add an item" maxlength="60">
    <button class="btn" id="add">Add</button>
  </div>
</div>


<script src="app.js"></script>
```

### 5. Write app.css

[Section titled “5. Write app.css”](#5-write-appcss)

```css
body {
  /* Required. The root has auto height, so percentage heights below need this. */
  height: 100%;
  font-family: game-ui;
  font-size: 14px;
  color: #ECEDF1;
}


.screen { height: 100%; padding: 16px; gap: 12px; background: #14161C; }


.bar { flex-direction: row; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; }


.list { flex: 1; min-height: 0; overflow: auto; gap: 6px; }


.row { flex-direction: row; gap: 8px; }


.field { flex: 1; height: 40px; padding: 0 12px; border-radius: 8px; background: #1D2029; align-items: center; }


.btn { padding: 0 18px; height: 40px; border-radius: 8px; background: #5E6AD2; text-align: center; align-items: center; }
.btn:hover { background: #6E7AE2; }
```

* Every box is a flex column. Add `flex-direction: row` for a row.
* A scrollable box needs `min-height: 0` next to `flex: 1`. Without it the box grows to its content and never scrolls.

### 6. Write app.js

[Section titled “6. Write app.js”](#6-write-appjs)

```js
const $ = (id) => document.getElementById(id);


function render() {
  const items = s1.call('items.list').split('\n').filter(Boolean);
  const box = $('items');
  box.replaceChildren();


  for (const text of items) {
    const row = document.createElement('div');
    row.className = 'item';
    row.textContent = text;
    box.appendChild(row);
  }


  $('count').textContent = String(items.length);
}


$('add').addEventListener('click', () => {
  const text = $('entry').value.trim();
  if (!text || s1.call('items.add', text) !== 'ok') return;
  $('entry').value = '';
  render();
});


s1.on('items.changed', render);
render();
```

### 7. Build and create the dev folder before the first launch

[Section titled “7. Build and create the dev folder before the first launch”](#7-build-and-create-the-dev-folder-before-the-first-launch)

1. Run `dotnet build` on your mod.
2. Create `Schedule I/Mods/mystash/` and copy `index.html`, `app.css` and `app.js` into it.
3. Start the game.

The file watcher starts only if that folder exists when the page first builds. If you launch first, you get no hot reload for the whole session.

## Check it works

[Section titled “Check it works”](#check-it-works)

Open the phone. The Stash icon is on the home screen. Open it, type an item, and press Add. The list and the counter update.

![The Stash app on the phone with three items and the counter at 3, the Add an item field and the Add button below](/img/guides/sideload/stash-app.webp)
