# Snitch changelog

> Every released version of Snitch and what changed in it.

All notable changes to Snitch are documented here. Format based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com).

## \[1.7.1] - 2026-10-16

[Section titled “\[1.7.1\] - 2026-10-16”](#171---2026-10-16)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed)

* Panels, counters and log lines a mod registers before Snitch loads now show up. With an early `Profiler.AutoRegister()` they stayed queued for good.
* Mods built against the 1.7.0 `Snitch.Api` get that fix without a rebuild: Snitch binds their copy of the shim itself.
* The `Vanilla.NPCs` and `Vanilla.Trash` states work on game 0.4.7f12 again. Both threw “Method not found”.
* `snitch ablate npc` works on 0.4.7f12 again. The game removed the pause call it used.

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed)

* `Vanilla.NPCs` counts “can’t move” (ragdolled, in a building or in a vehicle) instead of “paused”, which the game no longer has.

## \[1.7.0] - 2026-09-06

[Section titled “\[1.7.0\] - 2026-09-06”](#170---2026-09-06)

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added)

* The `(unattributed)` row: how much of a frame ran inside no section at all. A mod reporting 0.65 ms/frame was costing 144 ms in a Harmony postfix nothing wrapped.
* `snitch unattributed` splits your worst frames into the part your sections explain and the part nothing does.
* `snitch patches on`: times other mods’ Harmony prefixes, postfixes and finalizers under the mod that owns them. Off by default; `WrapModPatches` arms it with sampling.
* `SpikeFactor` sets how far above the window median a frame has to be to count as bad. Default 1.5.

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-1)

* Section labels no longer carry ANSI colour escapes out of a mod’s name. They reached `report_*.md` and `sections_*.csv` as raw bytes.
* The dashboard showed version 1.5.1 for four releases. It shows the running build now.

## \[1.6.2] - 2026-08-09

[Section titled “\[1.6.2\] - 2026-08-09”](#162---2026-08-09)

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-2)

* A mod’s debug build no longer hunts for Snitch on every API call when Snitch is absent. It searched five folders per call, hundreds of times during one world load.
* Log lines no longer repeat the mod’s own name. MelonLoader already puts it in front of every line.

## \[1.6.1] - 2026-08-04

[Section titled “\[1.6.1\] - 2026-08-04”](#161---2026-08-04)

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-1)

* `snitch` shows up in the game’s command list, so a console autocomplete or a terminal can offer it and complete it. It was answered by a patch and registered nowhere, which made it invisible to every tool that lists commands. Nothing about running it changes.

## \[1.6.0] - 2026-08-04

[Section titled “\[1.6.0\] - 2026-08-04”](#160---2026-08-04)

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-1)

* `snitch open` and `snitch close` show and hide the profiler panel without touching the keyboard. `snitch open all` and `snitch close all` do the same for the whole overlay. Needs Hotline 1.3.0 or newer.

## \[1.5.1] - 2026-08-01

[Section titled “\[1.5.1\] - 2026-08-01”](#151---2026-08-01)

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-2)

* Runs on Schedule I 0.4.6f11.
* Needs S1API 3.1.1, up from 3.0.5. Update it along with the mod.

## \[1.5.0] - 2026-07-31

[Section titled “\[1.5.0\] - 2026-07-31”](#150---2026-07-31)

Tune a mod’s values by dragging them, and open the dashboard without leaving the game.

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-2)

* **Sliders in mod panels.** A mod can expose a value as a slider (`Profiler.RegisterSlider`, `Panel.Slider`) instead of a number you type into the console. Snitch clamps it to the declared range and snaps it to the step before the mod’s setter runs, so every write path - dragging in game, the web dashboard, the phone remote, `snitch slider` - is bounded identically.
* Sliders render everywhere panels already do: the in-game overlay, the web dashboard and the phone remote.
* `snitch slider <sliderId> [value]` reads or writes one from the console. Omit the value to read it back. A slider is a mouse control and cannot be driven by a test harness; this is the scriptable equivalent.
* **Open dashboard** button in the Snitch panel, and `snitch dashboard`. It serves the bundled copy from `Mods/Snitch/wwwroot` when one is present, otherwise the hosted build, which connects back to the same loopback socket. With the data server off it says so rather than opening a page that cannot connect.

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-3)

* `snitch hud` and `snitch panel <id>` were still documented after 1.3.0 moved the overlay to Hotline, so following the docs printed “unknown”. The wiki now matches the commands that exist.

### Requirements

[Section titled “Requirements”](#requirements)

* In-game sliders need [Hotline](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Hotline) 1.2.0 or newer, which draws them. Without Hotline, Snitch still runs and the sliders remain usable from the console and the dashboard.

### Notes

[Section titled “Notes”](#notes)

* Control ids are slugified from the label and punctuation is dropped, so two labels differing only in punctuation collide and the second replaces the first. Give each control distinct words.

## \[1.4.0] - 2026-07-08

[Section titled “\[1.4.0\] - 2026-07-08”](#140---2026-07-08)

Use your phone as a remote for the profiler - scan a QR and start/stop sampling or trigger any mod’s actions without switching back to the browser window.

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-3)

* **Phone remote.** A “Connect a phone” QR - both in the web dashboard and in the in-game Snitch panel. Scan it and you get a compact remote: the live FPS, Start/Stop/Reset, and every mod’s panel actions and toggles.
* Works on the **same Wi-Fi** (the phone connects directly to the game) and **across networks** (the game relays through a small pairing service, so it works even over mobile data). On the same network the phone switches to the direct local connection on its own.
* **End-to-end encrypted** with a one-time key carried in the QR, so the relay only ever forwards ciphertext - your telemetry stays private even over the internet.
* Turn it on from the Snitch panel toggle or with `snitch lan on` (off by default).
* The dashboard now reads a capability list from the connected instance, so it only offers features the running build actually supports.

### Requirements

[Section titled “Requirements”](#requirements-1)

* The in-game QR uses [Hotline](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Hotline) 1.1.0 or newer (its panel image support). Everything else works without it.

## \[1.3.0] - 2026-06-26

[Section titled “\[1.3.0\] - 2026-06-26”](#130---2026-06-26)

The in-game overlay moves to the new Hotline framework, so every mod shares one overlay and one hotkey. The web dashboard and the profiling itself are unchanged.

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-3)

* The in-game overlay is now provided by Hotline (a dependency). Snitch contributes its profiler panel (frame stats, sections, states, Start/Stop/Reset) to the unified Hotline overlay, opened with Hotline’s master key (default F6).

### Removed

[Section titled “Removed”](#removed)

* Snitch’s own in-game windowing and its overlay settings (`ShowHud`, `HudFontSize`, `HudX`, `HudY`, `WindowLayouts`) and the `snitch hud` / `snitch panel <id>` console verbs - the overlay lives in Hotline now.

### Note

[Section titled “Note”](#note)

* Without Hotline, Snitch still profiles and serves the web dashboard, but has no in-game overlay. Hotline is pulled in automatically as a dependency.

## \[1.2.0] - 2026-06-25

[Section titled “\[1.2.0\] - 2026-06-25”](#120---2026-06-25)

The on-screen overlay becomes a small windowing layer, every mod gets its own panel, and there is a combined log timeline. The modder bridge ABI is unchanged (additive), so existing integrations keep working.

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-4)

* Multi-window overlay: the profiler HUD is now an “Overview” window alongside per-mod panels and a log “Timeline”. Each window is independently shown/hidden, dragged (title bar) and resized (bottom-right grip), with a scrollable body and a layout that persists across restarts.
* Per-mod panels: any mod that reports data gets its own toggleable panel of counters, state distributions, free text, action buttons, toggles and a log channel - in the overlay and the web dashboard. New modder API: the `Profiler.RegisterPanel(...)` fluent builder (`Counter`/`State`/`Text`/`Action`/`Toggle`/`Log`) and `Profiler.Log(...)`.
* Log timeline: a combined, chronological view of all channels (each mod plus Snitch and the console), with per-mod filtering, both in-game and on the dashboard.
* Arm sampling from the overlay: Start / Stop / Reset buttons in the Overview (no console needed). `F6` toggles the overlay and always summons the Overview, so it can’t get stuck closed.
* New console commands: `snitch panels`, `snitch panel <id> [on|off|move|size|reset]`, `snitch act <id>`, `snitch toggle <id>`, `snitch log [<channel>|all]`.

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-4)

* The on-screen “resize” is now a real window resize (width/height with scrolling); font size is a separate setting. Button labels no longer clip descenders.

## \[1.1.0] - 2026-06-24

[Section titled “\[1.1.0\] - 2026-06-24”](#110---2026-06-24)

The on-screen HUD is now movable and resizable, and remembers where you put it.

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-5)

* HUD position and font size are adjustable and persist across restarts: `snitch hud move <x> <y>`, `snitch hud font <n>`, and `snitch hud reset` (back to defaults), plus matching `HudX`, `HudY`, and `HudFontSize` settings (sliders in the Mod Manager UI). The overlay auto-fits, so a bigger font makes a bigger window.
* Drag the HUD with the mouse: grab the body to move it, or its bottom-right corner to change the font size (works while the cursor is free, e.g. with the phone or pause menu open).

### Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed-4)

* The `F6` hotkey now actually toggles the HUD (it was documented but never wired up).

## \[1.0.2] - 2026-06-22

[Section titled “\[1.0.2\] - 2026-06-22”](#102---2026-06-22)

Less code in mods, more profiling for free. No change to the host data/wire protocol or the bridge ABI, so existing integrations keep working.

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-6)

* Auto-instrumentation: while sampling, every other loaded mod’s per-frame methods (`OnUpdate`, `OnFixedUpdate`, `OnLateUpdate`, `OnGUI`) are timed automatically and shown as `<Mod>.OnUpdate` - per-mod frame cost with zero code on the mod’s side. Toggle with the `AutoInstrument` preference.
* Zero-wiring registration: a mod’s `SnitchProbe.Register()` is now discovered and called by the host automatically when sampling starts, so a mod no longer wires a registration call into its `OnInitializeMelon`.

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-5)

* Modder API shim class renamed `Snitch.Api.Snitch` -> `Snitch.Api.Profiler` (drops the `using Prof = ...` alias; just `using Snitch.Api;` then `Profiler.Sample(...)`). The bridge contract is unchanged, so previously shipped shims still bind and report.
* Cheaper no-op path: the shim’s pre-bind host lookup no longer scans every loaded assembly each call.

## \[1.0.1] - 2026-06-22

[Section titled “\[1.0.1\] - 2026-06-22”](#101---2026-06-22)

Internal cleanup. No functional or behavioural changes.

### Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed-6)

* Removed leftover development scaffolding: the dev-only verification probes and all internal “phase”-process references in code comments, console help, and docs.

## \[1.0.0] - 2026-06-22

[Section titled “\[1.0.0\] - 2026-06-22”](#100---2026-06-22)

Initial release. Feature-complete and verified in-game.

### Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added-7)

* Frame-time + GC sampler (the load-bearing measurement layer).
* Stopwatch section timer (`Snitch.Sample`), backing both the modder API and vanilla probes.
* Built-in state providers: NPCs (movement/visibility), trash (physics), quests (state).
* Vanilla CPU cost attribution via Harmony accumulators (`snitch vanilla on`) - e.g. `NPCMovement.Update/FixedUpdate`.
* Ablation A/B harness with a stability gate + lever registry (`snitch ablate <lever>`), built-in `npc` lever.
* Local HTTP + WebSocket data server (loopback `:6140`) with CORS/PNA/Origin/token.
* SnitchWeb live dashboard (React + uPlot), bundled offline at `http://localhost:6140/`.
* Zero-overhead modder API (`Snitch.Api`) - copy-in source or referenced DLL, no hard dependency.
* In-game HUD, periodic telemetry, and Markdown/CSV report export.

# Console commands

> Look up every snitch console command with its arguments and effect.

Look up a `snitch` command here. Open the in-game developer console and type it. Snitch is idle until `snitch start`.

| Command                              | What it does                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `snitch start`                       | Arm sampling and start streaming live data.                                                                                |
| `snitch stop`                        | Disarm sampling. The game keeps running.                                                                                   |
| `snitch status`                      | One-line summary: active, fps, section, state and counter counts.                                                          |
| `snitch frame`                       | Log the frame-time distribution (mean, median, p95, p99, min, max, fps, GC).                                               |
| `snitch top [n]`                     | Log the top N sections by ms/frame. Default 8.                                                                             |
| `snitch sections`                    | Log all sections.                                                                                                          |
| `snitch states [id]`                 | Log entity-state distributions, optionally filtered.                                                                       |
| `snitch counters`                    | Log the registered counters.                                                                                               |
| `snitch panels`                      | List the registered mod panels and their control counts.                                                                   |
| `snitch act <actionId>`              | Run a panel action by id, for example `Siesta:force-cosmetic`.                                                             |
| `snitch toggle <toggleId> [on\|off]` | Flip a panel toggle. Omit the state to switch it.                                                                          |
| `snitch slider <sliderId> [value]`   | Write a panel slider. Omit the value to read it with its range and step. See [Add a slider](/mods/snitch/guides/sliders/). |
| `snitch dashboard`                   | Open the [web dashboard](/mods/snitch/guides/web-dashboard/) in your browser.                                              |
| `snitch log [<channel>\|all] [n]`    | Print the last N log lines of a mod channel, or the combined timeline.                                                     |
| `snitch vanilla on\|off`             | Time vanilla hot paths, for example `NPCMovement.Update` and `FixedUpdate`.                                                |
| `snitch ablate <lever>`              | Measure a subsystem’s frame cost with an A/B toggle. Built-in lever: `npc`.                                                |
| `snitch levers`                      | List the ablation levers.                                                                                                  |
| `snitch report [md\|csv\|all]`       | Write a report to `Mods/Snitch/runs/` as Markdown and CSV.                                                                 |

## Notes

[Section titled “Notes”](#notes)

* `snitch slider` clamps and snaps like a drag. Use it for scripted tuning, because a script cannot drag.
* `snitch dashboard` opens the bundled dashboard when it sits beside the DLL, and the hosted site otherwise. It opens nothing when the local data server is off, and says so.
* `snitch vanilla on` adds Harmony probes that sum one label over all instances. Only the methods Snitch wraps are timed. See [How Snitch measures](/mods/snitch/guides/how-it-works/).
* `snitch ablate npc` switches all NPC movement off and measures the settled frame-time change. It runs host-only. Disable other NPC mods such as Siesta first.

# How Snitch measures

> Look up what each Snitch number measures, and where it cannot see.

Look up how Snitch gets its numbers. Snitch shows only numbers it can back up.

## The four layers

[Section titled “The four layers”](#the-four-layers)

| Layer               | What it measures                                                                                                                                               | Limit                                                                                                           |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Frame time and GC   | A rolling window gives mean, median, p95, p99 and fps. It also counts GC gen-0 and gen-1 collections per 1000 frames.                                          | None. Build-independent. Every other number is checked against it.                                              |
| Sections            | Stopwatch time of named sections: the ones a mod registers through the [API](/mods/snitch/guides/modder-api/), and vanilla hot paths with `snitch vanilla on`. | Self-measured. It sees only wrapped methods and includes a small patch overhead. It is not a sampling profiler. |
| State distributions | Counts of entities by state (NPC movement and visibility, trash physics, quest state, mod providers), read a few times a second.                               | Read-only tallies.                                                                                              |
| Ablation            | `snitch ablate <lever>` switches a subsystem off, waits for a stable frame time and reports the change.                                                        | Needs a calm scene.                                                                                             |

## Rules to know

[Section titled “Rules to know”](#rules-to-know)

* ProfilerRecorder engine counters do not work in the IL2CPP build. Snitch does not use them.
* Section times miss native work such as the NavMeshAgent. Use ablation for the total cost of a subsystem.
* Snitch shows its own cost as the `Snitch.Self` section.
* Everything is idle until `snitch start`.
* Profiling is read-only and safe in multiplayer. Ablation levers change state and run host-only.

## Example

[Section titled “Example”](#example)

`NPCMovement.Update` costs about 0.06 ms/frame for 200 NPCs. `NPCMovement.FixedUpdate` costs more, because it runs at the physics rate. The largest per-NPC cost is native (NavMeshAgent), and only ablation shows it.

## Next

[Section titled “Next”](#next)

* [Console commands](/mods/snitch/guides/console-commands/)
* [Profile your mod](/mods/snitch/guides/modder-api/)

# Install Snitch

> Install the Snitch profiler and start sampling from the Schedule I developer console.

Install Snitch, then start sampling from the developer console.

**You need:** the IL2CPP build of Schedule I, MelonLoader 0.7.x and S1API (`ifBars-S1API_Forked`). See [Install](/install/) for MelonLoader.

## Steps

[Section titled “Steps”](#steps)

1. With a mod manager (r2modman or the Thunderstore app), install **Snitch**. MelonLoader and S1API come as dependencies.
2. Without a manager, install MelonLoader and S1API, then put `Snitch.dll` in the game’s `Mods/` folder.
3. Optional: install [Hotline](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Hotline) for the in-game windows. Without it, Snitch still runs, reports to the console and serves the web dashboard.
4. Start the game and open the developer console.
5. Run `snitch start`.

## Check it works

[Section titled “Check it works”](#check-it-works)

* The MelonLoader console shows `Snitch v... - profiler.` at startup.
* `snitch status` prints a one-line summary.
* With Hotline installed, **F6** opens the overlay.

## Settings

[Section titled “Settings”](#settings)

Settings are in `UserData/MelonPreferences.cfg` under `Snitch_01_Main`, or in the in-game Mod Manager UI.

They cover the master switch, multiplayer behavior, auto-start, HUD, provider poll rate and the local data server. The server port is `6140` and listens on loopback only.

## Next

[Section titled “Next”](#next)

* [Console commands](/mods/snitch/guides/console-commands/)
* [Open the web dashboard](/mods/snitch/guides/web-dashboard/)
* [Troubleshooting](/mods/snitch/guides/troubleshooting/)

# Profile your mod

> Show your mod's timings, counters and controls in the Snitch overlay and web dashboard.

Add a Snitch panel to your mod. It shows your counters, state bars, buttons, toggles, sliders and log in the overlay and the web dashboard.

Snitch times `OnUpdate`, `OnFixedUpdate`, `OnLateUpdate` and `OnGUI` of every loaded mod without any code. Your mod already appears as `<YourMod>.OnUpdate`. Follow the steps only if you want more.

**You need:** Snitch in your test game and a MelonLoader mod project. Players do not need Snitch: every call is a no-op without it.

## Steps

[Section titled “Steps”](#steps)

1. Copy `Snitch.cs` from [ScheduleOne-SnitchExample](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-SnitchExample) into your project. It compiles into your DLL. You can reference `Snitch.Api.dll` instead.

2. Add a static class named `SnitchProbe` with a static `Register()` method. Snitch finds and calls it. You do not call it yourself.

3. Register a panel in `Register()` and add controls.

   ```csharp
   using Snitch.Api;   // Profiler, Panel, StateSnapshot


   internal static class SnitchProbe
   {
       public static void Register()
       {
           Panel p = Profiler.RegisterPanel("MyMod", "My Mod");
           p.Counter("QueueLength", () => MyMod.Queue.Count, "items");
           p.State("Jobs", () => new StateSnapshot { Title = "Jobs" }
               .Add("running", MyMod.Running).Add("queued", MyMod.Queued));
           p.Text(() => $"mode: {MyMod.Mode}");
           p.Action("Flush queue", () => MyMod.Flush());
           p.Toggle("Verbose", () => MyMod.Verbose, v => MyMod.Verbose = v);
           p.Slider("batch size", 1, 64, () => MyMod.Batch, v => MyMod.Batch = (int)v, 1);
           p.Log();
       }
   }
   ```

4. Time a hot section by hand. The call allocates nothing and does nothing when Snitch is not sampling.

   ```csharp
   using (Profiler.Sample("MyMod.Pathfinding")) { /* expensive work */ }


   // Skip even the call on a hot loop:
   if (Profiler.Enabled) using (Profiler.Sample("MyMod.Tick")) { /* ... */ }
   ```

5. Optional: register an ablation lever. `snitch ablate mymod.fx` then measures what your subsystem costs per frame.

   ```csharp
   Profiler.RegisterAblationLever("mymod.fx", apply: () => DisableFx(), restore: () => EnableFx());
   ```

6. Optional: mark a one-off spike with `Profiler.Mark("MyMod.LevelLoaded")`.

## Check it works

[Section titled “Check it works”](#check-it-works)

1. Start the game and run `snitch start` in the console.
2. Run `snitch panels`. Your panel and its control counts appear.
3. Open the panel from the `windows` list of the Overview window, or in the [web dashboard](/mods/snitch/guides/web-dashboard/).

![The My Mod card under Mod panels in the web dashboard, with the mode text, the queue counter, the Jobs state, the batch size slider, the Verbose toggle and the Flush queue button](/img/guides/snitch/mod-panels.webp)

## Rules

[Section titled “Rules”](#rules)

* Call the API from the Unity main thread. Snitch also runs your counter, state, action, toggle and slider delegates on the main thread, so they may use game objects.
* Prefix labels with `MyMod.` so they group per mod.
* Write log lines with `p.Write("...")` or `Profiler.Log("MyMod", "...")`. They appear in your panel and in the combined timeline.
* Registrations made before Snitch loads are queued. Load order does not matter.
* Lower-level calls exist: `Profiler.RegisterCounter`, `RegisterStateProvider`, `RegisterAction`, `RegisterToggle`, `RegisterSlider`, `RegisterText`, `Log`.

## Next

[Section titled “Next”](#next)

* [Add a slider](/mods/snitch/guides/sliders/)
* [Console commands](/mods/snitch/guides/console-commands/)
* [API reference](/mods/snitch/api/)

# Add a slider

> Tune a value by dragging it in your Snitch panel, in the overlay, the dashboard or the console.

Add a slider to your Snitch panel. You drag it in the overlay or the [web dashboard](/mods/snitch/guides/web-dashboard/), or write it with `snitch slider`.

This page uses the **Snitch** API (`Snitch.Api`). For the Hotline API, see the [Hotline slider guide](/mods/hotline/guides/sliders/).

**You need:** a Snitch panel. See [Profile your mod](/mods/snitch/guides/modder-api/).

## Steps

[Section titled “Steps”](#steps)

1. Call `Slider` on your panel, inside `SnitchProbe.Register()`.

   ```csharp
   using Snitch.Api;


   Panel p = Profiler.RegisterPanel("Yoink", "Yoink (Winch)");
   p.Slider("size", 0.2, 2.0, () => WinchItem.HeldScale, v => WinchItem.HeldScale = (float)v, 0.05, "x");
   p.Slider("pull force", 0, 60000, () => Preferences.PullNewtons, v => Preferences.PullNewtons = (float)v, 500, "N");
   ```

2. Pick a range wider than the values you expect. The ends are hard limits.

3. Give every slider in the panel a label that differs in its words. See “Label collisions” below.

The signature:

```csharp
Panel Slider(string label, double min, double max, Func<double> get, Action<double> set,
             double step = 0d, string unit = null)
```

| Parameter     | Meaning                                                               |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`       | Text next to the value. It also makes the slider id.                  |
| `min` / `max` | Ends of the track. `max` must be greater than `min`.                  |
| `get`         | Reads the current value on the main thread.                           |
| `set`         | Applies a new value on the main thread.                               |
| `step`        | Snap increment. `0` means continuous.                                 |
| `unit`        | Short suffix after the number, for example `m`, `N`, `deg`. Optional. |

The static form is `Profiler.RegisterSlider(panelId, label, min, max, get, set, step, unit)`.

Snitch clamps the value to `[min, max]` and snaps it to `step` before it calls `set`. Your setter needs no range check.

## Check it works

[Section titled “Check it works”](#check-it-works)

1. Run `snitch panels`. The panel lists one more slider.
2. Run `snitch slider Yoink:size`. It prints the value, range and step.
3. Run `snitch slider Yoink:size 0.85`. The game applies the clamped, snapped value.
4. Drag the slider in the overlay or the dashboard. Both use the same path.

![The Yoink (Winch) card in the web dashboard with the size slider at 1.00 x and the pull force slider at 20000.00 N](/img/guides/snitch/yoink-sliders.webp)

## Label collisions

[Section titled “Label collisions”](#label-collisions)

A slider id is `<panelId>:<slug of the label>`. The slug keeps letters and digits, lowercases them and turns every other run of characters into one hyphen.

| Label                         | Id in panel `Yoink`    |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| `size`                        | `Yoink:size`           |
| `pull force`                  | `Yoink:pull-force`     |
| `size -0.05` and `size +0.05` | both `Yoink:size-0-05` |

Two labels with the same id replace each other. No warning or log line appears, and the first control disappears. Use `size down` and `size up`, not `size -0.05` and `size +0.05`.

## Rules

[Section titled “Rules”](#rules)

* Register from the Unity main thread.
* A call is dropped silently if `max` is not greater than `min`, or if `get` or `set` is null.
* Registering the same id again replaces the slider. Running your probe twice is safe.
* Overlay, dashboard, phone remote and console all reach the same `set`. Write it so any of them can call it at any time.
* On a Snitch without sliders, the call is a no-op.

## Next

[Section titled “Next”](#next)

* [Console commands](/mods/snitch/guides/console-commands/)
* [Web dashboard](/mods/snitch/guides/web-dashboard/)
* [API reference](/mods/snitch/api/)

# Troubleshoot Snitch

> Find the Snitch symptom you see and apply its fix.

Find your symptom below. Check `MelonLoader/Latest.log` first.

## The dashboard says “Searching…” and never connects

[Section titled “The dashboard says “Searching…” and never connects”](#the-dashboard-says-searching-and-never-connects)

* Check that the game runs with Snitch installed and a save is loaded. The log shows `Snitch v...` when the mod loads.
* The hosted page connects to `ws://127.0.0.1:6140`. If the browser asks to “allow access to your local network”, allow it.
* For a custom dashboard origin, add it to the `AllowedOrigins` preference. Localhost and the official hosted domain are allowed already.
* Another tool may use the port. Change the `ServerPort` preference (default `6140`) and reconnect.

## The dashboard connects but shows “idle”

[Section titled “The dashboard connects but shows “idle””](#the-dashboard-connects-but-shows-idle)

Sampling is off. Press **Start** on the page, or run `snitch start`.

## `snitch dashboard` opens nothing

[Section titled “snitch dashboard opens nothing”](#snitch-dashboard-opens-nothing)

The local data server is off. Set `ServerEnabled` in MelonPreferences and restart the game.

## fps looks the same with `snitch vanilla on`

[Section titled “fps looks the same with snitch vanilla on”](#fps-looks-the-same-with-snitch-vanilla-on)

Vanilla section costs cover only the methods Snitch wraps. The main cost of a system can be native code. Run `snitch ablate <lever>` for the real total.

## An ablation result looks wrong or negative

[Section titled “An ablation result looks wrong or negative”](#an-ablation-result-looks-wrong-or-negative)

Ablation measures a settled frame-time change. Run it in a calm scene, not right after a load. Disable other mods that act on the same subsystem, for example an NPC-LOD mod when you ablate `npc`.

## A control is missing from my mod panel

[Section titled “A control is missing from my mod panel”](#a-control-is-missing-from-my-mod-panel)

Two slider labels may give the same id. See [Add a slider](/mods/snitch/guides/sliders/). Run `snitch panels` to compare control counts.

## Ablation does nothing on a client

[Section titled “Ablation does nothing on a client”](#ablation-does-nothing-on-a-client)

Ablation levers run on the host only. Measurement itself runs on every peer.

## I need to ask for help

[Section titled “I need to ask for help”](#i-need-to-ask-for-help)

Run `snitch report all`. Attach the files from `Mods/Snitch/runs/` and `MelonLoader/Latest.log`.

# Open the web dashboard

> Watch live Snitch data in a browser, or read it from your own tool over JSON.

Open the Snitch dashboard in your browser. It shows a live frame chart, section costs, state bars, counters and your mod panels.

Snitch runs a loopback server at `127.0.0.1:6140` and streams data over WebSocket. The data never leaves your machine. The hosted site serves only the static app.

## Steps

[Section titled “Steps”](#steps)

1. Start the game and load a save.

2. Open the dashboard in one of three ways:

   * Press **Open dashboard** in the Snitch panel, or run `snitch dashboard`. Snitch picks the bundled copy (`Mods/Snitch/wwwroot`) if present, and the hosted site otherwise.
   * Open [snitch.doodesch.de](https://snitch.doodesch.de). It finds your game on its own.
   * Open `http://localhost:6140/`. This copy works offline.

3. If Chrome asks to “allow access to your local network”, allow it. The hosted page needs it.

4. Press **Start**, or run `snitch start`. The dashboard stays idle until sampling is armed.

If the local data server is off, `snitch dashboard` opens nothing. Set `ServerEnabled` in MelonPreferences and restart.

## Check it works

[Section titled “Check it works”](#check-it-works)

The page shows a moving frame-time chart. If it says “Searching…”, see [Troubleshooting](/mods/snitch/guides/troubleshooting/).

![The Snitch web dashboard, connected on port 6140, with 94 fps and the frame-time chart](/img/guides/snitch/dashboard.webp)

## What the page shows

[Section titled “What the page shows”](#what-the-page-shows)

* **Frame chart:** mean frame time in ms, newest sample on the right. Lower is better. Hover a point for its value.
* **Sections:** ms/frame per section, grouped by mod. Click a group header to collapse it. Hover a row for worst-frame ms and calls/frame.
* **State distributions:** hover a bar for its count and share.
* **Controls:** Start, Stop, Reset and report export.
* **Mod panels:** one card per mod with text, buttons, toggles and [sliders](/mods/snitch/guides/sliders/). The host clamps and snaps slider values.

## Read the data in your own tool

[Section titled “Read the data in your own tool”](#read-the-data-in-your-own-tool)

The data is JSON.

| Endpoint                     | Use                     |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| `GET /snapshot`              | Full state.             |
| `ws://127.0.0.1:6140/stream` | Live push of the state. |
| `GET /health`, `GET /caps`   | Describe the instance.  |
| `POST /control`              | Write a command.        |

The wire format is in [`Server/WireProtocol.cs`](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Snitch/blob/main/Server/WireProtocol.cs). The dashboard source is [ScheduleOne-SnitchWeb](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-SnitchWeb).

Each entry of `panels[]` has `actions`, `toggles` and `sliders`:

```json
{
  "id": "Yoink",
  "title": "Yoink (Winch)",
  "actions": [ { "id": "Yoink:give-winch", "label": "give winch" } ],
  "toggles": [ { "id": "Yoink:arms-visible", "label": "arms visible", "value": true } ],
  "sliders": [
    { "id": "Yoink:pull-force", "label": "pull force", "unit": "N",
      "min": 0, "max": 60000, "step": 500, "value": 12000 }
  ]
}
```

`step` `0` means continuous. Read the array as `panel.sliders ?? []`: an older Snitch omits it.

Write a slider through `/control`:

```plaintext
POST /control?cmd=slider&id=Yoink:pull-force&value=12500
```

* `cmd`, `id` and `value` may also be JSON fields in the body.
* Send any number. The game clamps it and snaps it to the step.
* A good write returns `{"ok":true,"cmd":"slider"}`. A missing `id` or a bad `value` returns `{"ok":false,"error":"..."}`.
* The game applies the write on its next frame. Read the result from the next snapshot.

## Next

[Section titled “Next”](#next)

* [Console commands](/mods/snitch/guides/console-commands/)
* [Troubleshooting](/mods/snitch/guides/troubleshooting/)

# SnitchExample

> Example + modder API (Snitch.cs shim) for the Snitch Schedule I performance profiler.

|          |                                                                                                 |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Version  | No release yet, documented from `main`                                                          |
| Download | [GitHub](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-SnitchExample)                            |
| Help     | [Discord](https://mods.doodesch.de) · [Report a bug](https://support.doodesch.de/snitchexample) |

A minimal example of integrating with the [**Snitch**](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Snitch) performance profiler for Schedule I. Snitch lets your mod report its own performance - timed sections, numeric counters, entity-state distributions, and ablation levers - and it is a **zero-overhead no-op when Snitch is not installed**, so you can ship the integration with no hard dependency.

## The basics are free

[Section titled “The basics are free”](#the-basics-are-free)

When Snitch is installed and sampling, it **auto-times every loaded mod’s per-frame methods** (`OnUpdate`, `OnFixedUpdate`, `OnLateUpdate`, `OnGUI`) and shows them as `<YourMod>.OnUpdate` - with **no code on your side**. Your mod already appears in the frame budget. Add the API below only to go further.

## Two ways to add the API

[Section titled “Two ways to add the API”](#two-ways-to-add-the-api)

* **Copy-in source (recommended):** drop [`Snitch.Api/Snitch.cs`](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-SnitchExample/blob/main/Snitch.Api/Snitch.cs) into your mod project. It compiles into your DLL - nothing extra to ship.
* **Reference the DLL:** build `Snitch.Api/Snitch.Api.csproj` and reference `Snitch.Api.dll`.

Both bind to the running Snitch host purely by reflection, so they share no type with it and work regardless of load order.

## Give your mod a panel with zero wiring

[Section titled “Give your mod a panel with zero wiring”](#give-your-mod-a-panel-with-zero-wiring)

Name a class `SnitchProbe` with a static `Register()` - Snitch **discovers and calls it automatically**, so nothing goes into your `OnInitializeMelon`. There, declare a **panel**: your mod’s own toggleable, movable, resizable area in the Snitch overlay and web dashboard, holding your counters, state, free text, action buttons, toggles and a log channel. See [`SnitchExample/Core.cs`](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-SnitchExample/blob/main/SnitchExample/Core.cs):

```csharp
using Snitch.Api;   // Profiler, Panel, StateSnapshot


internal static class SnitchProbe
{
    public static void Register()
    {
        Panel p = Profiler.RegisterPanel("MyMod", "My Mod");        // counters/state added here become "MyMod.*"
        p.Counter("QueueLength", () => MyMod.Queue.Count, "items"); // numeric gauge
        p.State("Jobs", () => new StateSnapshot { Title = "Jobs" }  // name -> count distribution (bars)
            .Add("running", MyMod.Running).Add("queued", MyMod.Queued));
        p.Text(() => $"mode: {MyMod.Mode}");                        // free multi-line readout
        p.Action("Flush queue", () => MyMod.Flush());              // a button (replaces a debug hotkey)
        p.Toggle("Verbose", () => MyMod.Verbose, v => MyMod.Verbose = v); // an on/off control
        p.Log();                                                    // show this panel's log channel
    }
}
```

Then `p.Write("...")` (or `Profiler.Log("MyMod", "...")`) from anywhere sends a line to your panel’s log and the combined timeline. Actions and toggles run on the Unity main thread, so they may touch game objects.

## The full API

[Section titled “The full API”](#the-full-api)

```csharp
using Snitch.Api;   // Profiler, Panel, StateSnapshot, Scope


// 0) Your panel (toggleable/movable/resizable in the overlay + dashboard). Fluent builder:
Panel p = Profiler.RegisterPanel("MyMod", "My Mod");
p.Counter("QueueLength", () => _queue.Count, "items"); // -> MyMod.QueueLength
p.State("Jobs", () => new StateSnapshot { Title = "Jobs" }.Add("running", _running));
p.Text(() => $"mode: {_mode}");                        // free multi-line readout
p.Action("Flush", () => Flush());                      // button (replaces a debug hotkey)
p.Toggle("Verbose", () => _verbose, v => _verbose = v);// on/off control
p.Log();                                               // show this panel's log channel
p.Write("something happened");                         // -> panel log + combined timeline


// 1) Hand-time a sub-section (finer than the automatic per-mod timing). No heap alloc; no-op when not sampling.
using (Profiler.Sample("MyMod.Pathfinding")) { ...expensive work... }


// gate hot loops for the absolutely-free path:
if (Profiler.Enabled) using (Profiler.Sample("MyMod.Tick")) { ... }


// 2) A numeric gauge (polled a few Hz by the host)
Profiler.RegisterCounter("MyMod.QueueLength", () => _queue.Count, "items");


// 3) An entity/state distribution (shown as a bar panel in the HUD + web dashboard)
Profiler.RegisterStateProvider("MyMod.Jobs", () =>
    new StateSnapshot { Title = "Jobs" }.Add("running", _running).Add("queued", _queued));


// 4) An ablation lever so 'snitch ablate mymod' measures your subsystem's causal frame cost
Profiler.RegisterAblationLever("mymod.particles", apply: () => DisableParticles(), restore: () => EnableParticles());


// 5) Mark a one-off spike
Profiler.Mark("MyMod.LevelLoaded");
```

**Rules:** call from the Unity main thread. Prefix your labels with `MyMod.` so they roll up per mod in the UI. Counter/state delegates are invoked by the host on the main thread, so they may touch game objects.

## See your data

[Section titled “See your data”](#see-your-data)

In game: `snitch hud on` (F6) for the overlay, then open your panel from the Overview window’s `windows` list (or `snitch panel MyMod on`); `snitch panels` lists them. `snitch start` arms sampling (or the Start button in the Overview). In the browser: open the Snitch web dashboard - it auto-connects and shows your panel (counters, state, actions, toggles) and the log timeline live alongside the vanilla NPC/trash/quest data.

## Building this example

[Section titled “Building this example”](#building-this-example)

The `.csproj` files reference MelonLoader from a local `Workspace/lib` (the author’s build layout) and copy to the game’s `Mods/` folder on build - adjust those paths to your own setup. You only really need `Snitch.Api/Snitch.cs` and `SnitchExample/Core.cs` to learn the API.

# Stash

> Public shared source for DooDesch's Schedule I mods (starts with the FullHouse lobby-cap engine).

|          |                                                                                         |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Version  | No release yet, documented from `main`                                                  |
| Download | [GitHub](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Stash)                            |
| Help     | [Discord](https://mods.doodesch.de) · [Report a bug](https://support.doodesch.de/stash) |

The **Stash** is the public, MIT-licensed source that several DooDesch Schedule I mods share. It exists so the actual mod logic lives in the open - some mods (like [FullHouse](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-FullHouse)) are basically just this shared engine plus packaging, so without the Stash their repo would look empty.

The private build workspace (the decompiled game, the game’s managed DLLs, internal design docs) stays private - none of that is needed to read or edit the source here.

## What’s inside

[Section titled “What’s inside”](#whats-inside)

| Path                       | What                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `fullhouse/FullHouse.cs`   | The FullHouse engine - raises the co-op lobby cap (Steam lobby member limit + the game’s `Lobby`/`LobbyInterface`). Shared by the standalone FullHouse mod and embedded into Side Hustle. |
| `build/FullHouse.props`    | One-line linked-source import so a host mod compiles the engine in.                                                                                                                       |
| `nudge/Nudge.cs`           | Update check - tells the player in the console which of their mods have a newer GitHub release.                                                                                           |
| `build/Nudge.props`        | One-line linked-source import for Nudge (also switches the check off for Thunderstore builds).                                                                                            |
| `tools/copy-game-libs.ps1` | Helper to copy the game/MelonLoader DLLs you need to build, out of your own Schedule I install.                                                                                           |

More shared source will move here over time.

## Using it in a mod

[Section titled “Using it in a mod”](#using-it-in-a-mod)

A host mod adds one line to its `.csproj` (after its `<Compile Remove>` guards) and calls the engine once:

```xml
<Import Project="$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)../Stash/build/FullHouse.props"
        Condition="Exists('$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)../Stash/build/FullHouse.props')" />
```

```csharp
DooDesch.FullHouse.Lobbies.Install();   // early, e.g. OnInitializeMelon
```

The engine is `internal`, so several mods can each compile it in without a CS0436 clash, and a runtime single-flight guard makes sure only one loaded copy patches.

## Nudge - “your mods are out of date”

[Section titled “Nudge - “your mods are out of date””](#nudge---your-mods-are-out-of-date)

Same two steps:

```xml
<Import Project="$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)../Stash/build/Nudge.props"
        Condition="Exists('$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)../Stash/build/Nudge.props')" />
```

```csharp
DooDesch.Nudge.Nudge.Watch();   // once, in OnInitializeMelon
```

It checks **every loaded mod**, not just yours. MelonLoader already knows each mod’s version and download link, so any mod that names its repo in `MelonInfo` is covered whether or not it has heard of Nudge:

```csharp
[assembly: MelonInfo(typeof(Core), "MyMod", "1.0.0", "Me", "https://github.com/me/MyMod")]
```

The newest version is the repo’s latest GitHub release tag. Outdated mods get one yellow block in the console; when everything is current it says nothing at all.

```plaintext
[Nudge] 2 mods are out of date
[Nudge]   Snitch       1.6.0 -> 1.7.0   https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Snitch/releases
[Nudge]   Side Hustle  2.2.3 -> 2.3.0   https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-SideHustle/releases
```

One consumer covers a whole install - further copies detect each other and stand down. Answers are cached in `UserData/DooDesch/Nudge.txt` for six hours, so a big mod list stays inside GitHub’s anonymous rate limit. Players switch it off with `UpdateCheck = false` under `[DooDesch]` in `MelonPreferences.cfg`.

Nudge never downloads or installs anything - it only tells you. Building with `-p:StoreBuild=thunderstore` compiles the endpoint, the HTTP client and the parser out of the DLL entirely and leaves `Watch()` a no-op.

## Building / contributing

[Section titled “Building / contributing”](#building--contributing)

You need two things to build a mod that uses the Stash:

1. **This repo + the mod’s repo**, checked out as siblings (`Stash/` next to e.g. `FullHouse/`).

2. **The game’s managed DLLs** (Assembly-CSharp, the Il2Cpp interop assemblies, MelonLoader, Steamworks, TextMeshPro). These are game binaries and are NOT redistributed here - grab them from your own Schedule I + MelonLoader install:

   ```powershell
   # from the Stash folder, point at your Schedule I install:
   ./tools/copy-game-libs.ps1 -GameRoot "D:\...\steamapps\common\Schedule I"
   # -> fills Stash/lib/il2cpp/{game,melonloader}
   ```

Then build the mod pointing at those libs, e.g.:

```plaintext
dotnet build ../FullHouse/FullHouse.csproj -c Release -p:WorkspaceLibPath="<abs path>/Stash/lib"
```

(The mod csprojs default `WorkspaceLibPath` to the maintainer’s private lib folder and fall back to `../Stash/lib`, so once you have run the helper the default just works.)

# TightBeam

> A believable, limited-range handheld flashlight for Schedule I with a cross-mod control API.

|                |                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Latest release | `2.1.1`                                                                                                                                       |
| Download       | [GitHub](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-TightBeam) · [Thunderstore](https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/p/DooDesch/TightBeam/) |
| Requires       | MelonLoader 0.7.3                                                                                                                             |
| Start here     | [Control the flashlight](/mods/tightbeam/guides/modder-api/)                                                                                  |
| API            | [Reference](/mods/tightbeam/api/)                                                                                                             |
| Help           | [Discord](https://mods.doodesch.de) · [Report a bug](https://support.doodesch.de/tightbeam)                                                   |

> A proper handheld flashlight for Schedule I. It upgrades the game’s own flashlight - toggle it with your flashlight key, then hold **ALT + mouse wheel** to dial the beam from a wide near-flood to a tight, far-reaching throw. No map-wide floodlight, no blinding glare - just a light that feels like a flashlight.

## Features

[Section titled “Features”](#features)

* **A beam you can aim and shape.** Hold **ALT + mouse wheel** to slide a single Focus axis: the wide end is a short, broad flood right in front of you; the narrow end is a tight cone that throws far. Range and cone angle both follow the focus, so you get real control without ever washing out the map.
* **Velocity-sensitive focus.** Scroll slowly for fine steps; flick fast and the beam races to the nearest extreme. The displayed beam eases in smoothly instead of popping.
* **Fixed, sane brightness.** The beam holds a sensible brightness within a hard floor and ceiling - no accidental whiteout. Brightness is not a player control; mods can drive it through the API (e.g. dim it in a dark room).
* **Shadows and a cool-white tint by default**, so the beam is blocked by walls and reads against the game’s warm lighting. Both are configurable (turn shadows off on low-end machines).
* **In perfect sync with the game.** TightBeam drives off the game’s own flashlight state, so its on/off never falls out of step - your flashlight key toggles it, and it swaps the vanilla point light for its own clean cone.
* **Works in co-op.** Everyone else’s flashlight becomes a TightBeam cone too, pointed where they are looking rather than sitting on their chest, with their own focus, brightness and colour. Players who join late see the lights that are already on - the base game never tells them about those. Capped, distance-culled and shadow-free by default so a full lobby stays smooth, and anyone without the mod still gets a cone instead of the vanilla dot.
* **Light-touch and update-resilient.** A spotlight that follows your camera - no gameplay rewired, and nothing written to the game’s own state. In co-op your beam’s shape goes on a noticeboard in the Steam lobby that the game itself never reads, so players without the mod are not touched by it at all. A tiny guard keeps ALT+scroll from cycling your hotbar.
* **Cross-mod API.** Other mods can drive the beam - dim it in a dark room, flicker it near power, blink it as an alert - through a drop-in `Beam` shim. See [For modders](#for-modders).

## Controls

[Section titled “Controls”](#controls)

| Input                           | Action                                    |
| ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| Flashlight key (your game bind) | Toggle the flashlight on/off              |
| `ALT` + mouse wheel             | Focus: wide near-flood to tight far-throw |

On/off uses your game’s own flashlight key; the focus modifier is rebindable in TightBeam’s config.

Requirements

| Component   | Version / Source                    |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------- |
| Schedule I  | IL2CPP (current Steam public build) |
| MelonLoader | `0.7.3+`                            |

No other dependencies - just MelonLoader. TightBeam reads the game’s own flashlight state and renders its own light; no S1API. Co-op works with only some players having the mod, though everyone gets the best result if you all do.

Installation

### Recommended: a Thunderstore mod manager

[Section titled “Recommended: a Thunderstore mod manager”](#recommended-a-thunderstore-mod-manager)

Install with r2modman / Gale from the Schedule I community; MelonLoader is pulled in automatically.

### Manual

[Section titled “Manual”](#manual)

1. Install **MelonLoader 0.7.3** for Schedule I.
2. Drop **`TightBeam.dll`** into your Schedule I `Mods/` folder.

## Configuration

[Section titled “Configuration”](#configuration)

Settings live in `UserData/MelonPreferences.cfg` under `[TightBeam]`. Highlights:

| Setting                         | Default     | What it does                                         |
| ------------------------------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `Enabled`                       | `true`      | Master on/off for the whole mod.                     |
| `FocusModifierKey`              | `LeftAlt`   | Hold this and scroll to change focus.                |
| `DefaultFocus`                  | `0.5`       | Starting focus. `1` = wide flood, `0` = tight throw. |
| `DefaultIntensity`              | `7`         | Base brightness (clamped to Min/Max).                |
| `MinIntensity` / `MaxIntensity` | `1` / `20`  | Hard floor / ceiling for brightness.                 |
| `RangeWide` / `RangeNarrow`     | `8` / `34`  | Beam range (m) at each focus extreme.                |
| `AngleWide` / `AngleNarrow`     | `66` / `16` | Cone angle (deg) at each focus extreme.              |
| `ColorHex`                      | `#E6F2FF`   | Beam colour (cool white).                            |
| `CastShadows`                   | `true`      | Soft shadows (turn off on low-end machines).         |

There are more fine-tuning knobs for the focus feel (sensitivity, easing, flick threshold) in the same section if you want to dial it in. Editing the file takes effect on the next launch.

## For modders

[Section titled “For modders”](#for-modders)

TightBeam exposes a small cross-mod control API so your mod can drive the player’s flashlight - on/off, brightness, range, colour, plus Blink/Flicker/Pulse and scoped per-field overrides. Every call is a safe no-op when TightBeam is not installed, so you can ship it with no hard dependency.

**Full reference: the [TightBeam Wiki](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-TightBeam/wiki)** - see the [Modder API](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-TightBeam/wiki/Modder-API) page.

Copy the [Beam shim](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-TightBeam/wiki/The-Beam-Shim) (`TightBeam.cs`) into your project (or reference `TightBeam.Api.dll`) and call it:

```csharp
using TightBeam.Api;


Beam.Blink(3);                                 // blink as an alert
using (var ov = Beam.BeginOverride("MyMod"))   // scoped, per-field override
{
    ov.SetIntensity(1f).SetSpotAngle(28f);     // dim + narrow while in a zone
}                                              // released -> back to the player's own settings
```

Credits

* **DooDesch** - mod author.

# TightBeam API

> Look up every public type and member of TightBeam 2.1.1.

## Use this API

[Section titled “Use this API”](#use-this-api)

Copy [`TightBeam.cs`](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-TightBeam/blob/v2.1.1/TightBeam.Api/TightBeam.cs) into your project. That one file is the whole API.

```xml
<Compile Include="path\to\TightBeam.cs" />
```

Mark it optional, so your mod still loads without it:

```csharp
[assembly: MelonOptionalDependencies("TightBeam")]
```

Without TightBeam every call does nothing and returns a default. Calls made before TightBeam loads run once it does.

First steps: [Control the flashlight](/mods/tightbeam/guides/modder-api/).

Source: [`TightBeam.Api/TightBeam.cs`](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-TightBeam/blob/v2.1.1/TightBeam.Api/TightBeam.cs) at `v2.1.1`.

# Beam

> TightBeam's cross-mod control API for the player's flashlight.

```csharp
public static class Beam
```

Namespace `TightBeam.Api`

TightBeam’s cross-mod control API for the player’s flashlight. Reference TightBeam.Api.dll OR drop this single file into your mod. Drive the beam from any mod: on/off, brightness, range, colour, plus Blink/Flicker/Pulse and scoped per-field overrides (e.g. dim it in a dark room, flicker it near power).

Every call is a zero-overhead no-op when TightBeam is not installed and lights up automatically when it is, so you can ship this unconditionally with no hard dependency. All calls MUST be on the Unity main thread.

```csharp
using TightBeam.Api;
Beam.Blink(3);                                   // event blink
var ov = Beam.BeginOverride("MyMod");            // scoped, per-field override
ov.SetIntensity(1f).SetSpotAngle(28f);           //   dim + narrow while in a zone
ov.Dispose();                                    // release -> beam returns to the player's own settings
```

# OverrideHandle

> A scoped, per-field override on the flashlight for one owner.

```csharp
public struct OverrideHandle : IDisposable
```

Namespace `TightBeam.Api`

A scoped, per-field override on the flashlight for one owner. Set fields to drive the beam; Clear or Dispose to release them and let the player’s own settings show through. Safe no-op if TightBeam is absent.
